title.title: Network issues 💔🙁😕
title.body:
by Khing Addy on Adrians Lifestyle 
View my bio on Blurt.media: https://blurt.media/c/adrianslifestyle [![Network issues 💔🙁😕](https://blurt.media/lazy-static/previews/97b08556-8295-43dc-b782-820588c27ad4.jpg)](https://blurt.media/w/sJhhLU87u2ooPspNAxGTGm) 
 
 The plan for today was to play eFootball PVP in Division mode, but the network in the room would not cooperate at all. It kept lagging and dropping, so playing online properly was not possible. Since content was needed for the gaming posts, something had to be done. The posts usually cover Steemit Gaming, Cur8, and eFootball, and there was even a thought to try Call of Duty for the day. But the network dissolved too much, so that option was out. In the end, the choice was to just play an exhibition match offline and make something out of it.

Even with the bad network, the match started and a goal came in just a few minutes. That early goal gave some confidence, so the game was played more carefully. Because the connection was unstable and the player was only partially focused, a lower-tier team was picked instead of a strong one. Manchester B, which is Manchester City’s B team, was chosen to play against a tougher opponent. It felt risky using a weaker side, but it also made the match more interesting. Playing with less strength forced better control and smarter moves.

The result was surprising. The match ended 4-0, and it was a clean win. That kind of score had not been recorded before, so it felt like a first. The network problems made everything harder, but the win still came through. It was a rough game because of the lag and the choice of a lower team, but it turned out to be good content in the end. Now there is something solid to post about, and hopefully the network behaves better next time so PVP Division can be played properly.
Thanks for visiting  
 ***
[**Check out today's video..!**](https://blurt.media/w/sJhhLU87u2ooPspNAxGTGm)

title.title: LBI Weekly Update post - Year 2 Week 45 - W/E 31 May 2026
title.body:
LBI is a pooled investment token on Hive Engine, with a diverse range of holdings across HIVE.  From HP and HBD, to positions in liquidity pools and various Hive Engine projects, think of LBI as a diverse basket of Hive assets.  We have invested for asset growth, and share a portion of our weekly income as a SWAP.HBD dividend.  Another portion of our income provides liquidity incentives for token holders to add LBI into various pool.  

Each week we publish this detailed update, showing where all our assets are invested, how our income has tracked, and any other relevant information for token holders and potential holders.  Our token is fully distributed, and we have a slightly deflationary token supply thanks to a weekly buy back and burn program.


![New LBI gif.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lbi-token/23tbR7Tgh7kNgdCeUHU1ozAjC5vpV4oKLDy6xDRY3WCexc5oAQg7Zzcsac37rSWqxeHXr.gif)

Here are the token prices used in this weeks update:

![prices 31may26.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lbi-token/EprYuGHtyhw8pkEtkg6ExXkxLWLGEiZZXJYoFPQKy85CY9WhoerRM21xxafoVK7pvJW.png)

And [here is the link to the last report for comparisons](https://peakd.com/lbi/@lbi-token/lbi-weekly-update-post-year-2-week-44-we-24-may-2026)

_________

# Assets

### @lbi-token


![token 31may26.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lbi-token/23ynmS6RShTXX5y7yY7XPoEVPXW7aheKiEDAzF1L43zmrZmUAcjduZR7sXvQsWNFPg2ro.png)

I have not done a lot with this wallet this week.  We gained 40 HP, and 1.2 HBD across the week.  I've moved another 1000 HSBIDAO over to the Three wallet.  Value is down a bit, with HIVE slightly lower, and LEO (which is now held in this wallet) down also.

### @lbi-eds


![eds 31may26.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lbi-token/242DdiSZSGvpzk4nAz29Mj7L3VZ5q84GSsCG5oeUQqabKiB5KnEoCsSP1r9Xkxk978DJa.png)

We added 56.68 EDSI across the week, with our EDSI growing faster these days.  Our increased HP delegation adds more EDSI than we used to get, and the EDSD contributes well while HIVE price is so low.  Added a bit more HP over the week from the Leo wallet power-down.

### @lbi-dab 


![dab 31may26.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lbi-token/243WkicUodvw9NU4asNBcWdRborHSLdDtk1gYpvJzaEqpMCcDn3tttbDrmfbyPgxF1BEA.png)

We gained 53 DAB for the week, and 20 DBOND from our RUG rewards.  We shifted to all liquid DAB to boost income across the week.  No changes this week overall.

### @lbi-cent 


![cent 31may26.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lbi-token/23ydQzYFDAPBkgf2jisz2xkmjhAueurs1F7kvTgmysDkTC6TWgKQ4Wz99UbMB7W8AWeQN.png)

In amongst all that detail for the CENT wallet is CENT stake.  We bought a bunch of CENT this week, and now hold 2.5 Million staked.  These are then delegated to @centtoken, who reward us with weekly SWAP.HBD.  This has given a boost to the yield of this wallet.  I used some remaining LEO sitting in the LEO wallet to make those purchases.  LEO keeps going down, and CENT has held or is up a little, and I think will perform better in the short to medium term tbh.  

### @lbi-three 


![three 31may26.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lbi-token/23zGyVoiMFgG2iqnAYhq5JoUW3rtr1DGvjedp2DDBb38xwkxefG2GV9AUtyi1rSbFFMeb.png)

Shifted some of the HSBIDAO over from the main wallet to add to these pool positions.  Will continue to do that gradually over the coming weeks and eventually all our HSBIDAO will be in this wallet. Slow and steady in the game itself, waiting for new features and add-ons to role out.  

### @lbi-alive and @lbi-leo 


![leoalive 31may26.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lbi-token/EpR19Tp5nv3AXXG1QVFawytdTsHMZ9WJbusDoMTpcgAR9CNLd7qVNQtL4hJfwSQF2ZM.png)

We continue to wind down the LEO wallet, and slowly build the new \

wallet.  We have added to the LP position, to help ALIVE improve it's liquidity in advance of the launch of a new ALIVE:LBI pool.  Watch this space...

### @lbi-bbb 


![bbb 31may26.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lbi-token/23yJdXaFDqgKiiwPK1MW4t1aYQADkhhZWKriNHhbGWhRW31xb4ndiCnrfP9a4MkzqrVG8.png)

Another week without any token buys for LBI.  Each week that passes without a buy is a good week, as it means that LBI has not traded at or below it's asset backed value at all across the week.  That is a win in my books.



_____________

# Totals


![total 31may26.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lbi-token/EopyAi6KnaiiSc1WUTSaVApjHe5aY9Essz3JUPXgQo83SiH8jiQukbvjz3hJjR5zHbP.png)

We end the week with an asset backed valuation of $0.064, around $12,172 of assets in our wallets.  HIVE has been under $0.06, and LEO continues to drop, so in this light I am happy to hold above $12,000 for now.


![assets 31may26.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lbi-token/23tHXKoy6N7NzsJAayfPrkvEpcSJrraozU85WLdXjefRJJXkFYKZAiUSPRtZVpGmgLfSB.png)

LEO is down to 13% of our fund now, it's lowest point I think I can remember.  40% HIVE, 20% USD and the rest you can see above.



____________

# Income


![income 31may26.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lbi-token/23xLFuuVKLMfh4Q72w3tZ8ARv8VSFKaW18WAhcS5xA3dbfSrWueUu27oaxVoaE8p93VXC.png)

A good week for income, topping 14 SWAP.HBD for the first time since switching over from LEO as our base currency.  An increase in the price of HIVE would do wonders for this, but building the income base while HIVE is low is going to work well for us.  Next goal is to push over 15 for the week.


![dist 31may26.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lbi-token/23t86RmjdJuWcKNyiK1XivLVb1PNxz2kBLq9p2z9gC2TCoxWp6MX6sAeK88F4tM9dZ785.png)

Dividends have gone out for the week, at a yield above 2% for the first time since early March, back when Leostrategy yield was still (sometimes) getting paid out.  2% dividend, for a growth fund is decent.  Don't forget you can get extra yield from your LBI by adding to the Liquidity pools.  Take a look at [the weekly update on LBI liquidity](https://peakd.com/lbi/@lbi-token/lbi-weekly-liquidity-update-27-may-2026) to see the options and how they stack up.

____________

# Conclusion

We close the books on another week for LBI, with this week really being about consolidating our positions and improving our liquidity.  The pools have nudged above the 20,000 LBI liquidity in them for the first time in a long time.  Income is up a bit to it's highest amount in the time since we swapped over from LEO to HBD.  Despite HIVE's woes, we are doing ok, and positioned as well as we can be to survive more woes, or prosper on an improved performance for our home base.



Thanks for checking this weeks update, drop a comment below with any thoughts, questions or opinions on anything LBI.

Have a great week,

JK
@jk6276 for LBI

__________

title.title: Confeccionando florero con forma de piña, para decorar mi hogar.Reciclando.(Esp/Eng)
title.body:
# Español

# Saludos amigos amantes de las manualidades.💁☀️

¡Feliz día para todos!

Amigos, amo la práctica del papel maché, pues además de generarme paz emocional cuando la practico, me permite reciclar materiales en deshuso.Hoy, les quiero compartir a través de un tutorial, como confeccioné un florero con forma de piña para decorar mi hogar, reciclando cartones de huevos. Acompáñenme amigos, y ¡comencemos a crear!.
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260530_152301092.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/AJpn6jrpN7B6JenntS5ktTaaVLTjM53MzdUrKESYJLEAZY11ZW75UbRfWU5S1ug.jpg)
</center>
#
# ✨Florero frutal( forma de Piña)✨

# ✨Materiales
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260530_144722121.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23wCLbrpZ9TZfKPzUntxqMjZcea88CBw4jk6PJGjiDFJiKZsLUCayrcnC2bwsCLrjxYpQ.jpg)
</center>
#
.Papel maleable
.Tiras de papel blancas
.Cartón de soporte de huevos: 1
.Cartón
.Cartulina
.Tijera
.Pega elaborada de harina
.Temperas
.Pincel
.Lápiz

# ✨Modo de confección✨

Para confeccionar este florero, dividí el proceder en tres momentos, un primer momento, dónde cree su cuerpo con relieve, un segundo momento dónde creé su base y parte superior, y un tercero, dónde unifiqué todas las partes, y le di vida a la manualidad con toques pintorescos.

# ✨Pasos para crear el cuerpo(parte central)
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260530_145108285.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/AJmu2ZUHkoMrDVt1ndykkz3hxiimeYtnzLVvdEn5TDa7KxQyfEZnzXWBAWfpffj.jpg)
</center>
#
Inicié el proceder tomando el cartón de huevos, y cortándole con ayuda de una tijera las dos hileras superiores. Seguidamente, coloqué está hilera a continuación del cartón restante, para lograr el completo del cuerpo del florero. Luego, fuí realizándoles dobleces al cartón, para lograr una estructura circular cerrada semejante a la de una piña.
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260530_145543505.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/AK2EyxjscFvPNs6JfmkaE92DRVQ5m77QF5qGdBM4PcwpiQyCVBiq6MgNh4CJqbv.jpg)
</center>
#
Durante este proceso, el cartón se agretió, pero no fue significativo, pues continué el proceder, dándole tres capas de empapelado a la estructura completa con : tiras de papel blanco y pega elaborada de harina. Dejé secar la estructura 8 horas.

# ✨Pasos para confeccionar la base
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260530_145829019.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23yJTLzqfHJEpBmKAJsxLXhCRT9VLPvcuD3wRH8MAK3jRB6X4Q6az8ytNmYFNdGmNwqZw.jpg)
</center>
#
Tomé un cartón cuadrado, realicé una circunferencia en él con ayuda de un lápiz, y corté con ayuda de una tijera la guía marcada, dando cómo resultado un círculo perfecto, al que le dí dos capas de empapelado con : tiras de papel blanco y pega elaborada de harina. Dejé secar la estructura por 8 horas.

# ✨Pasos para crear la parte superior

Tracé en una cartulina blanca un rectángulo de: 25 centímetros de largo y 5 centímetros de ancho. Seguidamente, lo recorté con ayuda de una tijera siguiendo la guía marcada, y le realicé al lateral superior cortes, que lograron ondas continuas.
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260530_150515403.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/AJkU3VfBFSNQDZzwr3VynNJZmmLbfFQDS9WAXGVE6kqcBuqfFKarRqgiUbeAxnJ.jpg)
</center>
#
Habiendo logrado todas las partes del florero, las coloqué cada una en la región destinada, y comencé a unificarlas con tiras de papel blanco y pega elaborada de harina. 
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260530_150830026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23vsbRxJoDkajQSHayqy8uXc7nwzMrsPENTvw3V9wFvxdHNQC8LfpgQZnDD5vx44th2j2.jpg)
</center>
#
Una vez empapelada la estructura completa, la dejé secar por 5 horas y seguidamente, la decoré con pinceles y acuarelas.
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260530_153221958.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/EpXLyJvyVrsvPQQuCoexVKtA571kYuukksAeFxDc9AmAUaqL41vu7xQGeABCv6rkcRq.jpg)
</center>
#
Tonalidades difuminadas de: verde, naranja, rojo, negro, amarillo, fueron las que empleé para darle mi toque personalizado de pintora aficionada☺️.
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260530_152908608.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/ALG1Nr16dM1cQyUyFGTdmyYkLvrY5p16Pox63RnnCD7hXYqPyb9jRVi9fazBnxp.jpg)
</center>
#
Amigos, me encantó el resultado, pues luce espectacular el florero con forma de piña ambientando la sala, generando el deseo a quien lo aprecie , de una deliciosa piña colada 😅. Espero que a ustedes también les haya gustado, y que se animen a reciclar junto a los pequeños de casa con la práctica de esta técnica, les aseguro que la amarán.

Les deseo a todos un feliz y relajado fin de semana en familia y días venideros creativos.¡Abrazos!

Fotografías propias.
*** 
*** 
# English
#  Making a vase in the shape of a pineapple, to decorate my home.Recycling.

# Greetings friends who love crafts.💁☀️
Happy day to everyone!

Friends, I love the practice of paper mache, because in addition to generating emotional peace when I practice it, it allows me to recycle unused materials.Today, I want to share with you through a tutorial, how I made a pineapple-shaped vase to decorate my home, recycling egg cartons. Join me friends, and let's start creating!.
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260530_152301092.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/AJpn6jrpN7B6JenntS5ktTaaVLTjM53MzdUrKESYJLEAZY11ZW75UbRfWU5S1ug.jpg)
</center>
#
# ✨Fruit vase (Pineapple shape)✨

# ✨Materials
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260530_144722121.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23wCLbrpZ9TZfKPzUntxqMjZcea88CBw4jk6PJGjiDFJiKZsLUCayrcnC2bwsCLrjxYpQ.jpg)
</center>
#
.Malleable paper
.White paper strips
.Egg holder carton: 1
.Cardboard
.Cardboard
.Scissor
.Paste made of flour
.Temperas
.Brush
.Pencil

# ✨Mode of preparation✨

To make this vase, I divided the procedure into three moments, a first moment, where I created its body with relief, a second moment where I created its base and top, and a third, where I unified all the parts, and gave life to the craft with picturesque touches.

# ✨Steps to create the body (middle part)
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260530_145108285.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/AJmu2ZUHkoMrDVt1ndykkz3hxiimeYtnzLVvdEn5TDa7KxQyfEZnzXWBAWfpffj.jpg)
</center>
#
I started the procedure by taking the egg carton, and cutting the top two rows with the help of a scissors. Then, I placed this row next to the remaining cardboard, to achieve the complete body of the vase. Then, I was making folds to the cardboard, to achieve a closed circular structure similar to that of a pineapple.
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260530_145543505.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/AK2EyxjscFvPNs6JfmkaE92DRVQ5m77QF5qGdBM4PcwpiQyCVBiq6MgNh4CJqbv.jpg)
</center>
#
During this process, the cardboard was attacked, but it was not significant, because I continued the procedure, giving three layers of wallpaper to the complete structure with : strips of white paper and glue made of flour. I let the structure dry for 8 hours.

# ✨Steps to make the base
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260530_145829019.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23yJTLzqfHJEpBmKAJsxLXhCRT9VLPvcuD3wRH8MAK3jRB6X4Q6az8ytNmYFNdGmNwqZw.jpg)
</center>
#
I took a square cardboard, made a circumference on it with the help of a pencil, and cut with the help of a scissors the marked guide, resulting in a perfect circle, to which I gave two layers of wallpaper with : strips of white paper and glue made of flour. I let the structure dry for 8 hours.

# ✨Steps to create the top

I traced on a white cardstock a rectangle: 25 centimeters long and 5 centimeters wide. Then, I cut it with the help of a scissors following the marked guide, and I made cuts on the upper side, which achieved continuous waves.
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260530_150515403.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/AJkU3VfBFSNQDZzwr3VynNJZmmLbfFQDS9WAXGVE6kqcBuqfFKarRqgiUbeAxnJ.jpg)
</center>
#
Having achieved all the parts of the vase, I placed them each in the intended region, and began to unify them with strips of white paper and glue made of flour.
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260530_150830026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23vsbRxJoDkajQSHayqy8uXc7nwzMrsPENTvw3V9wFvxdHNQC8LfpgQZnDD5vx44th2j2.jpg)
</center>
#
 Once the complete structure was papered over, I let it dry for 5 hours and then decorated it with brushes and watercolors.
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260530_153221958.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/EpXLyJvyVrsvPQQuCoexVKtA571kYuukksAeFxDc9AmAUaqL41vu7xQGeABCv6rkcRq.jpg)
</center>
#
Faded shades of: green, orange, red, black, yellow, were the ones I used to give her my personalized touch as an amateur painter ☺️.
#
<center>
![GridArt_20260530_152908608.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/ALG1Nr16dM1cQyUyFGTdmyYkLvrY5p16Pox63RnnCD7hXYqPyb9jRVi9fazBnxp.jpg)
</center>
#
Friends, I loved the result, because the pineapple-shaped vase looks spectacular, setting the room, generating the desire to whoever appreciates it, of a delicious Pineapple juice 😅. I hope you liked it too, and that you are encouraged to recycle together with the little ones at home with the practice of this technique, I assure you that you will love it.

I wish you all a happy and relaxed family weekend and creative days ahead.Hugs!

Own photographs.

title.title: Las Aves del Paraíso un lugar para soñar - Birds of Paradise — a Place to Dream. [Esp-Eng]
title.body:
>Ya que estamos por aquí arriba, en nuestro recorrido virtual, pensaba terminar el tour de la Gran Piedra antes de bajar la loma, no solo por lo difícil que se haría subir por segunda vez, sino porque con esto cerraría un artículo relacionado a uno de los lugares naturales más bellos que he visitado en Cuba y aunque a él siempre estuve regresando, no he podido hacerlo en los últimos 6 años. Ya habíamos hablado de la Gran Piedra en sí, de sus hermosas vistas, de la experiencia de treparse a la cima y ver el mundo desde allá arriba, de contemplar las nubes como olas chocando en las laderas de la montaña, de las huellas que había dejado el paso del ciclón Sandy y que la naturaleza no curaba del todo. Por otra parte conversamos sobre la mano del hombre en el entorno y el asentamiento francés que transformó todo aquel paisaje en algo mucho más que naturaleza. Y ahora le toca el turno a un lugar sencillo al cual se llega por caminos angostos y repletos de recodos y curvas, hoy vamos a escribir un poco sobre la experiencia en aquel pequeño y hermoso jardín botánico que puede ostentar la categoría de las flores más bellas y raras de la geografía de Cuba. (esto es en sentido general porque la verdad no tengo autoridad para dar este título a nadie ni el conocimiento y experiencia suficientes). Diría entonces que es el jardín botánico con las flores más bellas y raras que he visitado en Cuba.

\n\n>

>Since we’re already up here, in our virtual journey, I thought I’d finish the tour of the Gran Piedra before heading back down the slope—not only because climbing it a second time would be quite the ordeal, but because doing so allows me to close an article dedicated to one of the most beautiful natural places I’ve visited in Cuba. And although I kept returning to it for years, I haven’t been able to go back in the last six.

\n> \n>

>We had already talked about the Gran Piedra itself—its breathtaking views, the experience of climbing to the summit and seeing the world from up there, watching the clouds roll in like waves crashing against the mountainsides, and noticing the scars left behind by Hurricane Sandy, marks that nature has not fully healed. We also spoke about the human hand in the landscape, and about the French settlement that transformed all that terrain into something far beyond nature alone.

\n> \n>

>And now it’s time to talk about a simple place reached by narrow roads full of bends and curves. Today we’ll write a bit about the experience of visiting that small and beautiful botanical garden—one that could easily claim to hold some of the most exquisite and rare flowers in all of Cuba. (I say this in a general sense, because I have neither the authority nor the expertise to grant such a title.) So I’ll put it this way: it is the botanical garden with the most beautiful and rare flowers I have ever visited in Cuba.

\n\n

>Unas de las flores que se robó el espectáculo, sin duda alguna, fue este lirio azul, esta flor imposible de crecer en el clima tropical y áspero de la isla. Muchos al ver mis fotos en redes sociales contactaban asombrados de que se pudiera retratar en Cuba esta flor conocida como agapanthus o lirio africano. Pero a decir la verdad en la isla es poco conocida, mucho menos popular que otras flores, otros lirios. Además, hay que reconocer y recordar que el clima de la Gran Piedra no tiene anda que ver con lo que se conoce del clima de Cuba y menos de gran parte del oriente cubano. Allí a más de 1000 metros sobre el nivel del mar (y aunque en la lejanía se puede observar la costa) las temperaturas bajan a tal punto que en el mes de mayo los habitantes usan abrigos a las 3 de la tarde. Casi todo el año se expone a temperaturas frescas y las nubes (su vapor) mantiene una humedad increíble en el entorno. Por esas y muchas razones vimos allí lo que en el llano no se conoce.

\n\n>

>One of the flowers that truly stole the show, without a doubt, was this blue lily—an impossible bloom to grow in the tropical, rugged climate of the island. Many people, after seeing my photos on social media, reached out in disbelief that such a flower—known as agapanthus or African lily—could be photographed in Cuba. But the truth is that on the island it’s not well known, far less popular than other flowers, other lilies.

\n> \n>

>And we must acknowledge something else: the climate of the Gran Piedra has little to do with what most people know about Cuba’s weather, especially in the eastern region. Up there, more than 1,000 meters above sea level (even though the coastline can be seen in the distance), temperatures drop so much that in May the locals wear jackets at three in the afternoon. Almost the entire year is marked by cool temperatures, and the clouds—their vapor—keep the environment incredibly humid. For these and many other reasons, we saw there what cannot be found in the lowlands.

\n\n

>Helechos, begonias y orquídeas eran la vegetación que rodeaba las carreteras y los caminos que te llevaban a todos los lados. Recuerdo ver con asombro que allí existían de forma silvestres plantas que solo había visto en macetas y muy bien cuidadas en las casa de los amantes a la botánica. Asombrado de las características del lugar, de los helechos arbóreos (que ya había conocido en Viñales) y que se hacían presente en estas hermosas montañas; de las orquídeas que nacían en la tierra y que solo había visto de forma controlada en invernaderos u otros jardines botánicos que había visitado en otros lugares y muchas más cosas que me parecieron maravillosas.

\n\n>

>Ferns, begonias, and orchids lined the roads and paths that led everywhere. I remember being astonished to see, growing wild, plants I had only ever seen in pots, carefully tended in the homes of botany enthusiasts. I was amazed by the characteristics of the place: by the tree ferns (which I had already encountered in Viñales) now appearing in these beautiful mountains; by the orchids sprouting directly from the earth, which until then I had only seen cultivated in greenhouses or other botanical gardens I had visited elsewhere; and by many other things that struck me as truly wonderful.

\n\n

>Pues allí estaba todo preparado para que nosotros lo descubriéramos al final de uno de esos intrincados caminos. Pensábamos que habíamos errado las señas y que andábamos algo perdido, caminamos por más de un kilómetro y cuando ya dudábamos de le existencia del lugar, cuando la idea de rendirnos comenzaba a rondar la cabeza, de pronto apareció ante nosotros lo que era la entrada a una de las experiencias más intensas vividas en las alturas de la sierra. Donde otrora hubiera un cafetal estaba el jardín, en lo que era uno de esas más de 171 cafetales de antaño, ocupando el espacio que pudiera estaba el jardín. Hoy recuerdo que encontraba muros desgastados por el tiempo y la intemperie, caminos de piedra muy bien colocados en cresta de colinas y dentro de todo aquello en armonía las especies vegetales que se conservaban.

\n\n>

>Everything was set there for us to discover at the end of one of those intricate paths. We thought we had misread the directions and were somewhat lost; we walked for more than a kilometer, and just when we began to doubt the existence of the place—when the idea of giving up started to creep into our minds—suddenly the entrance appeared before us, leading to one of the most intense experiences I’ve ever lived in the heights of the Sierra.

\n> \n>

>Where once there had been a coffee plantation, now stood the garden—occupying the space of one of those more than 171 plantations of old. I remember finding walls worn down by time and weather, stone paths carefully laid along the ridges of hills, and within all of it, in harmony, the preserved plant species

\n\n

>Orquídeas negras ¡Qué espectáculo! lirios que me hicieron recordar telenovelas brasileñas emitidas en mi infancia, otras plantas que aún estoy averiguando que son, cómo se llaman, qué función cumplen. Todas llenas de vidas, invitando al foráneo que disfrute de todo aquello que se le ofrecía, mostrándose como en la representación de un teatro por actos la belleza de la naturaleza concentrada en aquel espacio de tierra.

\n\n>

>Black orchids—what a spectacle! Lilies that brought back memories of Brazilian soap operas aired during my childhood, and other plants I am still trying to identify—what they are called, what role they play. All of them brimming with life, inviting the outsider to delight in everything they offered, presenting themselves as if on a stage, act by act, with nature’s beauty concentrated in that patch of earth.

\n\n

>Pero lo mejor siempre se reservaba para el final, en ese último tramo de suelo que tienes que recorrer y que te va indicando que la vista va concluyendo. En ese camino, rodeado por ambos lados un enjambre de lo que inicialmente parecían colibríes en pleno vuelo, libando las flores que habían a su alrededor, pero no, la sorpresa fue aún mayor cuando nos dimos cuenta que era un enjambre pero de flores, hermosísimas flores, que se metamorfoseaban y parecían el diminuto ave. En eso momento se aclararon mis ideas y el nombre del jardín comenzó cobrar sentido: Aves del Paraíso.

\n\n>

>But the best was always reserved for the end, in that last stretch of ground you have to walk, the one that signals the view is drawing to a close. Along that path, surrounded on both sides by what at first seemed to be hummingbirds in full flight, sipping from the flowers around them—but no, the surprise was even greater when we realized it was not a swarm of birds but of flowers, exquisite flowers, metamorphosing and resembling the tiny bird. At that moment, my thoughts became clear, and the name of the garden began to make sense: Birds of Paradise.

\n\n

>Ahora solo queda dejar la narración en silencio para que se pueda contemplar las minúsculas maravillas que se iban encontrando a cada paso, cada metro valió la pena recorrer, admirar y dejar grabado en la memoria de nuestro viaje por cada uno de los rincones de esta isla.

\n\n>

>Now all that remains is to let the narration fall silent, so that the tiny wonders discovered at every step can be contemplated. Every meter was worth walking, admiring, and engraving into the memory of our journey through each corner of this island.

\n\n

/>

title.title: Champions League final: PSG are champions of Europe. Again.
title.body:
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cryptosimplify/23swdrj5kBokP9yDQizy6eAWa9yaHRZvFTTw5M8rztHe51c4s7brFXptYSu1UwAjqPUCg.png)


I said at the end of the semi-final piece that I wouldn't make a prediction for this final. I said I wanted to quit while I was ahead after calling the PSG-Arsenal matchup correctly. I said something like \

They couldn't. And they didn't.

PSG 1-1 Arsenal after extra time. 4-3 on penalties. Paris Saint-Germain are the first team to retain the Champions League since Real Madrid won three straight from 2016 to 2018. And Arsenal, after everything — after twenty years of waiting, after the greatest season in their modern history, after getting so close they could practically taste it — are going home with nothing but heartbreak and a penalty miss that Gabriel Magalhães will see every time he closes his eyes for the next decade.

---

## Six minutes of hope

Arsenal scored first. Of course they did. Because the universe needed to give them hope before ripping it away. That's how these stories work.

Kai Havertz found the net in the sixth minute. The German — who apparently joined Cristiano Ronaldo on some historic Champions League scoring list with this goal, though I'll be honest I didn't have time to look up which one — got on the end of a loose ball in the PSG box and finished with the composure of a man who's been waiting his entire career for this moment. 1-0 Arsenal. Six minutes played. The Emirates would have been shaking if they were in London. Instead, the Arsenal end of the Puskás Aréna erupted and for a few minutes, just a few beautiful minutes, you could feel an entire fanbase believing that this was finally their year.

But here's the thing about scoring early in a final. It sounds great on paper. In practice, it means you have eighty-four minutes to defend the lead against a team that has the best attack in European football. And PSG have the best attack in European football.

Arteta set up Arsenal exactly as he'd done against Atlético in the semis — deep, compact, disciplined, suffocating. The same approach I praised in the semi-final writeup. Rice dropping between the centre-backs. Saliba and Gabriel forming a wall. Raya sweeping up behind them. The plan was clear: score early, sit deep, frustrate, counter, survive.

For forty-five minutes, it worked. Sort of. PSG had the ball — 75% possession by the end of the game, which is genuinely obscene — but Arsenal's shape held. Marquinhos made a brilliant sliding tackle in first-half stoppage time to stop Havertz from making it 2-0, which would have been curtains. Instead, it stayed 1-0 at the break and Arsenal retreated to the dressing room knowing they were forty-five minutes from glory.

They were also forty-five minutes from agony. They just didn't know it yet.

---

## The inevitable Dembélé

I've written about Ousmane Dembélé so many times over these playoff rounds that I've lost count. Two goals and an assist in the first leg against Bayern. The decisive goal in the second leg in Munich. The reigning Ballon d'Or winner. The best player in the Champions League this season. The man for the biggest moments.

So of course he scored in the final. Of course he did.

65th minute. Kvaratskhelia — the guy I've been describing all tournament as the man who sends defenders to the shadow realm — picked up the ball on the left, drove at Mosquera, got into the box, and was brought down. Penalty. No debate, no VAR controversy, just a clear foul on a player who'd been terrorizing the Arsenal right side all evening.

Dembélé stepped up. The Ballon d'Or winner, the man with ice in his veins, the man who's scored in virtually every knockout game this season. Raya went the wrong way. 1-1.

And from that moment, the final changed. Arsenal had been comfortable — not dominant, not in control, but comfortable in their defensive shell. The equalizer cracked the shell open. Suddenly Arsenal had to come out and play, and PSG were waiting for exactly that.

Kvaratskhelia hit the crossbar with about fifteen minutes left. It took a slight deflection off an Arsenal defender and kissed the bar on its way over. Inches. Literal inches from PSG taking the lead. Vitinha unleashed a right-footed strike from the edge of the box that whistled past the far post by centimeters. PSG had 21 shots to Arsenal's 7. Four on target to Arsenal's one. Safonov didn't have to make a single save. Not one. For an entire Champions League final, the Arsenal attack produced precisely zero shots on target in open play. The only shot that beat Safonov was Havertz's goal in the sixth minute, and even that came from a scramble rather than a constructed move.

---

## Extra time and the slow march to penalties

Extra time was tense, messy, exhausting. Both teams were running on fumes. PSG made tactical subs — Marquinhos and Vitinha came off for Zabarnyi and Lucas Beraldo, which told you everything about Luis Enrique's mindset: fresh legs for a potential penalty shootout, not fresh attackers for a late winner.

Arsenal tried to push but they had nothing left. Gyökeres and Havertz kept winning aerial duels from Raya's long kicks, giving Arsenal an outlet, but the final ball was always missing. Rice was immense, covering every blade of grass, but even he was flagging by the 110th minute. Saka, who'd been so brilliant in the semis against Atlético, couldn't find the space to run into. PSG's defensive shape — the same defensive shape I praised in Munich, where Luis Enrique turned the most attacking team in Europe into a defensive unit — was flawless.

The whistle blew on 120 minutes. 1-1. Penalties.

The last Champions League final to be decided on penalties was Real Madrid vs Atlético in 2016. A decade. We'd waited a decade for another shootout in the biggest game in club football. And boy, did it deliver.

---

## The shootout that broke Arsenal

I need to walk through this because every single kick matters.

Gonçalo Ramos went first for PSG. Calm, composed, sent Raya the wrong way. 1-0 PSG.

Gyökeres stepped up for Arsenal. The man who'd been so clinical from the spot against Atlético in the semis. Same composure. Bottom right corner. 1-1.

Désiré Doué for PSG. Right side, Raya went the other way. 2-1 PSG.

Eberechi Eze for Arsenal. And here's where it started to unravel. Eze — who'd been brilliant all season, who I mentioned in the semi-final preview as a potential match-winner — did one of those stutter runs where you stop three times before hitting it. He stuttered one too many times. The kick was weak, the direction was obvious, and Safonov saved. 2-1 PSG.

Achraf Hakimi for PSG. The Moroccan full-back who's been one of the best players in the world this season. Cool as anything. 3-1 PSG.

Declan Rice for Arsenal. Had to score. Did score. Brilliant penalty, hard and low, no chance for Safonov. 3-2 PSG.

Lucas Beraldo for PSG. The sub who'd come on specifically for this moment. Left-footed, into the corner. 4-2 PSG.

Gabriel Martinelli for Arsenal. Had to score to keep Arsenal alive. He did. Smashed it into the net with conviction. 4-3 PSG.

And then. Gabriel Magalhães.

---

## The cruelest irony in football

I wrote about Gabriel in the semi-final piece against Atlético. I said his last-ditch tackle on Giuliano Simeone \
I said he and Saliba were \

I meant every word of it. Gabriel has been extraordinary this season. A colossus. A leader. The kind of defender who makes everyone around him better.

And now he had to take the fifth penalty, with Arsenal trailing 4-3, with the entire season — the Champions League final, Arsenal's first since 2006, possibly the biggest moment in the club's modern history — resting on his right foot.

He ran up. He hit it. And the ball sailed over the bar. Not by a little. By a lot. Way, way over, into the Budapest night sky, into the void where Arsenal's Champions League dreams have lived for the past twenty years.

Gabriel fell to his knees. His hands went to his face. Marquinhos — the PSG captain, his fellow Brazilian, his friend — immediately ran over and put his arms around him. It was one of the most human, most devastating, most beautiful moments I've seen on a football pitch. The man who'd just won the Champions League consoling the man who'd just lost it. Because Marquinhos understood, the way only another footballer can, that Gabriel hadn't just missed a penalty. He'd missed THE penalty. The one that would follow him for the rest of his career, no matter how many league titles he wins, no matter how many clean sheets he keeps, no matter what else he does in his life.

The PSG end exploded. Flares were lit. Players piled on top of each other. Luis Enrique stood on the touchline with his arms raised, the same quiet intensity he's shown all tournament. Dembélé grabbed a flag. Kvaratskhelia slid on his knees. João Neves — our João Neves, the kid from Lisbon who's now won back-to-back Champions Leagues at 21 years old — was crying.

On the other side, Arteta stood motionless. Saka sat on the pitch with his head between his legs. Rice stared into the middle distance. And Gabriel stayed on his knees, head buried in his hands, while Marquinhos kept holding him.

---

## What this final meant

PSG are the first team to retain the Champions League since Real Madrid's three-peat. Let that sink in. Last year they beat Inter 5-0 in Munich. This year they beat Arsenal 4-3 on penalties in Budapest. Two completely different finals, two completely different challenges, same result. This PSG team isn't just good. They're a dynasty in the making.

Dembélé finishes the tournament as the standout performer. I said in the semi-final piece that he had to be in the Ballon d'Or conversation. After tonight — a penalty in the final, plus his absurd record of five goals and two assists in the knockout rounds — I'd say he's the favorite. The man who was once called a flop at Barcelona, who couldn't stay fit, who was dismissed as all talent and no end product, just scored in both legs of a Champions League semi-final AND the final. Redemption doesn't even begin to cover it.

Kvaratskhelia, despite not scoring tonight, was the best player on the pitch for long stretches. He won the penalty. He hit the bar. He terrorized every Arsenal defender who tried to stop him. The Georgian is the engine of this PSG team and everything dangerous they do starts with him.

And Luis Enrique. What do you say about Luis Enrique? The man took over a PSG project that was a punchline — the Qatari-funded circus that could never win in Europe — and turned it into the most dominant team on the continent. Back-to-back Champions League titles. No Messi. No Neymar. No Mbappé. Just a system, a philosophy, and a group of players who believe in it completely.

For Arsenal, this is devastating but not a failure. I know that sounds hollow right now, especially if you're an Arsenal fan reading this. But think about it. They won the Premier League. They reached the Champions League final for the first time in twenty years. They went unbeaten in the group stage and the knockouts until tonight. They took PSG — the defending champions, the team with 75% possession — to a penalty shootout and lost by one miss. ONE MISS. One penalty that went over the bar instead of into the net. That's not a failure. That's the thinnest margin imaginable between glory and heartbreak.

Arteta said afterwards that Arsenal should be \

this summer. He's right. This team is close. So close. They just need to find a way to take that last step. And maybe — maybe — the pain of tonight is what pushes them over the edge next year.

---

## Final thought

I started covering these Champions League semi-finals a few weeks ago. I predicted PSG vs Arsenal in the final after the first legs and got it right. I praised Dembélé as the player of the tournament and he proved it again tonight. I said Gabriel and Saliba were the best centre-back partnership in Europe and I stand by that, even now, even after the miss. Because one penalty doesn't define a player. A career does.

But tonight, in the Puskás Aréna, under the Budapest sky, one penalty defined a final. Gabriel's kick went over. Marquinhos held him. And PSG lifted the trophy.

Football can be beautiful. Football can be cruel. Tonight, at the same moment, it was both.

***Greetings nature observer community***
Hope everyone is doing well. I am also doing well. Today I am here to share a wonderful photography with you. Basically, today I am here to share a very beautiful photography of the Laughing Dove bird with you. 

After waking up in the morning, I was fresh and then enjoyed the nature outside. I really liked enjoying nature outside. Enjoying nature and the calls of all the birds and the cool breeze fascinated me. I enjoyed nature with great joy in the morning. 

Then I saw a beautiful bird in the hands of a little girl and it was a

title.title: SAYING THE TRUTH DOESN'T MEAN YOU ARE SAFE
title.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeatgWoSVEJBuk1NcM2rMSG3SPYESFNsM2jpv67uRan76/screenshot_20260222_114650_1.png)


Growing up, they told me “Truth is the best policy”. 
Nobody told me “Truth can also get you slapped”.

I learned it the hard way last year at work. 

My boss asked in the meeting: “Who forgot to send that client waybill report?” 
Silence. Everyone looking at the floor. 

I raised my hand. Told the truth. “It was me, sir. I mixed up the dates.” 

I thought honesty = safety. I thought they’d clap for my courage. 

Instead? Query letter. “Unprofessional”. Colleagues started avoiding me like I had virus. For weeks I became “that careless girl”. 

The truth set me free? No. The truth made me a target. 

That day I understood why people tell white lies. “It wasn’t me” would’ve kept me safe. “The system was slow” would’ve kept my name clean. 

I’m not saying lie always. I’m saying: Saying the truth doesn’t mean you are safe. 

Sometimes truth is medicine. Sometimes truth is a knife. 

So for Week 219, my take is this: Tell the truth, yes. But learn wisdom too. Learn timing. Learn how to say hard things without destroying yourself. 

Because being honest and being safe are not always the same thing. 

 I want to know:
Have you ever told the truth and regretted it? Or told a white lie and felt guilty but safe? Which one hurt you more? 👇

I’m @nc6, learning that honesty needs wisdom as backup.

title.title: Britain becoming a Gobal AI Hotspot...?
title.body:
According to Katie Prescott’s piece in The Times, “Striking gold in the streets of King’s Cross,” the UK is becoming one of the global hotspots for AI companies. 

Prescott points out how companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind are heading into London, and they are prepared to pay big salaries for top-tier AI developer talent. 

King's Cross has become a hotspot for this, where universities and starts up huddle and support each other. 

I guess this is no real surprise: Britain has some of the best centres in the world for maths, computer science, and engineering. Cambridge, Oxford, Imperial, UCL — for decades they’ve been the launchpad for tech talent all over the world.

And for once Britain finds itself in a field where it actually holds real global sway.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/revisesociology/23uQg3EQNPYGKzj2hgqLcm8BrHU16VSTwHCJY2Egx9db3hK4wcWpSd5TnmQNqkM46Pk5Z.png)


### The obvious upsides....

AI companies bring in money, credibility, and high salaries. More startups sprout up, more venture cash flows, and global eyes focus on London. If these firms really take off, King’s Cross could end up being to AI what Silicon Valley is to software.

It’s not just about tech jobs. Britain desperately needs a kick in productivity, and AI could help here. 


And at the development level AI doesn't require huge amounts of physical resources. It craves knowledge, networks, and computing power — stuff London actually has.

### The downsides...

One founder complains about a “salary arms race.” Smaller startups can’t keep up if the big US firms are tossing millions at the best people. It’s like the little fish end up grooming talent just for the giants to scoop them up.

This is just the way capitalism: works of course: little companies innovate, big companies gobble them up (or their people), and pretty soon all the power gathers at the top.

Most major AI firms still have American roots. Britain supplies the brains, but the profits and control can end up somewhere else.

And then there's the other people in King's Cross... if it does become like Silicon Valley the ordinary people are just going to get priced out as rents soar. 

### Final thoughts...

It's probably just another case of the top 1% winning and the rest of losing!

title.body:
¡Hola, Comunidad de Hive! Hoy les comparto una recopilación de la serie CABALLEROS DORADOS, una colección de dibujos que he venido trabajando en los últimos meses tomando como referencia a los personajes homónimos del anime Saint Seiya. Aquí les dejo un colage con los 12 caballeros así como su respectiva imagen individual. 
.
Hello, Hive Community! Today I’m sharing a compilation from the GOLDEN KNIGHTS series—a collection of drawings I’ve been working on over the past few months, inspired by the characters of the same name from the anime *Saint Seiya*. Here’s a collage featuring all 12 knights, along with individual images of each one.

title.body:
[![](https://images.3speak.tv/images/1780180664087-95e1e3f446ef7592.webp)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=lazybug/d8a99757)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=lazybug/d8a99757)


---

<center><sup>The thumbnail was created in Canva.</sup></center>

<div class=\

>

After detonating explosives to harvest the Black Rock Prism, I evaded hostile Astral Spikes in the quarry. I fought through Hiss Soldiers, escaped via a control point, and returned to Marshall. I delivered the prism, learning that Jesse's brother Dylan was detained here as candidate P6.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmT5TuuvjtmAxvio8pbV7itrq27sDyZAeSM3oZRthvuKd1/screenshot_1_.png)

I had to collect the Black Rock Prism from the excavated seam after activating the explosives to excavate it.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaRkkSt7b1bewbhVTvrZseX8jzXqpq9QzyPdmDnbbnk7e/screenshot_2_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYg5rvTBX7VKtcSweSPBnpNxE3b29UZ46wgtS8CofrW7T/screenshot_3_.png)

Right after collecting the prism, I noticed there were more than one Astral Spike to stop me. So I climbed up to a height as soon as I could, when I had to meet and speak with Marshall next.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZdkMAcwoBrBditatdwhnrbQkrmAhjB3STQa6rDgUsobj/screenshot_4_.png)

I was looking for a way to get out of this mining area without facing those Astral Spikes. But when I was getting back through the same route I came by, I noticed there were some Hiss Soldiers to stop me when there were already some Astral Spikes placed around.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNguWhuNGaRbGsHMPGZBhweyJsRysGveGkNvgS9JDbu9Y/screenshot_5_.png)

I ran back to the mining area, as I understood it wouldn't be good for me if the Astral Spikes caught me, and the Astral Spikes were not leaving me by any chance.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRRtcNnNkaKQJsUst2easP5GkH9KVKfPiVD4cxT2pA1nA/screenshot_6_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmU3nowDZ3yhZfxYq8QTNaqFJrEe5PvGqXrtrCmyFTNhFX/screenshot_7_.png)

After checking around and taking some time, at last I decided to go forward, ignoring the risk, and after taking care of some Hiss Soldiers, I walked out of the mining quarry while an Astral Spike was on my trail.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQE3Jgo9zfBxf3a4Q5rTBiAfn8Yectse8x6xirM8CmxVw/screenshot_8_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYkeYSD4ZkDWkedU32R4S1eg9icSb8Z9KJJ4KRbfmBksi/screenshot_9_.png)

Then I found a control point that I used to fast travel to the central executive right away. And I found Marshall waiting for me there.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXc5Gw5KekS41Vmhj8HighQt8tgmXY8L6CQLmuZAaM6oP/screenshot_10_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWCwCfWPJaKTMHTbWw3Z4TyXRu8Tf1dzdH1doKgBca1u2/screenshot_11_.png)

After handing the prism over to Marshall, she mentioned they would restart HRA production immediately. And then Marshall talked about Jesse's brother when Jesse was confused about whether she should talk to her about Dylan.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXEsvgLx7rwnBdydVY6Avzif3qra8CstdfANG7SSHZKGg/screenshot_12_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfKKtdscWH1fRYRqvtWy54kRwmPcFv7RVEMhGAm2YupXx/screenshot_13_.png)

Marshall said Jesse's brother is here, who was once known as Prime candidate 6, codename P6. And they brought him here after the ordinary event, as he had talents far beyond any other candidate in the program.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeNTUPpmcCCb5Q6xjZ5Kd1PJ79HDCx9LFboAswBRnwtaA/screenshot_14_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaoYCeY3z9BMz57GhaBZHFkkwMhJSbhBLuPA6jFk7xUeU/screenshot_15_.png)

Then I was shown a cabin where I could see the name Jesse written on a glass by sketches, and I had a glimpse of Dylan.

**To be Continued...**

---

title.body:
Interesting idea !  Personally, I hate that the world is moving towards an SaaS model, but I accept that's the way the world is. 

From a business perspective, I've just gone through a serious process recently of trimming out those packages I don't use enough or which are no longer value for money. Too many packages have gone from £5, £10 or £20 a month two years ago to £50 or £100 or more a month now. That's an increase way above inflation, and almost always because the companies involved have been bought out by venture capital. It leaves a gap in the market for good products that are sensibly priced.

I like the plugin model that Wordpress uses, but it's something which will need careful thought and long-term planning. We dropped a WooCommerce site last year (which is effectively a Wordpress plugin), because it was getting incredibly slow, clunky and unmanageable. The key issues were plugins that stopped playing nice with each other as different teams updated each one, combined with problems handling growing volumes of historical data. With nearly 10,000 products and a stack of historical order data growing by several thousand a month, plus some real inefficiencies around email handling, it just didn't work.

So it's definitely a good idea, but needs good planning. It could create you a huge workload, though, so I'd suggest documenting everything as you do it so that it's easy to bring other talented coders onboard when you need them (not to mention that good documentation can be make or break from a user perspective). I wonder if using HBD as the native crypto, but enabling customers to pay in BTC, ETH etc that gets converted to HBD to minimise fees, would be a great core integration. Some people run from crypto, but if you can make it feel like a natural part of the system that might be less of an issue.

I'd say go for it, even though there is a lot to consider and a huge amount of marketing needed ! Just make sure you plan it out so you don't get overwhelmed, and make sure the monetisation model works for the users but also gives you enough to make it worthwhile !

title.title: Hotel Saratoga (Esp-Eng)
title.body:
> Hola, mis amigos. Que placer saludarlos este sábado. Excelente fin de semana para todos. Hace unos días anduve caminando por la Habana y pude ver que esto es lo que queda del Hotel Saratoga, un mítico hotel de cinco estrellas, famoso por su ubicación privilegiada y su historia. Durante muchos años, este inmueble fue visitado por miles de turistas. Se encuentra ubicado casi frente al Capitolio y desde sus habitaciones y su terraza con piscina las vistas dan justo hacia el Capitolio. Alcanzó mayor popularidad gracias a la visita de figuras como Beyoncé o Madonna. Cada cubano o foráneo qué lo vio, puede dar fe de que este no era un sitio cualquiera.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmefajeYEff2rYxv26jABwQXoMgkjhUPu3Nrvza2P7w2WP/1780180888760.jpg)

> El Hotel Saratoga es un ícono de esta capital con más de un siglo de historia. Si se fijan bien, en la parte superior está grabado con hermosas letras el nombre. El Hotel Saratoga no era solo un lugar para hospedarse, era una clase magistral de arquitectura de La Habana. Ubicado en la esquina de Prado, su presencia era un homenaje a la elegancia europea. Primeramente fue construido como un edificio de vivienda, pero su verdadero esplendor llegó en la década de 1930 cuando fue transformado en el hotel que cautivó al mundo. Su fachada monumental, de estilo neoclásico, era su mayor tesoro. Los detalles arquitectónicos que se podían ver eran una muestra de artesanía exquisita. Al caminar por sus aceras, la mirada se elevaba inevitablemente. Recuerdo que tiempo atrás pasaba por allí y me quedaba boquiabierta admirando la belleza del lugar. En una ocasión me tomé un café allí con una amiga. El Saratoga no solo se contemplaba, sino que se vivía. Su azotea y terraza no eran un simple mirador, sino un balcón privilegiado hacia la historia, ofreciendo vistas panorámicas del Paseo del Prado y el Capitolio que se fundían con el horizonte habanero. Aunque por dentro fue modernizado para convertirse en un lujoso hotel de cinco estrellas, su fachada se preservó como evidencia de la grandeza académica que, incluso con sus cicatrices, nunca dejó de ser el emblema distinguido de jna de las esquinas más fotogénica de La Habana . Sin embargo, toda esa belleza ahora es historia, una horrible tragedia lo dejó así como lo ven ahora. El 6 de mayo de 2022, una explosión de una pipa de gas destruyó gran parte de la fachada y provocó más de 40 víctimas mortales. Por suerte, no había turistas en su interior en ese momento, pero en cambio, si murieron varios cubanos, casi todos trabajadores del hotel. Recuerdo que la esposa de un colega mío de trabajo perdió la vida allí. Durante la explotación los pisos de arriba quedaron intactos y por eso no fue necesario demolerlo y empezar de cero. Actualmente el hotel se encuentra cerrado al público y en proceso de reconstrucción y no se puede visitar. A diario se ven movimientos y ruidos que denotan que se trabaja. Las autoridades trabajan en tareas de restauración y apuntalamiento estructural, pero aún no hay fecha para su reapertura. A decir verdad, va bastante lenta esta obra. Los invito a buscar en Internet para que vean su antigua fachada y demás. Esperemos que más temprano que tarde, el Hotel Saratoga vuelva a recuperar su antiguo esplendor.
https://images.ecency.com/DQmUJDibgVv7QpnG7cFRyL8RrNKwrY4Tkx4636U9mec4jSH/img_8206.gif https://images.ecency.com/DQmeR514KUcazwo9QidR6DqXvT3VXLKNLMwh76kPaoFQmCe/img_9027.png

> Hotel Saratoga Hello, my friends. What a pleasure to greet you this Saturday. Wishing you all an excellent weekend. A few days ago, I was walking around Havana and I could see that this is what remains of the Hotel Saratoga, a legendary five-star hotel, famous for its privileged location and its history. For many years, this building was visited by thousands of tourists. It is located almost in front of the Capitol, and from its rooms and its rooftop terrace with a pool, the views look directly toward the Capitol. It gained even greater popularity thanks to visits from figures like Beyoncé and Madonna. Every Cuban or foreigner who saw it can attest that this was no ordinary place.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmefajeYEff2rYxv26jABwQXoMgkjhUPu3Nrvza2P7w2WP/1780180888760.jpg)

> The Hotel Saratoga is an icon of this capital city, with more than a century of history. If you look closely, the name is engraved at the top in beautiful lettering. The Hotel Saratoga was not just a place to stay; it was a masterclass in Havana’s architecture. Located on the corner of Prado, its presence was a tribute to European elegance. It was first built as a residential building, but its true splendor came in the 1930s when it was transformed into the hotel that captivated the world. Its monumental neoclassical façade was its greatest treasure. The architectural details visible were a display of exquisite craftsmanship. Walking along its sidewalks, your gaze would inevitably lift upward. I remember that some time ago I would pass by there and stand in awe, admiring the beauty of the place. Once, I had a coffee there with a friend. The Saratoga was not just something to be contemplated; it was something to be lived. Its rooftop and terrace were not merely a lookout point, but a privileged balcony onto history, offering panoramic views of the Paseo del Prado and the Capitol, blending with the Havana skyline. Although the inside was modernized to become a luxurious five-star hotel, its façade was preserved as evidence of its academic grandeur, which, even with its scars, never ceased to be the distinguished emblem of one of Havana’s most photogenic corners. However, all that beauty is now history. A horrible tragedy left it just as you see it now. On May 6, 2022, an explosion from a gas tanker destroyed much of the façade and caused more than 40 fatalities. Fortunately, there were no tourists inside at the time, but instead, several Cubans died, almost all of them hotel workers. I remember that the wife of a colleague of mine lost her life there. During the explosion, the upper floors remained intact, so it wasn’t necessary to demolish it and start from scratch. Currently, the hotel is closed to the public and in the process of reconstruction, and it cannot be visited. Daily, there are movements and noises indicating that work is being done. Authorities are carrying out restoration and structural shoring tasks, but there is still no date for its reopening. To be honest, this work is progressing quite slowly. I invite you to search online so you can see its former façade and more. Let us hope that sooner rather than later, the Hotel Saratoga regains its former glory.

title.title: 🔥 Learning to Be Confident in My Own Skin
title.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmTMjeFrV9RNicx4zg22jeGzdkzda9V2tbkYavaYHmAx83/IMG_8733.jpg 

Some days I feel stronger… more sure of myself, like I’m finally starting to understand who I am. Not because everything is perfect, but because I’m learning to accept every part of me, even the parts that are still growing.

I used to overthink a lot about how I looked, how I acted, what people expected from me. But now, little by little, I’m letting that go. I’m realizing that confidence doesn’t come from being perfect… it comes from being real.

I’m still figuring out my future, still thinking about studying chemistry and building something meaningful with my life. But at the same time, I’m also learning that I can feel beautiful, strong, and proud of myself right now, not just when I “make it.”

This is me… learning, growing, and slowly becoming someone who is not afraid to be seen.

title.title: Música patriótica: Cantaremos por siempre la marcha militar
title.body: Música patriótica: Cantaremos por siempre la marcha militar =========================================================== * * *
>Cantaremos por siempre la marcha militar (Hát mãi khúc quân hành) es una famosa y perdurable canción patriótica de Vietnam compuesta y escrita por Diệp Minh Tuyền en 1984.

>La canción captura el idealismo y la dedicación del personal militar vietnamita, con su inquebrantable espíritu de lucha, como se sabe prácticamente imposible de derrotar (a menos sea exterminado) dado su ilimitada disposición a sacrificarse por su patria.
>La segunda estrofa de la canción expone bien lo comentado por medio de una de las metáforas más relevantes de la música patriótica de Vietnam:

>

Dù rằng đời ta thích hoa hồng

>

Aunque en nuestra vida amamos las rosas,

>

Kẻ thù buộc ta ôm cây súng

>

el enemigo nos obliga a empuñar el fusil.

>

Ta yêu sao làng quê non nước mình

>

¡Cuánto amamos las aldeas, las montañas y los ríos de nuestra tierra!

>

Tình quê hương vút thành thanh âm khúc quân hành ca.

>

El amor por la patria se eleva hasta convertirse en el sonido de esta marcha.

**Nota:** La traducción es de Gemini
>En otras palabras, no buscamos la guerra, amamos la paz, pero no por eso vamos a dejar de luchar si somos atacados, porque no estamos dispuestos a ceder un palmo de nuestra tierra.

>En efecto, como es conocido, en Vietnam fueron capaces de derrotar no a una, sino a dos potencias, primero a Francia y luego a EE.UU.; si bien en este último caso la guerra era más bien civil y no está del todo claro el vencedor puesto hoy en día Vietnam se parece más a Vietnam del Sur.

>La música pueden escucharla por medio del siguiente video en YouTube, donde se muestra un desfile militar de batallones femeninos vietnamitas:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kj3HDD8W\_fE ¿No les parece motivante esta marcha? Me despido deseándoles lo mejor a todos los miembros de la comunidad. En una próxima publicación trataré de comentarles sobre otra música propia de una de las variadas culturas del mundo menos conocidas en mi región. ¡Hasta la vista!

title.title: The Dragon Summoner Dragonlord Mancer Has Been Added To  My Deck
title.body: /> Hello, my lovely friends in the Splinterverse. I hope everyone is having a great time in Splinterlands, with even more fun from new cards and strategies. For a long time, I have not been writing about Splinterlands as I am not playing the game so often as I used to play previously. Even I am not collecting my daily rewards not from the modern or the frontier format. But I found that Splinterlands is becoming more exciting as new abilities are coming to the Splinterverse regularly with the new cards and so many new summoners. I am so happy to be part of the journey of the evolving Splinterlands, and I am very happy to have found a special summoner from the last conflict from the Conclave Arcana edition. The summoner I have got from the last conflict of this Conclave edition and it a dragon summoner called 'Dragonlord Mancer' which is the best one from this edition according to the number of abilities that it provides to the friendly monsters in the battle.

/> Dragonlord Mancer is also the most expensive summoner in this series which is good luck for me, and I have used it in some battles, and it is really giving some amazing results for winning these battles. I have now plan to level up this summoner to the level two version that will be a great addition to my decks to have better results in my battles, especially in the modern format. I hope to write about more details about the performance of the summoner in my future blogs. I hope you find some useful information in the post that will add more fun to your Splinterlands journey. If you have any questions, you can ask me in the comments. I will try to answer them as much as I can. Thanks a lot for your time and attention. I will catch you at the next one. Have a great day! #SplinterlandsStrategy

/> And, If you want to be a proud member of the Splinterlands community and enjoy the magical world of hundreds of monsters and strategies for your battle **you will have the opportunity of amazing battles with some extraordinary monsters with amazing abilities that will uplift your online gaming experience to a new level.** You can enter the Splinterverse through this link [sign up to join Splinterlands](https://splinterlands.com?ref=tanzil2024)

title.title: The W.I.S.E model
title.body:
![2FC37ED2-6851-47ED-A03A-31828E68110B.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dwayne16/23wqnrg26uMKfmBTHLM1EfTja6ah42ZuKE2YN1YGNjtBrRdag4kWLVGGn89GLxiu7oVxn.jpeg)

***
Positive Thinking and Creative Problem-Solving
The W.I.S.E. Model is a unified framework drawn from five transformative works. The framework brings together ideas from five influential authors across five decades and presents them as a single architecture for peak thinking and creative problem-solving.
The five voices behind this framework are Dr. David O. Oyedepo, author of Winning Wisdom; Dr. Caroline Leaf, author of Switch On Your Brain; Norman Vincent Peale, author of The Power of Positive Thinking; Edward de Bono, author of Lateral Thinking; and James Webb Young, author of A Technique for Producing Ideas. Together, these works contribute different dimensions of thinking, creativity, and personal transformation.
The W.I.S.E. Model consists of four stages. W stands for Wisdom and asks the question, “Where does true insight begin?” This stage is drawn from the teachings of Dr. David Oyedepo. I stands for Inner Architecture and asks, “How do I build a mind that can receive it?” This stage is based on the work of Dr. Caroline Leaf. S stands for Spirit of Possibility and explores the question, “What attitude enables me to act on it?” This stage is influenced by Norman Vincent Peale. E stands for Execution and asks, “How do I channel it into solutions and ideas?” This final stage draws from the work of Edward de Bono and James Webb Young. Each stage depends on the one before it, and together they form a complete architecture for Peak Thinking and Creative Problem-Solving.
The first stage is Winning Wisdom. According to Dr. David Oyedepo, “Winning wisdom is the Supernatural Ability to bring solutions to matters too difficult for the ordinary human mind.” In the context of problem-solving, this means that the greatest answers are received by the prepared thinker, not manufactured. Wisdom is not the reward of more effort; it is the fruit of divine connection. Before developing a strategy, one should first go to the Source, which is God.
Dr. Oyedepo further explains that wisdom is not the same as mental exertion. Wisdom is not thinking harder, researching more, or simply being more disciplined. Rather, wisdom is “Uncovering God's approach to every issue of life.” It involves knowing which way to go before the path is fully visible and represents the application of knowledge rather than its mere accumulation. As Dr. Oyedepo states, “The application of knowledge is what is called wisdom. Until a man amasses adequate knowledge, there will be nothing for him to use.”
This understanding is illustrated through the Knowledge-Wisdom Ladder. The first level is Information, which involves gathering facts, data, and experience. This is where most people begin. The second level is Knowledge, which involves organising and understanding information. Many people stop at this stage. The third level is Wisdom, which is the application of knowledge to produce results. Most people never reach this level. The key insight is that knowledge gives power, while wisdom gives strength. The leap from knowledge to wisdom requires more than study; it requires seeking.
The second stage of the framework is Inner Architecture, based on the work of Dr. Caroline Leaf. Her core discovery is that every thought a person thinks physically changes the structure of the brain. Referencing Romans 12:2, she argues that the brain is not fixed but is instead a living, dynamic architecture that is constantly being built or dismantled. Individuals are not merely products of their neurology; they are its architects. Consequently, the mind that is prepared to think well is also the mind that is positioned to receive wisdom.
This stage creates a critical link with the ideas presented by Dr. Oyedepo. While Dr. Oyedepo teaches that wisdom must be received, Dr. Leaf explains the mechanism through which this reception becomes possible. A healthy and properly structured mind becomes the environment in which wisdom can flourish.

Mogę podsumować to jedynie subiektywnie. Dziękuję za wszystkie spotkania z dziećmi, młodzieżą, opiekunami, kierowcami i przedstawicielami biur podróży. Było miło i wszystkich wspominam pozytywnie. To jest fajne w tej pracy.

title.title: God is waiting for you to let go
title.body:
I have realized that the major problem of believers, including myself, is truly trusting in God. We may feel like we do, say it with our lips; but deep down we still fear the situation before us. Jesus said to his disciples when they came in contact with the barren fig tree (Mark 11:12-25) that a little faith like a mustard seed can move mountains, yet as small as the mustard seed is, our faith cannot measure up to it, not because we can't but because instead of seeing Jesus before our situations we see the situation first and fear never leaves room for faith to grow.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXCJfRBSNursPmSAekHw7r77k1yJNv6aWajw5uSw7RqHa/1780180441407.png)

**Image gnerated using Gemini AI**

See yourself holding a sharp knife under your palm with your fist closed. You may pray and ask God to take the knife out from your palm, but he wouldn't, not because he can't, but because he would hurt you if he pulls it out with your fist closed. You'll first need to open your palm and let go of the knife gripped under your palms for him to take it out without hurting you. The knife is your problems, the hands gripping the knife are doubt, fear, and uncertainty. You'll need to let them go first for God to come in.

True trust shifts our focus from our problems to God's character, which naturally silences anxiety (Isaiah 26:3). All that God requires from believers is faith—that he is able and is beyond whatever situation we are in. We may not understand the process or his ways, but he requires that we choose his way daily, setting aside doubts and every form of it. To trust God, we would first understand that no amount of our worries can add a single solution to our problems, just like in Matthew 6:27. So let go of that fear, let go of the worries of tomorrow, and shift our focus to God's character—that nothing is too hard for him to do.

title.body: Have you ever seen an ocean-like wave crashing inside a river? Deep here in South Papua, at the Digul River, we face a natural phenomenon locals call \

​ https://img.leopedia.io/DQmVzMxWnzrcEBoMcJdVMSkxzCenwzyWCM5YLb89AYB6oeW/1000662282.jpg

It is a powerful reminder of nature's raw energy.

title.body:
Saludos amigos de la comunidad Hivediy, les mando un abrazo virtual y espero estén pasando un buen fin de semana, hoy en casita descansando para comenzar de nuevo la rutina esta semana del trabajo y la universidad, hoy quería realizar algunas figuras pero la electricidad no me dejó.


>Greetings friends of the Hivediy community, I send you a virtual hug and hope you are having a good weekend. Today I'm at home resting to start the routine again this week of work and university. Today I wanted to make some figures but the electricity didn't let me.



https://i.ecency.com/DQmQJDFJP2HBgkvq1jAAoNBNHRtMMi85pamQ7yqLuVhbRWd/1001524727.jpg




Así que hoy les quiero compartir un nuevo llavero inspirado en una de las cartas del juego Splinterlands, se trata de la marioneta poseída, está carta se ve tenebrosa por su apariencia física lleva consigo cuchillos, y su la forma de su cara fuera de lo común, así que es una buena idea para recrear con limpiapipas.


>So today I want to share a new keychain inspired by one of the cards from the Splinterlands game, it's the possessed puppet. This card looks creepy because of its physical appearance, it carries knives, and the unusual shape of its face, so it's a good idea to recreate it with pipe cleaners.


<center>
![Possessed Puppet.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXHgrdBBi4kmgszMG2XDYGetYqou3Qbfn15i9kFCd79Au/Possessed%20Puppet.png)
[Possessed Puppet](https://www.splintercards.com/chaos_rewardsb_possessed-puppet) 
</center>


Tarde unas 4 horas en terminar ya que algunos detalles son complicados de realizar y quería que fuese lo más parecida posible, espero les guste el resultado a continuación los materiales y el paso a paso.


>It took me about 4 hours to finish because some details were complicated to do and I wanted it to be as similar as possible. I hope you like the result. Below are the materials and the step-by-step instructions.


<center>
![ezgif-17234730318dcd18.gif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaP3FTwt3ea1iQzTD3hBVAEvVt64y8DU9FdjhbspQMazH/ezgif-17234730318dcd18.gif)
</center>




![1000100308.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQX1QCU8EKjdgAjeZpBNuDdZqxkg2pWGQEVHPRjdtuyPX/1000100308.png)


|Materiales | Materials|
| --------|---------|
|Limpiapipas gris, blanco, negro, rojo, marrón |Gray, white, black, red, brown pipe cleaners|
| Tijera, silicón | Scissors, silicone |
|Esfera de anime #4 | Anime Sphere #4|
| Encendedor|Lighter|
| Aro para llavero |Keychain ring |


![1001521468.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marile21/23wCJSZ6ETkPFP3wVLA9PqipARCWRtWK4xJWWChCUiVeHfZTepUznp5bz3cJssmGxQNv4.jpg)


![1000100308.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQX1QCU8EKjdgAjeZpBNuDdZqxkg2pWGQEVHPRjdtuyPX/1000100308.png)

### *Paso a paso / Step by step*
#




El primer paso que vamos a realizar será seleccionar el número de la esfera de anime, en este caso será una #4.


Voy a comenzar a cubrir con limpiapipas blanco uno de los extremos hasta alcanzar la mitad de la esfera, luego vamos a cubrir la otra mitad pero de color negro, considerando que el lado izquierdo será blanco y el lado derecho negro como se muestra en la imagen.



>The first step we'll take is to select the number of the anime sphere; in this case, it will be a #4.

>I'm going to start by covering one end with white pipe cleaners until I reach the middle of the sphere. Then we'll cover the other half with black pipe cleaners, keeping in mind that the left side will be white and the right side black, as shown in the image.


|![1001521548.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marile21/EoK6p8uLZnYPibh5cYMygnzFKzxftKuZVnmpdGAyeNz8XUDTebZ1QntP84mP8AZcEoT.jpg)|![1001521549.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marile21/23wCBrgei4LD7sfWBRB1kYrDBQYBc9kJ7LfEGSXBhumfZnAG7vsuVqhG6J2QXKyWBhNR2.jpg)|![1001521556.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marile21/23u69XwYe39w1RckVqeFxWKBFdQ9MWEbtJxkgzTkby74XhrSJ3BphiS2qETUjbdfR7zqd.jpg)|
|-|-|-|


|![1001521662.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marile21/23tvnfKRyTCTaqPhtZRucNNB4wNmgVt7L2px6E4zUnWffpxma5BNxU8tTwHUTAxqDpUw7.jpg)|![1001521720.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marile21/23vsYmCCkRDbyfhm738QMxBo5MkMFRso9nNEQB1VpGLno3eGWEC5r9UuoPW1d7pwuFRkc.jpg)|
|-|-|




Ahora vamos a cubrir en el centro con limpiapipas blanco y negro la idea es realizar la línea irregular que lleva en el centro de la cara, también voy a realizar el cabello, para esto utilicé limpiapipas gris, voy a unir tres piezas dobles para formar las trenzas.

>Now we're going to cover the center with black and white pipe cleaners. The idea is to create the irregular line down the center of the face. I'm also going to do the hair; for this I used gray pipe cleaners. I'm going to join three double pieces to form the braids.


|![1001521767.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marile21/23x1FTcWr6k97WuoAZWWDur4gHs3X1ReBFmbZh4pxPTExJqpyFmzgV1BbgDtiUMKC8f2W.jpg)|![1001521813.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marile21/23uFYA1fakqN1coGgddAa1qtXJMv9EU24sEAsTcpNqHxnmPpxBEbPhA1ptckfcDV6dEVR.jpg)|![1001521836.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marile21/23w2uRut83MTbiVwkMQKKnbeXkZTgCYfvJaNbSqNGvNWL5jYpZPTXwL5n3dacP7nS97YR.jpg)|
|-|-|-|


|![1001521843.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marile21/23uFaMK8kV58o8XLGtvZ4bKJpuPh539gWP1kRTnB5hqTVBBjfbF9XKrTRntnZB9p27uiw.jpg)|![1001521884.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marile21/23wMh2aC2KjKYMhP5QNYVCJy6xZBxULyEqNoS3H5RKiiQ8diGZEvsBdtiy4ymknWtUt9Z.jpg)|
|-|-|




Pegamos en la parte superior y cubrimos con otra capa de limpiapipas, en las puntas colocamos limpiapipas marrón, y así mismo realicé dos lazos que ubiqué de cada lado.


>We glued it on top and covered it with another layer of pipe cleaners, at the tips we placed brown pipe cleaners, and I also made two bows that I placed on each side.


|![1001521887.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marile21/23w2sG9weQR2dwngdSKbdNjthJuFW2vfgsXVdez6VN47J8nHLB7W5reE82RVrAVZe3T3h.jpg)|![1001521888.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marile21/23wqrjn7ESFcWmhu3MGSZuBs7mrTJ1VqZapDBxhLdYLNtrBbUP397qQLwCVGxnzrgP57C.jpg)|
|-|-|





Ahora vamos con los detalles del rostro, del lado izquierdo realicé el ojo de color negro, para las líneas lo que hice fue cortar pequeñas piezas del alambre del limpiapipas y pegamos, del lado derecho el ojo blanco, en el centro un círculo de limpiapipas rojo, y una linea de color amarillo.

>Now let's go over the details of the face. On the left side, I made the eye black. For the lines, I cut small pieces of pipe cleaner wire and glued them on. On the right side, the eye is white, in the center is a red pipe cleaner circle, and a yellow line.

|![1001521889.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marile21/23wCJN9nrqTCghqpYUcSbSu9XHqWD4sZMWusy7YcQXFwFQxg8ydL1TetS8TBkuUm2UjyM.jpg)|![1001521891.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marile21/23w2uCz2gUHF6WwD7gsrPmwoJ7g1jtTCgNFXuRTZZ2AxqA13EzRKTVE5LXcuRYmDTk3jL.jpg)|
|-|-|




Del lado derecho colocamos los dientes, solo debes cortar pequeñas piezas de limpiapipas blanco y pegar, y del lado izquierdo un alambre de limpiapipas rojo. De esta forma terminé la figura de la marioneta. 


>On the right side, we attach the teeth; you just need to cut small pieces of white pipe cleaner and glue them on. On the left side, we attach a red pipe cleaner wire. That's how I finished the puppet figure.


|![1001521896.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marile21/23tvpttCeJEgk5NpfwUAyiwiyHtdeHTBuzDSzaWMhLcCZLfR6B1q5iuubAtXZh1RSUGrv.jpg)|![1001521919.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marile21/23u6BsQ8115aNACSuhiowzUjhesNZqmXzWB55YR4zi83N7ej7tepd6qtp8PVhhmjH8ut1.jpg)|
|-|-|




Espero les haya gustado el resultado, muchas gracias por el apoyo y por visitar mi publicación, nos vemos en una próxima oportunidad con más ideas creativas.


>I hope you liked the result, thank you so much for your support and for visiting my post, see you next time with more creative ideas.


|![1001521920.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marile21/23xVTLdHP2xXWyfPfimoeR8e713pMaCAX1bMgRUUePd4ystyta2mrCncxJ3mF3RLumoMs.jpg)|![1001521926.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marile21/23vi6Tou4KuP93yWskJFEEgiCrChWzEcNUkt5d9QpZm33A5oHQx5o6PmDkwfr5XkGHzxT.jpg)|
