body.title: ¡Nadie está leyendo mis Artículos! -Cuando el Fracaso obliga a Revisarnos- ¿Cómo Evaluar?  (ES/EN)
body.body:
<center>![español ziodanilo-male-3220990_1920.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emiliorios/23tvkg9HtGdrH1QyTNEHcCcX8Wm7aqT8PYotAJaRhe7yRpQ3CyWw7tZ1wcdEH3ue5sPDw.jpg)</center>

> *<center>[Pixabay-Ziodanilo; editada en Paint](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/masculino-la-gente-retrato-adulto-3220990/)</center>*

###### <center>*Todos sabemos cuánto duele preparar un artículo que se estudia, se piensa y se desarrolla, para que luego, al ser publicado, tenga poca visualización, interacción y una baja valoración. No, no es que estemos dando por sentado que el artículo es bueno, pues puede que simplemente no sea un tema que importe; pero el dolor es el mismo.*</center>

###### <center>*Detrás de un artículo cuidadosamente escrito para tus seguidores hay variables que deben tenerse en cuenta, como que existe una inversión de tiempo que se hace en blogs de seguimientos, en plataformas como #Hive donde hay que mantenerse activo; que existe una cantidad de seguidores fieles y otros que de vez en cuando llegan; y que hay una temática que deseamos desarrollar. Detrás hay una serie de fracasos y de éxitos, de experiencias y, aprendiendo a veces a golpes; y hay dedicación, hay amor por ofrecer lo mejor que se pueda; por eso hablemos sobre: **¿Cómo mejorar esto y cómo evitar de alguna manera que tu artículo pase sin pena y sin gloria?***</center>

<center>![stocksnap-people-2605980_1920.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emiliorios/23x14eqsXen7P1QabYNswmZSm829RRsoKSLTcPYccocCp3PxoLszXb3Qb7a1MoNocKe6H.jpg)</center>
> *<center>[Pixabay-StockSnap](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/gente-hombre-chico-barba-2605980/)</center>*

<div class=\

> ### Horas y horas invertidas, que no escribiendo… Detrás de un artículo hay horas; hay tiempo para gestar una idea, estudiarla, analizarla, buscar razones, opiniones y referentes. *No se valora un artículo por el tiempo de lectura: **¡Si tiene 15 minutos de lectura, seguro que tardó 15 minutos en hacerlo!*** *Esto no es verdad.* Un buen artículo tarda aproximadamente entre 1 a 2 días en gestarse; y esto cuando es rápido; y yo reconozco que soy bastante rápido, porque tengo experiencia en trabajos de investigación y tengo mi rutina de cómo buscar un tema determinado que me interesa desarrollar. Generalmente, parto por mi experiencia y, con base en lo que vivo, desarrollo temas que valoro, aleccionadores y generadores de opiniones. Esta semana desarrollé sobre la creatividad, que tanto se me está exigiendo para los trabajos de investigación y que nos sirve para desarrollar un pensamiento de poder en emprendimientos. *Creo que sin creatividad no hay buenas empresas ni soluciones a los problemas mundiales; sin embargo, el artículo actualmente es prácticamente un fracaso.* A mí me pareció sumamente importante, pero a otros no. Y tuvo su tiempo de estudio a nivel teórico… Igualmente, escribí sobre la esperanza, que es una vivencia que Venezuela tiene hoy en día y que es algo que me gustaría que desarrolláramos en nuestras plataformas de bienestar. Son temáticas que nacen de la experiencia, es cierto, pero necesitan estudios; no se pueden lanzar opiniones desde mi perspectiva sin tener referentes que certifiquen, que den datos ciertos, por respeto al público. *Por eso, es importante que pongamos atención a ciertos detalles. Y aunque he publicado anteriormente sobre cómo escribir y mejorar la marca personal, nunca está de más volverlo a hacer.*
![stocksnap-guy-2618928_1920.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emiliorios/Ep1VuEW5DJEw3aHWsCDfWLFF3FFptjV6rgPAmVLqZzUxo2yQHGzTjorsoMLaXBqNt39.jpg)
> *
[Pixabay-StockSnap](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/chico-hombre-laboral-2618928/)
* ### ¿Por qué fracasó mi artículo tan bueno? *[Gabriela Literaria es un blog para afrontar desafíos de escritura](https://gabriellaliteraria.com/)*; entre esos, hay un artículo que se llama: ***[Las 13 razones por las que nadie visita tu blog (de escritor)](https://gabriellaliteraria.com/nadie-visita-tu-blog/)***; y aunque evidentemente lo está escribiendo desde el año 2000 o 2001, es un referente para que nos explique las posibles razones por las que un artículo poco interesó. Ella nos pide que evaluemos nuestro diseño de publicación, ya que hay momentos en que la forma como ofrecemos las fotografías y el texto, marean o no gusta. Evaluar qué tan extensos son tus escritos, qué tan actuales los temas y revisar si tienes el mismo modelo todo el tiempo. *Creo que a mí me está faltando eso; ya me pondré a pensar qué debo cambiar porque mis artículos ya no son tan bien evaluados como antes… A pesar de que son temas tan diferentes.* ***Es cierto que @hive en estos momentos no está siendo la de antes, pero, al navegar diariamente en ella, veo que siguen existiendo ventanas y puertas a diferentes partes del planeta por las que podemos llegar hasta otros, pues seguimos siendo muchos.*** Por último, hay que determinar si la gente sabe de qué se trata tu estilo, tu marca personal, tu ortografía y, por supuesto, si existe o no la posibilidad de que estés compartiendo con quienes te leen y generes una historia de vida entre tú como autor y el lector amigo. *Lo cierto es que es importante revisar tu blog, porque tu obra es lo que muestras de tu persona; por lo tanto, si hay que cambiar, se cambia.*
![ziodanilo-male-3222718_1920.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emiliorios/23wqko6XWbSsKC5regqks7PQdr7gcaJ6gksnTcv8QNj9HV4MADwHggCLn895dYbUMG3Rr.jpg)
> *
[Pixabay-Ziodanilo](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/masculino-la-gente-retrato-adulto-3222718/)
* ### Y lo que opina otro Blogger Además de todas de todos los detalles e innovaciones que debemos estar haciendo constantemente en nuestro blog para que se nos vea, otros escritores blogueros de éxito como **[Javi Pastor](https://www.javipastor.com/home/)**, en: ***[La cara oculta del blogging](https://www.javipastor.com/la-cara-oculta-del-blogging/)***, observa que escribir en las redes no es que está de moda, es una manera importante y con beneficios utilizada para interaccionar con otros seres humanos y mejorar nuestras calidades de vida. *Un blog es mucho más que solo escribir, es interaccionar, es dedicarnos y dedicarle horas posteriormente al producto para revisar comentarios e interaccionar con quien te lee.* Es importante responder, así sea un solo comentario; eso es tan vital como 15 o 20 opiniones. No importa si a tu artículo no se le dio la valoración correcta, este es un hijo que debes cuidar y, tarde o temprano, tal vez lanzado en otra plataforma luego, se desarrollará correctamente. Pero como hay plataformas que contemplan evaluar en forma lo más justa posible la calidad de los artículos, uno confía. *En nuestra comunidad soy parte de aquellos que valoran y evalúan los artículos que se publican y puedo decir que me gusta reconocer el esfuerzo y, claro está, las indicaciones muy puntuales del sitio.* Pero sobre todo lo que tiene que ver con originalidad y esfuerzo, pues llegan a nuestros amigos y hermanos que invierten tiempo en navegar en nuestra comunidad y deben tener el mejor contenido respetuoso. *Por último, recordemos que no le gustamos a todo el mundo; que no somos perfectos; que algo puede fallar y muchas veces no sabemos por qué pasó.* ***Y eso se respeta.*** También, que entrar a leerte requiere tiempo, esfuerzo, tanto, como el que tiene el que escribe.
*Al fin y al cabo, todos somos libres de decidir qué nos gusta y que no.*
***Y lo importante es que mantengamos una visualización crítica ante lo que hacemos, porque mejorar, definitivamente es la base de todo crecimiento.***
![línea .png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emiliorios/243LGK6jZhPemzoyW4Y6ZwwG2wS8d24s3Hj3jLs5siVAK741DF7MYgdmfhzdTciEQD3HX.png)
![english a.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emiliorios/23tGTQhrY2qsD9zYVnv6yNSB38E5RUcndDUo2QrnNNjBdWop8nfJ1V9EwAoYNi34zacxy.png)
#
No One Is Reading My Articles! -When Failure Forces Us to Reassess Ourselves- How Should We Evaluate?
![ziodanilo-male-3220990_1920.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emiliorios/23uFY5cytGjveNNgBctMo7wG9iBEWkHLyj63n7eTQXK5GDduxghHzuKhtLtmbweUfGMHU.jpg)
> *
[Pixabay-Ziodanilo; edited in Paint](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/masculino-la-gente-retrato-adulto-3220990/)
* ######
*We all know how painful it is to write an article that you’ve researched, thought through, and crafted, only to have it receive few views, little engagement, and low ratings once it’s published. No, we’re not assuming the article is good—it might simply be a topic that doesn’t matter—but the pain is the same.*
######
*Behind a carefully written article for your followers, there are variables to consider, such as the time invested in following blogs and staying active on platforms like #Hive; the fact that there are loyal followers and others who drop by from time to time; and the specific topic we want to explore. Behind it all lies a series of failures and successes, of experiences, and sometimes learning the hard way; and there is dedication, there is a love for offering the best you can; so let’s talk about: **How can we improve this, and how can we somehow prevent your article from passing by without fanfare?***
![stocksnap-people-2605980_1920.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emiliorios/23x14eqsXen7P1QabYNswmZSm829RRsoKSLTcPYccocCp3PxoLszXb3Qb7a1MoNocKe6H.jpg)
> *
[Pixabay-StockSnap](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/gente-hombre-chico-barba-2605980/)
*

> ### Hours and hours spent—and not just writing… Behind every article lie hours of work; there’s time to develop an idea, study it, analyze it, and search for reasons, opinions, and references. *An article isn’t judged by how long it takes to read: **“If it takes 15 minutes to read, it must have taken 15 minutes to write!”*** *That’s not true.* A good article takes about 1 to 2 days to develop—and that’s on the fast side. I admit I’m pretty fast because I have experience in research and my own routine for researching a specific topic I want to explore. Generally, I start with my own experience and, based on what I’ve lived through, develop topics that I find meaningful, thought-provoking, and opinion-shaping. This week I wrote about creativity, which is so heavily demanded of me for my research work and which helps us develop a mindset of empowerment in entrepreneurship. *I believe that without creativity there are no good companies or solutions to global problems; however, the article is currently practically a failure.* It seemed extremely important to me, but not to others. And it took time to study it on a theoretical level… I also wrote about hope, which is something Venezuela is experiencing today and that I would like us to explore on our wellness platforms. These are topics that stem from experience, it’s true, but they require research; I can’t simply share my opinions without references to back them up and provide accurate data—out of respect for the audience. *That’s why it’s important for us to pay attention to certain details. And although I’ve written before about how to write and improve your personal brand, it never hurts to revisit the topic.*
![stocksnap-guy-2618928_1920.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emiliorios/Ep1VuEW5DJEw3aHWsCDfWLFF3FFptjV6rgPAmVLqZzUxo2yQHGzTjorsoMLaXBqNt39.jpg)
> *
[Pixabay-StockSnap](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/chico-hombre-laboral-2618928/)
* ### Why Did My Great Article Fail? *[Gabriela Literaria is a blog dedicated to tackling writing challenges](https://gabriellaliteraria.com/)*; among them is an article titled: ***[“The 13 Reasons Why No One Visits Your (Writer's) Blog”](https://gabriellaliteraria.com/nadie-visita-tu-blog/)***; and although it was clearly written back in 2000 or 2001, it serves as a valuable reference for understanding the possible reasons why an article might not have garnered much interest. She asks us to evaluate our post design, since there are times when the way we present photos and text can be confusing or unappealing. Assess how long your posts are, how current the topics are, and check if you’re using the same template all the time. I think that’s what I’m missing; I’ll start thinking about what I need to change because my articles aren’t being received as well as they used to… Even though the topics are so different. ***It’s true that @hive isn’t what it used to be right now, but as I browse it daily, I see that there are still windows and doors to different parts of the world through which we can reach others, because there are still many of us.*** Finally, we need to determine whether people understand what your style, your personal brand, and your writing voice are all about—and, of course, whether or not there’s a chance you’re connecting with your readers and building a shared narrative between you as the author and your reader-friend. *The truth is, it's important to review your blog, because your work is a reflection of who you are; therefore, if changes need to be made, you make them.*
![ziodanilo-male-3222718_1920.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emiliorios/23wqko6XWbSsKC5regqks7PQdr7gcaJ6gksnTcv8QNj9HV4MADwHggCLn895dYbUMG3Rr.jpg)
> *
[Pixabay-Ziodanilo](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/masculino-la-gente-retrato-adulto-3222718/)
* ### And here’s what another blogger has to say In addition to all the details and innovations we need to constantly incorporate into our blog to gain visibility, other successful bloggers like **[Javi Pastor](https://www.javipastor.com/home/)**, in ***[The Hidden Side of Blogging](https://www.javipastor.com/la-cara-oculta-del-blogging/)***, note that writing on social media isn’t just a trend—it’s an important and beneficial way to interact with other people and improve our quality of life. *A blog is much more than just writing; it’s about interacting, dedicating ourselves to it, and spending hours afterward reviewing comments and engaging with your readers.* It’s important to respond, even if it’s just one comment; that’s just as vital as 15 or 20 comments. It doesn’t matter if your article didn’t receive the right rating; this is a child you must care for, and sooner or later—perhaps after being reposted on another platform—it will develop properly. But since there are platforms that aim to evaluate the quality of articles as fairly as possible, one can trust them. *In our community, I’m one of those who review and evaluate the articles that are published, and I can say that I like to acknowledge the effort put in and, of course, the site’s very specific guidelines.* But above all, it’s about originality and effort, because these articles reach our friends and fellow members who invest time in browsing our community and deserve the best, respectful content. *Finally, let’s remember that not everyone likes us; that we aren’t perfect; that something might go wrong, and often we don’t know why it happened.* ***And that deserves respect.*** Also, reading your posts takes time and effort—just as much as it takes the writer to create them.
*At the end of the day, we’re all free to decide what we like and what we don’t.*
***And what’s important is that we maintain a critical perspective on what we do, because improvement is definitely the foundation of all growth.***
![línea .png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/emiliorios/243LGK6jZhPemzoyW4Y6ZwwG2wS8d24s3Hj3jLs5siVAK741DF7MYgdmfhzdTciEQD3HX.png)

body.title: ‎🔧 Will My Job Exist in 10 Years? A Plumber's Honest Thoughts About the Future of Work
body.body: ‎Hi Hive,\n‎\n‎It's another beautiful day and according to this week prompt on #indiaunited community \

And here is my answer to that 
‎

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRnUaiqPyjruxv6xQxB6ByQKQAAx5qF2tYpbvMmKUW4bE/1780172771463.jpg)


‎Anytime I hear people talking about artificial intelligence and robots taking over jobs, I always find myself asking one question: What will work look like in the next ten years? Many professions are already changing because of technology, and some jobs are even disappearing completely. It makes a lot of people nervous about the future.
‎
‎As a plumber, I have thought about it too.
‎
‎Will my job still exist in the ten years to come?
‎
‎But, I personally believe it will.
‎
‎Plumbing is not one of those jobs that suddenly appeared in modern era. But it has been around for generations, even long before computers, smartphones, and the internet became part of our daily lives. Every society has always needed clean water and a way to safely dispose of waste. And those needs have never changed till now, and I don't think they ever will.
‎
‎In my own line of work, I deal with real-life problems every day. A leaking pipe in someone's kitchen, a blocked drainage system, or a faulty water connection cannot be solved by a chatbot or an app. Because someone has to show up, inspect the problem, get their hands dirty, and fix it properly. That is where plumbers come in.
‎
‎Even though, I know technology is advancing rapidly. New plumbing tools and smart water systems are making the job easier, faster and more efficient. I actually see that as a good thing. Instead of replacing plumbers, these innovations help us work better and makes our job neat. The way we do the job may change, but the need for skilled plumbers will always remain.
‎
‎And another reason why I am so confident about the future of plumbing is that people will never stop building houses. New homes, offices, schools, and hospitals are being constructed every year. Even old buildings need maintenance and repairs. Pipes don't last forever, and water systems need regular attention.
‎
‎One thing this profession has taught me is that every job evolves. The people who survive are usually the ones who keep learning and adapting. That is why I always try to improve my skills and stay informed about new developments in the industry.
‎
‎So, when people ask whether my job will exist in ten years, I smile and say yes. Because as long as people need water running through their homes and buildings, plumbers will always have a role to play. Trends may come and go, technology may continue to advance, but I honestly believe plumbing is one profession that will remain relevant for many years to come.
‎
‎What about you? Do you think your current job will still exist in ten years?

body.body: >This is probably the most imperfect music video I have ever published here on hive, but then, that is the idea; to make mistakes and to grow. I made this video quite a while ago, but decided that I would not post it simply because I thought it was not perfect. However, I had a change of heart at some point. ____ ![WhatsApp Image 2026-05-29 at 2.03.59 PM.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ernesto6402/244osundZ9bXtYAXdREpmhS8i1Yc6abMJGtFPRQEkfAMc2XXijqf1sf4o6TcHqv71tGrw.jpeg) ___ I have been into music for a long time now, but I have never been good with lyrics. I know friends who could come up with beautiful lyrics right on the spot, but it is just not what I am good at. At some point, I took it as a challenge. I started making gospel freestyles and posting them here on Hive. All the while, it has been going well, but I am not perfect yet. Or probably, I am not yet as good as I wish to become. I have performed freestyles that are better than this in the past. Just like I said, this is probably the worst music video I have ever published here on Hive. Yet, I have decided to post it as I consider it part of my journey. After all, it has not been a perfect journey. There have been so many re-recordings, edits, and sometimes, changes to the intended post; but in all, we kept on making attempts to become better. I ask then, that you consider this post my imperfect attempt. The lyrics were not previously intended, but they ended up speaking of the loving nature of God and the fact that we are completely dependent on His love. The lyrics are indeed beautiful; though they were not organized, they are beautiful. Given that I am yet to get really good at this freestyle thing, I might not have used the most beautiful words, but the message is clear and direct. **I am @ernesto6402, and I appreciate you for stopping by. Make sure to tell me what you think about my performance in the comment section. One Love ✌️.** ![1000347524.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ernesto6402/23wqgaFpe23NAxZ39i2U727FDfnt3x41LQ2xXMNd6SUwBsvLg9UqZR5e7sQ6SD3hs7v2c.png) --- ▶️ [3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=ernesto6402/b774db5b)

body.title: RULES AND REGULATIONS.
body.body: I wouldn't prefer a world where there were no rules nor government because man cannot function without them. And I'm giving my explanation from Christian stand point. ![IMG-20260201-WA0023.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/onyinye-chi/241tb7JDajkAhQ16ctmMzQhzY1Yd5VR85KqFesZUMivKJ7waexb7RWBUrBmwcfVfykYkX.jpg) The Human mind is like an empty container awaiting instructions that will help it function. That is why when God created man He gave him specific instructions pertaining his purpose and function on the earth. Now, with those instructions man was functioning just fine. Perfectly even. But let's allow ourselves to imagine that there were no instructions given to man initially. He would have probably just lived like the other creatures he met. Without any form or sense of morality, and seeing that he was somewhat different from the animals all around him, there's a chance that he would have lived anyhow. Maybe we wouldn't have even gotten to the point of civilization. Let's also consider another scenario where all of a sudden there ceased to be rules and government like we know it. The world will plunge into severe chaos. It will be an apocalypse. Because man in his natural self is selfish. Therefore, every single person will want to only lookout for themselves. Jobs will be abandoned, systems will stop working. It will be the literal end of civilization as we know it. I feel chills just imagining it. The rules and governments that have been and is now have never been perfect, but has helped to shape the world and civilization we experience today. I don't there is much to say here, because we can all try and imagine it ourselves a d see that the world will be too hostile if there were no laws or government, or they stopped existing. One very sure thing is that global population will drastically reduce. Because then it will be the real 'survival of the fittest' case. It will be kill or be killed. Steal or get stolen from. Become vicious or become a prey. The list goes on and on. So no, I do not prefer a lawless world or one without government. Thanks for stopping by my blog. See you soon. 🤗 ### peace out ✌️ ##### ALL PICTURES ARE MINE

>My emotional stability depends on them: my two children, my two cats. I suffer from anxiety and depression, and my days used to be awful, but since they came into my life, everything changed. I feel like I have to work hard for them, earn money to feed them, and take them to the vet when they're sick. Honestly, I don't know what my life would be like if I lost them. I depend on them emotionally, and they love me because they show it with their affection, always seeking me out. When they meow for affection, I have to drop everything, and even though they sometimes make me angry because they don't eat all their food and then ask for more, it's all worth the effort. When I can't find them quickly because they're asleep somewhere hidden, I get scared and start calling their names until they come and I see them. Then I feel at peace. So yes, my emotional stability depends on my cats, Alejandro and Maxinne. That's why I'm sharing some more pictures of my boys from today.

title.title: Sometimes Truth Hurts.
title.body:
Hello Community,

 
When people hear the words white lie they usually think of something harmless.. If I am being honest I think almost everybody has told a white lie at some point in their life.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeSRP69SveoyRtLQFpj6Mt8VNV69GwDBQnjWqQ2XQJgbr/1780171926248.jpg)

I know I have told a lie.

These white lies are not the kind that destroys trust or causes problems but the kind where you are trying to avoid hurting someones feelings,For example when a friend asks if their new haircut looks good and you do not exactly love it, you do not want to completely crush their confidence. These little situations happen all the time with lies.

Now does that make telling lies okay?

Well that is where things get complicated with lies.

Personally I think intention matters a lot when it comes to lies, there is a difference between telling a white lie to protect yourself from accountability and telling a white lie because you are trying to spare someone unnecessary pain with white lies.

For example imagine someone is going through a period in their life,  Maybe they failed an exam lost a job or are dealing with something heavy, Sometimes people do not need honesty at that exact moment, Sometimes they need encouragement first with lies.

That said, I do not think white lies should become a habit.

The problem with lies, even small ones is that they can grow. One white lie often leads to another lie and before you know it you are trying to remember what story you told to which person about the white lie, That is one headache I do not want with lies.

I have also seen situations where people used the phrase  \

as an excuse to hide truths with white lies, In those cases the white lie usually ends up causing damage than the truth would have caused in the first place with white lies.

For me if the truth involves something that directly affects a persons life with white lies then they deserve to know it about the white lie.

It might hurt

It might be uncomfortable

They might even be angry

At least they can make decisions based on reality .

On the hand if we are talking about small everyday situations where the truth serves no real purpose other than hurting somebodys feelings with  then I can understand why people sometimes choose a gentler approach with white lies.

I think there is also a difference between being honest and being harsh

Some people pride themselves on telling it like it is,  but sometimes they are just being unnecessarily rude, You can tell the truth, Still be kind about it, Those two things can exist.

Personally if I had to choose I would still lean more toward honesty than telling lies, Maybe not always the full blunt version of the truth immediately. Honesty eventually.

Because trust is one of those things that's very difficult to rebuild once it is broken with white lies.

If somebody discovers that you have been lying to them with lies even for what you believed was a good reason they may start questioning everything else you have told them about white lies.

That is where problems begin with white lies.

So do I think white lies are always wrong?

No.

Do I think they should be used carefully with lies?

Absolutely.

At the end of the day I think the goal should be kindness without deception whenever possible, If you can tell the truth in a way that is respectful, compassionate and considerate, that is usually the better option 

Because while a white lie may make things easier for a moment honesty tends to last longer.


[Image Credit](https://unsplash.com/photos/selective-focus-photography-of-pinocchio-puppet-Q79XFGuTFfM)

*Good afternoon, lovely people of @diyhub! Today I'm feeling very happy and motivated because I'm bringing you a lovely recycling and sustainable fashion project. I made the most of some leftover scraps from sweaters I made into little boxes. These kinds of projects are my absolute favorites because you can create wonderful things with scraps that would otherwise go to waste.* >*Buenas tardes gente linda de @diyhub! El dia de hoy me encuentro muy feliz y motivada, pues os traigo un lindo proyecto de reciclado y moda sostenible. Donde aproveche al máximo unos recortes sobrantes de unos puloveres que hice cajita. Este tipo de proyectos son los que mas amo hacer, pues se pueden crear maravillas con recortes que hirian a la basura.*
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXZgQPj5A5eGRwd86oGy3jjLQBLQjZQkqHZm51wrFMvju/1780161873491.jpg)
*I don't know why I've become so obsessed with handbags lately. Every time I see a fabric scrap, I immediately start thinking about designs I could use to create an adorable, small, and, in my opinion, very practical accessory. This one was no exception, especially when I saw the remaining colors. Although I wasn't very confident about it because of the type of fabric, nothing can stop me when ideas are born...* >*Nose porque últimamente me he obsesionado tanto con las bolsas o carteritas de mano, cada vez que veo un recorte, enseguida me viene a la cabeza diseños que se pueden hacer para crear un accesorio adorable, pequeño y muy práctico a mi punto de vista. Este no fue la excepción, y mas caundo vi los colores que iban quedando, aunque no le tenia mucha fe por el tipo de tejido, pero nada me detiene cuando nacen las ideas...* >**Similar ideas came to mind...** **Ideas similares que me vinieron a la mente...** ⬇️ https://pin.it/1QlvBcSUI
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQ1qwxqitvdxFytbC69oQwCL3uFnqC4B3WM3hCmUsQ4WB/1780163033607.jpg)
⬇️ https://pin.it/2bMWps23v
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmehqsKyRZWaCtjvQCxKHiyx4VWaNEfvkGfppb6otkfYRh/1780163452626.jpg)
*Here's a mini-tutorial, with a small photo collage, showing the step-by-step process and the materials I used to recreate this garment. For those who love a challenge and sewing, I hope it's helpful and inspires your future creations.* >*Aquí les dejo un minitutorial, con un pequeño collage de fotos, mostrando el paso a paso del mismo y los materiales que utilice para recrear esta prenda. Para los amantes del reto y la costura, espero que les sirva y ayude en sus creaciones futuras.* 🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀

Materiales / Materials

  • Tela
  • Tijeras
  • Hilo y aguja
  • Cinta de medir
  • Alfileres
  • Maquina de coser
  • Liston verde
  • Elástico
    • >Fabric Scissors Thread and needle Measuring tape Pins Sewing machine Green ribbon Elastic 🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀🎀 **Procedure:** **1st step:** *I started by cutting out rectangles of equal size in the four leftover colors I had on hand—plus four strips in those same colors to serve as the handle and its fasteners. Once the pieces were cut, I stitched them together using a straight stitch to join each section, then reinforced the seams with a longer stitch placed 1 cm away from the initial seam.* >**Procedimiento:** **1er paso:** *Comence recortando rectangulos de la misma medida en los 4 colores que me habian quedado sobrando. A parte de cuatro listones de los mismos colores para el aza y amarre del mismo. Una vez picados, pase costura recta empatando cada pieza, y fijando las costuras con una puntada mas larga a 1cm de separación de la ya cosida antes.*
    ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWdAFWP8HXMayFxqfeEEXmWDBk1r4nUUFBW4YX8wTngKL/1780164681716.jpg)
    **2nd step:** *Next, using a pair of scissors, I carefully cut out the shape—or structure—of the bag I intended to create; I then joined the two pieces with their right sides facing each other, ensuring that all the seams would end up on the inside. In addition to this fabric, I took a scrap of denim to provide greater firmness and give the bag a bit more structure. This piece served as the lining for the small bag.* >**2do paso:** *Luego con ayuda de una tijera corte bien la forma o estructura del bolso que iba a desarrollar para luego unir las dos piezas donde estuviesen derecho con derechos, quedando de esta forma todas las costuras por dentro. A parte de este tejido, tome un recorte de mezclilla, para darle mas firmeza, y un toque mas paradito. Siendo este el forro del bolsito.*
    ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmb5x1F6e5v3gK6zSHaXbEcjfvydtWoAyi7xZjnv3jKiGb/1780166432166.jpg)
    **Step 3:** *I stretched the strips I had already cut with great force to create a cord-like strand, as the fabric was elasticized. Using these—or others—I crafted a beautiful five-strand braid, forming a unique, original, and eye-catching handle thanks to the contrast of all those colors. Next, I positioned the lining on the outside, placing it right-side-in so that it faced the right side of the bag's exterior. I then stitched all the way around the top edge, before turning the bag right-side-out through a small opening left at the bottom of the lining.* >**3er paso:** *Los listones que ya tenia recortados, los estiré con mucha fuerza, para obtener una especiede cordon, pues era un tejido elastizado. Con este o los otros realice una hermosa trenza de 5, haciendo un aza unica, original y muy diamativa, por ell contraste de todos esos colores. Seguido coloque el forro por fuera, donde el derecho quedara por dentro y de cara con el derecho de la parte de afuera de la bolsa. Pasando una costura por todo el contorno de la parte de arriba, volteandola luego por una pequeña abertura dejada en la parte baja del forro.*

title.title: Celebrar la vida (Es-En)
title.body:
Un abrazo para esta comunidad que siempre me recibe, mi infinito amor y agradecimiento a @Holos-Lotus.

Me hubiese gustado hacerlos parte de mi felicidad el día de mi cumpleaños, aunque ya les conté que celebro dos días, 26 y 27 de mayo, porque errores en la inscripción me hicieron parte de este puente existencial.

Estuve los dos días sin electricidad, algo terrible por lo que en términos de desarrollo implica tener electricidad: altas temperaturas y un silencio que atrapa cualquier alma.

Pero la felicidad dependía de mí en un gran %, por tanto preparé pastel y otros detalles de brindis, y recibí a mi familia el día 26.

---

---

https://i.ecency.com/DQmUEaaKDcwYyHEhbSxfeD8qByhKLN4KzSSfJGaU7wjeaTu/1780167981366.jpg

---

---

Celebrar la vida es un acto de resistencia y de luz propia. En un mundo que a menudo nos lleva a los límites de la rutina, el agotamiento o la queja, detenerse para honrar la existencia propia y la de los demás se convierte en una clave para ascender.

Desde el día anterior, Jorgito me dijo: \

. Generalmente a los niños les encantan las sorpresas. Me regaló un perfume y se encargó de buscar a sus amiguitos para comer pastel.

---

---

https://i.ecency.com/DQmaKqwXnN8UZQXqVQAxD67u1wPuawU9grgy1GdfBtXr2gT/1780168583860.jpg

---

---

Él no sabe de economía familiar; él solo sabe que en las celebraciones se comparte. Y cuando esa clave funciona, no solo abrimos una, sino muchas puertas que permanecían ocultas a la vista común.

Mi pastel también fue para algunos que, en esos días de oscuridad, posiblemente ese bocado sería lo único.

---

---

https://i.ecency.com/DQmPTk4A7HHofiop3Txt9FkJd4vtybPfcsauxHw9ujtLTFL/1780168908503.jpg

---

---

La primera puerta que se abre al celebrar es la de la conciencia plena. Cuando soplas las velas de una tarta, cuando brindas por un logro o simplemente bailas una canción sin motivo aparente, alejas las malas vibras.

De repente, fui consciente del ahora. Cumplí 57 y en algún agradecimiento dije que agradezco las canas, el no tener arrugas y el dar prioridad a los placeres.

---

---

https://i.ecency.com/DQmXf2ja3JeGi78E34TJZw6rKaoFJLWEAhZpS4Wi4xKgV4A/1780169078897.jpg

---

---

Recibí un regalo muy especial; parte de él eran tres rosas amarillas que venían a mí como fichas que completaban un puzle.

Celebrar te ancla en el presente, y en ese anclaje descubres que la vida no es solo un problema por resolver, sino un regalo por disfrutar. Entras a un estado de conciencia donde todo toma su orden.

https://i.ecency.com/DQmaRUykKsZz2aTYG4UQQ4sUFi8pqu9bQDhTYXEni8Jmxmo/1780169410515.jpg

Luego, mis amigas se confabularon para hacerme la vida más agradable. Se abrió la puerta de la conexión. La celebración es, por naturaleza, un acto colectivo. Incluso cuando celebramos en soledad, lo hacemos imaginando a quienes queremos o agradeciendo al universo.

La carencia y la crítica se disuelven para dar paso al abrazo, al cariño expresado sin miedo, a la vulnerabilidad compartida. Esa puerta da paso a un pasillo donde la empatía crece como una enredadera que une los corazones.

---

---

https://i.ecency.com/DQmfRJ8JXFeuWLysA5hzteUevEQuFaPFWoA1J5XZDFLcRWe/1780169578586.jpg

---

---

Al decidir festejar el simple hecho de estar vivos, aceptamos la fragilidad de nuestra existencia, y esa aceptación nos hace más fuertes. No se celebra a pesar de las grietas, sino con ellas, y al hacerlo, la luz entra por esas mismas grietas.

Finalmente, se abre la gran puerta de la gratitud. La celebración genuina: un café, una sangría, un cóctel. Cuando celebras lo pequeño, entrenas a tu cerebro para buscar el asombro. Y en ese estado, la vida deja de ser una lucha y se convierte en un mosaico de milagros cotidianos.

---

---

https://i.ecency.com/DQmeBovwHX8VTVJ3LVB4BAHH3DUbvieW3mWHmvX3aYYcXCB/1780169741251.jpg

---

---

Por eso, no esperes a tener todas las respuestas ni a solucionar todos los problemas. Celebra hoy. La puerta ya está ahí. Al otro lado, la vida te espera con los brazos abiertos y una fiesta que nunca termina.

https://images.ecency.com/DQmfFnEMCYnFkP4yn3RAjCC5Yi2Bw4pZMYk2wKE2HWeExdE/1739658658260.jpg

<sub>Gracias por visitar mi blog. Soy crítica de arte, investigadora social y amante de la cocina. Te invito a conocer más de mí, de mi país y de mis letras. Texto y fotos de mi propiedad.</sub>

https://images.ecency.com/DQmfAxqWjfHD2t6iFUv1FivzQTFzsMmbGqywoexFuT14L8s/1750582840520.jpg


**Celebrating Life**

A hug to this community that always welcomes me, my infinite love and gratitude to @Holos-Lotus.

I would have liked to make you part of my happiness on my birthday, although I already told you that I celebrate two days, May 26th and 27th, because mistakes in the registration made me part of this existential bridge.

I spent both days without electricity — something terrible, considering what having electricity means in terms of development: high temperatures and a silence that traps any soul.

But my happiness depended on me to a large extent, so I prepared a cake and other toast details, and I received my family on the 26th.

---

---

https://i.ecency.com/DQmUEaaKDcwYyHEhbSxfeD8qByhKLN4KzSSfJGaU7wjeaTu/1780167981366.jpg

---

---

Celebrating life is an act of resistance and one's own light. In a world that often pushes us to the limits of routine, exhaustion, or complaint, stopping to honor our own existence and that of others becomes a key to rising.

The day before, Jorgito told me: \

Children usually love surprises. He gave me a perfume and made sure to gather his little friends to eat cake.

---

---

https://i.ecency.com/DQmaKqwXnN8UZQXqVQAxD67u1wPuawU9grgy1GdfBtXr2gT/1780168583860.jpg

---

---

He doesn't know about family finances; he only knows that during celebrations, you share. And when that key works, we open not just one, but many doors that remained hidden from plain sight.

My cake was also for some people who, in those days of darkness, that bite might have been the only thing they had.

---

---

https://i.ecency.com/DQmPTk4A7HHofiop3Txt9FkJd4vtybPfcsauxHw9ujtLTFL/1780168908503.jpg

---

---

The first door that opens when we celebrate is that of full awareness. When you blow out the candles on a cake, when you toast to an achievement, or simply dance to a song for no apparent reason, you drive away bad vibes.

Suddenly, I became aware of the now. I turned 57, and in one moment of gratitude I said that I am grateful for my gray hair, for not having wrinkles, and for prioritizing pleasures.

---

---

https://i.ecency.com/DQmXf2ja3JeGi78E34TJZw6rKaoFJLWEAhZpS4Wi4xKgV4A/1780169078897.jpg

---

---

I received a very special gift; part of it was three yellow roses that came to me like pieces completing a puzzle.

Celebrating anchors you in the present, and in that anchoring you discover that life is not just a problem to solve, but a gift to enjoy. You enter a state of consciousness where everything falls into its place.

https://i.ecency.com/DQmaRUykKsZz2aTYG4UQQ4sUFi8pqu9bQDhTYXEni8Jmxmo/1780169410515.jpg

Then, my friends conspired to make my life more pleasant. The door of connection opened. Celebration is, by nature, a collective act. Even when we celebrate alone, we do so by imagining those we love or giving thanks to the universe.

Lack and criticism dissolve to make way for the hug, for affection expressed without fear, for shared vulnerability. That door leads to a hallway where empathy grows like a vine that unites hearts.

---

---

https://i.ecency.com/DQmfRJ8JXFeuWLysA5hzteUevEQuFaPFWoA1J5XZDFLcRWe/1780169578586.jpg

---

---

By deciding to celebrate the simple fact of being alive, we accept the fragility of our existence, and that acceptance makes us stronger. We do not celebrate despite the cracks, but with them, and by doing so, light enters through those same cracks.

Finally, the great door of gratitude opens. Genuine celebration: a coffee, a sangria, a cocktail. When you celebrate the small things, you train your brain to seek wonder. And in that state, life stops being a struggle and becomes a mosaic of everyday miracles.

---

---

https://i.ecency.com/DQmeBovwHX8VTVJ3LVB4BAHH3DUbvieW3mWHmvX3aYYcXCB/1780169741251.jpg

---

---

So don't wait until you have all the answers or until you've solved all your problems. Celebrate today. The door is already there. On the other side, life waits for you with open arms and a party that never ends.

***
***

<sub>Thank you for visiting my blog. I am an art critic, social researcher, and cooking lover. I invite you to learn more about me, my country, and my writing. Text and photos are my property.</sub>

title.title: My Actifit Report Card: May 30 2026
title.body:
Hello Actifit community and fellow fitness lovers! ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/10662e0d-8899-4e47-83c6-e52f9b3e1b09.jpg) ​Happy Saturday! Today is May 30, 2026, and the weekend is in full swing. After yesterday's amazing adventure in Richmond Park, I decided to keep the outdoor vibes going but switched things up with a refreshing walk along the gorgeous riverfront right here in Kingston upon Thames. Walking by the water has a unique way of making the exercise feel effortless, and today was no exception. ​I am thrilled to report that I've locked in another successful day of movement, finishing my Saturday evening with a solid total of 11,192 steps! ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/3be5abf5-1cce-49d8-be0e-dea57674a99c.jpg) ​Breaking Records 22 Days of Pure Dedication! ​Hitting my 10,000 step goal is always satisfying, but the real star of my Actifit dashboard today is the consistency tracker. I have officially extended my consistency streak to 22 days in a row! ​Entering the fourth week of an unbroken streak feels incredible. It proves that once you push past the initial hurdle, fitness stops being something you have to force yourself to do and simply becomes part of who you are. The Actifit Web updates are still looking great on the app interface, keeping everything running smoothly while I focus on maintaining this great momentum. ​Swans and Beautiful River Views. ​The River Thames in Kingston looked absolutely beautiful today. The water was calm, reflecting the bright blue sky and the lush green trees lining the opposite bank. One of the best parts of walking this route is the abundance of wildlife. I came across a wonderful group of swans gliding gracefully near the concrete steps by the edge of the water. ​ You can see a large gathering of them relaxing on the riverbed, while a few pigeons joined the mix, hoping to catch some crumbs from passersby. Getting up close to these elegant birds was the perfect excuse to pause for a moment, catch my breath, and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere. There is something incredibly therapeutic about the sound of water and the gentle movement of nature in the heart of the town. ​Making the Most of the Weekend. ​Weekend steps always hit a bit differently compared to busy weekdays. Without the rush of daily chores, I could truly take my time, extend my route along the towpath, and enjoy the vibrant energy of people out enjoying the riverside. If you are struggling to hit your numbers, heading to a local riverbank or waterfront path is one of the best ways to get those steps climbing without even noticing the distance. ​How is your weekend shaping up? Did you take advantage of the nice weather to get your steps in today? Let me know your numbers and your favorite walking spots in the comments below!
_This report was published via Actifit app ([Android](https://bit.ly/actifit-app) | [iOS](https://bit.ly/actifit-ios)). Check out the original version [here on actifit.io](https://actifit.io/@lovlygirl/actifit-lovlygirl-20260530t201108714z)_

title.body:
В переддень Дня Києва цікаво згадати важливий історичний момент в історії міста, а саме початок будівництва каналізаційної мережі, який почався 30 травня в 1893 році.

Як і перший водогін, каналізаційна мережа брала свій початок з тодішньої Царської площі (нині Європейська).

Але фактично запущена в роботу каналізаційна мережа була аж у жовтні наступного 1894 року. Київська каналізація була першою мережею на теренах тодішньої російської імперії, яка була спланована та збудована за правильними передовими розрахунками, які і нині залишаються актуальними.

Перша працююча каналізаційна мережа мала довжину трубопроводів 3000 км., до якої було під'єднано майже 2000 будинків.

title.title: The Lean Startup - Book Review
title.body:
>

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbnHP9pLc7gcnfCT2DWSkT1vCerXmFDFThvkW8Kx3WULq/the_lean_startup_book_review.jpg)

The Lean Startup is a book written by Eric Ries, which, through three parts (Vision, Direction, and Acceleration), aims to impart knowledge on how a startup should be managed to the reader.

It's quite curious how I came across this book. The other day, a short video recommendation appeared where the presenter discussed some books I had already read and ranked them below this book called \

which made me curious to see if it was really that interesting.\n\nI ended up looking for the book in some stores and noticed that the feedback was very positive, and since the subject seemed quite interesting, I decided to give it a chance. You might think this book isn't for you since it's about startups, but according to the author Eric Ries' own definition, \

In today's world, with innovations happening constantly, the possibility of pandemics, wars, and changes in global trade, we can conclude that we are in a scenario of extreme uncertainty, which is precisely the conditions that startups have to deal with. This book presents the lean startup methodology to help entrepreneurs succeed amidst constant uncertainty. Therefore, even if you are not a startup, the concepts in this book can help you survive in this uncertain environment. An example to illustrate how quickly everything changes is that every year technology companies hold meetings to share upcoming innovations, governments make agreements with other countries, and wars erupt unexpectedly. In this scenario, the more you learn to survive and have a sustainable company, the better it will be for you. I'll be much appreaciated if you **Votes**, **Reblogs** or give any **Tips**. Thanks and have good reading! 🍀 ---

>

## The Lean Startup - Short Book Review

<center> ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSKoAbzjvCRuuJWtBmTkhYuFYui1dFNCAsjb4mMjSWD5L/image.png) </center>
<center>Author: Eric Ries</center>

At the beginning of the book there is a topic titled \
which gives an overview of the content of each of these parts. The first topic of the book, \

, is more introductory and the author shares some stories and gives some definitions, such as who an entrepreneur would be, what a startup would be and a fundamental concept that is validated learning, which he himself learned thanks to a failure in one of his ventures.\n\nThe second is called \

, in which the author uses the lean startup method itself, addressing the build-measure-learn feedback cycle, something that is well used in businesses that work with the public, in which the feedback ends up shaping the final product.\n\nFinally, the last topic is \

, which is, as the name suggests, simply executing the feedback cycle presented previously in the Steering chapter, but faster. The difference is that at this stage, in addition to carrying out this task, at the same time it will be in the process of expansion. I'm still at the beginning of the book and until then, the feedback I have is from the first part of the book. What I liked so far is that it has good definitions and some insights that can be learned. The problem is that much of it comes from the author telling his own story, which ends up making this beginning quite tiring at least. I remember that in another book this was a big problem for other people when the author starts telling a lot of stories and doesn't get straight to the point. I think he spoke in a more explicit and simple step-by-step manner, I think a mix of the author explaining the concepts on one page and then telling them in a way that gives an example would be more interesting. --- https://img.leopedia.io/DQmVA8nYfdsJtPHvQ22mgMdhDhpJEiYmuLkjyQFGFtDHnFB/Divider.png ---

>

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbnHP9pLc7gcnfCT2DWSkT1vCerXmFDFThvkW8Kx3WULq/the_lean_startup_book_review.jpg)

The Lean Startup é um livro escrito por Eric Ries, que se propõe através de 3 Partes (Visão, Direção e Aceleração) que é a forma em que o livro é divido, em passar o conhecimento de como uma startup deve ser administrada para o leitor.

É bem curioso a forma como me deparei com esse livro. Um dia desses apareceu uma recomendação de vídeo curto, em que o apresentador comentou de alguns livros que eu já tinha lido e os colocou em ranks abaixo desse livro chamado \

, o que me deixou curioso para saber se realmente seria um livro tão interessante mesmo.\n\nAcabei procurando pelo livro em algumas lojas e notei que os feedbacks do livro eram bem positivos e como o assunto parecia ser bem interessante resolvi dar uma chance ao livro. Talvez você possa pensar que esse livro não é para você já que fala sobre startup, mas de acordo com a própria definição do autor Eric Ries \

. No mundo atual, com inovações acontecendo à todo momento, chances de pandemia, guerras, mudanças no comércio global, podemos chegar á uma conclusão estamos em um cenário de incerteza extrema, que é justamente as condições que a startup tem que lidar. O livro traz o método de lean startup para ajudar os empreendedores à ter sucesso em meio à incerteza constante. Assim, mesmo que você não seja uma startup, os conceitos do livro podem servir para você sobreviver ao cenário de incerteza. Um exemplo para mostrar como tudo muda tão rápido, é que todo ano as empresas de tecnologia fazem uma reunião para compartilhar as novidades que estão por vir, os governos fazem acordos com outros países, guerras surgem de forma inesperada. Nesse cenário, quanto mais você aprender à sobreviver e ter uma empresa sustentável melhor será para você. Fico agradecido se você puder dar um **Voto**, **Reblogs** ou algum **Tips**. Obrigado e boa leitura! 🍀 ---

>

## The Lean Startup - Short Book Review

<center> ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSKoAbzjvCRuuJWtBmTkhYuFYui1dFNCAsjb4mMjSWD5L/image.png) </center>
<center>Author: Eric Ries</center>

No começo do livro tem um tópico de título \
que dá uma visão geral do conteúdo de cada uma dessas partes. O primeiro tópico do livro que é \

é mais introdutório e o autor compartilha algumas histórias e dá algumas definições, como quem seria um empreendedor, o que seria uma startup e um conceito fundamental que é o de aprendizagem validada, que ele mesmo aprendeu graças à um fracasso em um de seus empreendimentos.\n\nO segundo é chamado \

, em que o autor parte para o método de startup enxuta em si, abordando o ciclo de feedback construir-medir-aprender, algo que é bem utilizado em negócio que trabalham com o público, em que o feedback acaba moldando o produto final.\n\nPor fim, o último tópico é o de \

, que é como o nome sugere, simplesmente executar o ciclo de feedback apresentado anteriormente no capítulo de Direção, mas de forma mais rápida. A diferença é que nessa etapa, além de realizar essa tarefa, ao mesmo tempo estará em processo de expansão. Eu ainda estou no início do livro e até então, o que eu tenho de feedback é da primeira parte do livro. O que eu gostei até o momento é que tem boas definições e alguns insights que dá para ser retirado. O problema é que grande parte vem do autor contando a sua própria história, o que acaba deixando bem cansativo esse início pelo menos. Me lembro de que em um outro livro isso já foi um problema muito grande para outras pessoas quando o autor começa a contar muitas histórias e não vai direto ao assunto. Acho que falou um passo a passo mais explícito e simples, acho que uma mistura do autor explicando os conceitos em uma página e depois contando de forma a dar um exemplo seria mais interessante. ---

title.title: Dnešní den
title.body:
Ráno jsem vstal později, oběd vařil brácha a dřív si nic nepamatuji.

S Martičkou jsme měli spicha, déle plánovaného, před její cestou do světa.

Bude dva roky pryč, užili jsme, nejdřív jsem hrál pár z těch skladbiček, které si troufám hrát, pak jsme šli s psiskem Na Růžek, zrovna byla Májka, potkal jsem Jirku Blábolila od kterého mám akordeon.

Odpoledne jsem psal s mamkou něco, co jsem nakousnul v pár minulých poustech, aby to bylo korektní a vědecky přijímané, bude to chtít odborné vedení, které moje máma umí.

Bude to pěkné.

Večer jsme s tátou rozehráli ještě velice zajímavou partii, kterou táta zaslouženě vyhrál, hrál poprvé \

, na mojí žádost, po výměně dam vyrazil s králem dopředu, na šachách nás kdysi učili, že v koncovce bez dam má centralizovaný král sílu věže, ještě se mu povedlo protlačit pěšce přes černá pole s našimi černopolnými střelci a pěšec v proměně matil.

Já jsem zradil bělošskou zásadu hrát vždycky na výhru (myslel jsem, že směřujeme k remíze) a nakonec jsem to projel.

Z hudební teorie se mi točí hlava, obzvlášť když se pouštím do těch úvah, že to mění vesmír, je mi těžko od hlavy a myslím, že se i bojím.

Doufám, že nedělám něco zlého...

Martičce jsem představoval Keithe Jarretta, Bacha (toho velkého) a maličké Kotykoviny.

Sára už je pryč sedm let...

Nikdy nevím, kolik jsem toho mohl zničit a kolik jsem toho zničil, prostě nevím.

Zkusím se hecnout a kromě pár knížek o harmonickém dualismu, které kvůli práci snad aspoň nakousnu se prokoušu zase aspoň dvěma stránkami té její Svaté.

Dělala ji kvůli mně?

Nevím.

Proč nevím? Nevěřím si?

Strach jsem měl vždycky jenom z výšek, ale už to kromě těch, z kterých se padá jsou i výšky tónové a vysoké školy.

Do toho jsem snad alespoň chtěl, aby nějaký teoretik (třeba ze školy) zkusil opravdu studovat, co jsem to udělal za nadělení.

Kdyby se řešilo co dělám nejen medicínsky, ale třeba taková Oplištilová nebo Štochl studovali moje skladby ve vztahu k mému prožívání a tomu, co se tu reálně děje se světem, mohl bych být o něco dál, než v koupeli samoty a bezmoci.

Učím se zvuky krájet, je to zlé?

Učím se funkce kombinovat, tak aby vyzněly víceznačně. Je to zlé?

Učím se polarizovat, učím se užívat, učím se utopit, učím se za se knout a ulevit si, najít v konstrukci chvíli, alespoň malou pro trochu štěstí....

Ano: Zde je ten problém: Vykonstruovat štěstí je násilná myšlenka, ale když jsem se to učil uvažovat ve společnosti, nejlíp z toho vyšla svoboda pro každého...

Mé světlé závěry, ke kterým všechno spěje, jsou v úvaze o skladbě na začátku.

Problém?

Ano, čím chce matematická duše žít větším, než jsou problémy a čím může být uspokojená více, než odpovědí v hudbě, světem, tak niterně navázaným na prožívání, že už snad nikdo nebude vědět líp, než skladatel, co je to taková opravdová trojka.

Sprosté?

A nevzalo se i toto slovo od prostoty?

Mnoho podnětů často bolí a dnes nemám skladbu pro Martičku, zkusím se ještě zasnít do světa, kde tercie neznačí celý akord, ale napovídá vztah dvou.

Dvou tónů a dvou potenciálních akordů, do kterých by šly oba tóny zasadit.

Snad proto mám nejraději dvojhlasy, nejvíc si toho umím s lidmi říct, když nepřekáží třetí osoba.

I v řeči, málokdy se bavím o někom třetím, než o mně a té druhé osobě, která je se mnou.

Učili jsme se na náboženství, že o druhých nemáme příliš mluvit o jeho zlých stránkách, když to není za účelem mu pomoci, alespoň modlitbou, nebo další komunikace s ním, třetím.

Ale pater řekl jasně, že pomluva je, až když lžeme, jinak jde o lehčí hřích nactiutrhání, jméno by měl mít každý ale tak důstojné, jak si zasluhuje, nemusíme nutně chránit idioty.

Dvojhlas v sobě nese mnoho toho, co je v hudbě ještě nevyčerpané, dvojhlas ještě není akord a nemá tím pádem jednu jasnou funkci, často i složité harmonie dělím na dílčí dvojhlasy, abych porozuměl jejich tenzím. Trojzvuk ve čtyřhlasé úpravě patří minulosti, v které se tahu kvintakordů podařilo dosáhnout maximální účisnnosti.

Trvalo to od sedmnáctého do konce devatenáctého století.

Dvojhlas má ale skromnou tradici, jednou z nejkrásnějších dvojhlasých skladeb je lidovka Javorina, chlapci, javorina, kde se v tercii obrátí citlivý tón na druhou stranu a rozvede se ze čtvrtého na třetí stupeň, osmému se tedy vyhne.

Je krásná!

A takové očíčka, o kterých se v ní zpívá, mývám já, když si sundám brýle, které to maskují.

Modré pod očima má možná i Sára, jednou jsem viděl fotku, tuším z předloňského roku, kde to modré je.

To je z bezesných nocí, je to jako když máte monokly.

Zkusím Martičce ještě nějaký dvojhlas po dnešku napsat, líbila se jí ta věnovaná Xeně k narozeninám, ta je zrovna taková krásná v těchhle věcech ohledně tónové polarity, centrum na a, na kterém to nakonec skončí, značí v tématu jen jedna doba, ta třetí, lehká, F dur je potom jasně subdominantní, ale nevíme, jestli k c nebo k a, další akordy respektují oba směry.

Vždyť jejda, kde se bere v lidech tolik humoru, nejvíc je ho vždycky tam, kde se něco pochopí jinak, kde je dvojsmysl, kde je vyloupnutí jiného významu, než se myslel prve. Tam se berou zvraty. Tam se bere sranda a v muzice je krásné, když tohle třeba ve dvojhlasu člověk udělá, že to může být až dojemné.

Jako v té písni, Javorina, jsem nerozvedl citlivý tón v několika skladbách, vždycky to působilo dojemně, jak je upřené to, co se v hudbě nejčastěji prostě musí, podle klasickkých pravidel-

Zkusím udělat jednu maličkou a půjdu spát, zítra se uvidíme ještě v kostelíku, bude čas na věnování.

In Zig, you can call fork directly through `std.posix.fork`:

```zig
const std = @import(\

Zig's `std.process.Child` wraps the fork/exec/wait pattern into a cleaner API. We used it in the shell episodes, but lets really dig into what it offers:

```zig
const std = @import(\

, .{result.stdout});
}
```

The `stdout_behavior` and `stderr_behavior` fields control how the child's output streams are handled. `.Pipe` creates a pipe that the parent can read from. `.Inherit` passes the parent's stdout/stderr directly to the child (useful when you want the child's output to appear on the terminal). `.Ignore` discards the output entirely. Under the hood, `.Pipe` sets up a Unix pipe via the `pipe2` syscall, the child's stdout file descriptor gets redirected to the write end, and the parent reads from the read end.

The `captureOutput` function shows how to read both stdout and stderr. There's a subtlety here though -- if you read stdout to completion before reading stderr, and the child writes a lot to stderr, the pipe buffer can fill up and the child will block waiting for someone to read stderr. In production code you'd want to read both streams concurrently (using threads or poll/epoll). For small outputs it doesn't matter, but for processes that produce megabytes on both streams, you need to be careful.

Having said that, for most practical uses where you just want to run a command and grab its output, `std.process.Child` does exactly what you need without having to manually fork, exec, set up pipes, and waitpid.

## Environment variables: reading, setting, passing to children

Every Unix process inherits a copy of its parent's environment variables. These are key-value string pairs that configure behavior without command-line arguments. Zig's standard library provides `std.posix.getenv` for reading and `std.process.Child` has an `env_map` field for passing a custom environment to child processes:

```zig
const std = @import(\

. The shell uses exit code 128+N to indicate a process killed by signal N (so SIGKILL/9 becomes exit code 137). But these are conventions, not enforced by the kernel.\n\nSignal-based termination is fundamentally different from normal exit. SIGTERM (15) is the polite \
signal -- processes can catch it and do cleanup. SIGKILL (9) is the unconditional \

signal -- the kernel terminates the process immediately, no cleanup possible. SIGSEGV (11) means the process tried to access invalid memory. SIGPIPE (13) means it wrote to a broken pipe. Understanding what signal killed your child tells you a lot about what went wrong.

The `WCOREDUMP` flag tells you whether the killed process produced a core dump file. Core dumps are memory snapshots that you can load into a debugger to examine what the process was doing when it crashed. On most modern Linux systems, core dumps are handled by `systemd-coredump` rather than being written as files directly.

## Process groups and sessions

Processes don't exist in isolation -- they're organized into process groups and sessions. A process group is a collection of related processes (like a pipeline `cat foo | grep bar | wc -l`). A session is a collection of process groups tied to a controlling terminal. This hierarchy is how the kernel knows which processes to signal when you press Ctrl+C or close a terminal:

```zig

, not a specific PID.

Zombies aren't dangerous in small numbers, but they can accumulate. Each zombie takes up a slot in the kernel's process table. If you hit the system-wide process limit (typically 32768 or higher on Linux), no new processes can be created. Server programs that fork workers need to reap children promptly. The common patterns are: a SIGCHLD signal handler that calls waitpid, a dedicated reaper thread, or periodic non-blocking polls like the code above.

There's a neat trick on Linux: setting the SIGCHLD handler to `SIG_IGN` tells the kernel to automatically reap children without creating zombies at all. But then you can't get their exit status, which defeats the purpose if you care about whether the child succeeded.

## The double-fork trick for daemonization

A daemon is a background process that runs independently of any terminal. Creating one properly requires a specific sequence of fork, setsid, and fork again. The double-fork trick ensures the daemon can't accidentally reacquire a controlling terminal:

```zig
const std = @import(\

, .{});
}
```

The supervisor manages a list of `SupervisedProcess` entries. For each one, it tracks the PID (if running), restart count, and maximum allowed restarts. The main loop calls `checkChildren` which does non-blocking waitpid to detect exited children. When a child exits, the supervisor automatically restarts it unless it's exceeded the restart limit.

The restart cooldown is important -- without it, a process that crashes immediately (bad binary, missing config file, port already in use) would restart thousands of times per second, eating CPU and filling logs. The code checks how long the process ran and forces a 1-second delay if it crashed in under a second. Real supervisors like systemd have configurable backoff strategies (exponential backoff, max restart frequency windows, etc.).

The `stopAll` function demonstrates graceful shutdown: first send SIGTERM (polite), wait up to 5 seconds, then SIGKILL (forceful) any processes that didn't exit. This two-phase approach is standard practice -- it gives well-behaved processes time to flush buffers, close connections, and clean up, while still guaranteeing that misbehaving processes eventually die.

## Exercises

1. Add a health check to the `Supervisor`. Each `SupervisedProcess` should have an optional `health_check_command` (another command string). Every 5 seconds, the supervisor should run the health check command for each running process. If the health check exits with a non-zero code, the supervisor should consider the process unhealthy and restart it (even though the main process hasn't exited). Test with a process that runs but becomes \

(e.g., a shell script that creates a file on start and the health check verifies the file exists -- delete the file manually to trigger the restart).

2. Write a process pool that maintains exactly N worker processes. When any worker exits, a new one is spawned immediately to keep the count at N. Each worker should receive a unique worker ID via environment variable (`WORKER_ID=0`, `WORKER_ID=1`, etc.). Write a test that verifies the pool maintains the correct count after killing workers with SIGKILL.

3. Implement a simple pipe executor that connects two processes via a Unix pipe -- the stdout of process A becomes the stdin of process B (like `cmd1 | cmd2` in a shell). Use `std.posix.pipe` to create the pipe, fork twice, and set up file descriptor redirection with `std.posix.dup2` in each child before exec. Test with `echo \

| wc -w` and verify the output is `2`.

## Wat we geleerd hebben

- The Unix process model has exactly three steps: `fork` copies the current process, `exec` replaces the copy with a new program, `wait` collects the result -- every shell command, every server worker, every daemon uses this pattern
- `std.process.Child` wraps fork/exec/wait into a clean API with configurable stdout/stderr piping, but understanding the syscalls underneath matters when you need fine-grained control
- Environment variables are inherited by default but can be replaced entirely via `env_map` -- an important security boundary when running untrusted child processes
- Exit codes are 8-bit (0-255) and signal-based deaths produce a different wait status -- the `W.IFEXITED`/`W.IFSIGNALED` macros decode which type of termination occured
- Process groups receive signals together (Ctrl+C sends SIGINT to the whole foreground group), and sessions tie process groups to a controlling terminal
- Zombie processes are children that exited but weren't waited on -- they consume process table slots and accumulate if the parent forgets to call `waitpid`
- The double-fork trick creates a proper daemon: fork, setsid (new session, no terminal), fork again (lose session leader status), close/redirect stdio, and change to root directory
- A process supervisor combines all these concepts: spawn children, reap them on exit, restart with cooldown, health checks, and graceful shutdown with SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL

Process management is one of those areas where you're directly interfacing with the kernel. Every concept here -- fork, exec, waitpid, signals, process groups, sessions -- maps directly to syscalls. No abstraction layers, no runtime overhead. Zig makes this natural because it doesn't try to hide the OS from you.

The concepts from today feed directly into what's coming next. We've been dealing with processes as separate entities that communicate through exit codes and signals. But processes can also talk to each other through pipes, shared memory, and other IPC mechanisms -- and that's where things get really interesting.

De groeten!

body.title: PSG Edge Arsenal in Thrilling Champions League Final
body.body:
PSG Beat Arsenal on Penalties to Retain Champions League Crown

Paris Saint-Germain have successfully defended their UEFA Champions League title after defeating Arsenal 4-3 on penalties following a dramatic 1-1 draw at the Puskás Aréna in Budapest.

The final started perfectly for Arsenal, who stunned the French champions with an early goal from Kai Havertz in the 6th minute. After a defensive mistake from PSG, Havertz reacted quickly and fired a powerful finish past goalkeeper Matvey Safonov to give the Gunners an early advantage.

Arsenal looked organized and disciplined throughout the first half, frustrating PSG’s dangerous attacking trio of Ousmane Dembélé, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, and Désiré Doué. Mikel Arteta’s side carried their 1-0 lead into halftime and appeared on course for a historic European triumph.

However, PSG responded in the second half. Their pressure finally paid off in the 65th minute when Ousmane Dembélé converted a penalty after a foul inside the box. The goal shifted momentum towards the French side as they pushed aggressively for a winner.

Both teams created chances during the closing stages of normal time and extra time, but neither could find the decisive goal. Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya produced important saves, while PSG also defended strongly under pressure.

With the score locked at 1-1 after 120 minutes, the Champions League final was decided by a penalty shootout. PSG held their nerve from the spot, converting four penalties, while Arsenal missed crucial opportunities. Gabriel’s miss proved costly as the French champions secured a 4-3 shootout victory.

The result means PSG have now won back-to-back Champions League titles, further cementing their place among Europe’s elite clubs. For Arsenal, the defeat is heartbreaking as they miss out on what would have been their first-ever Champions League trophy despite an outstanding season.

Although Arsenal leave Budapest without the trophy, their journey to the final and Premier League success this season show that the club has firmly re-established itself among Europe’s top teams.

Final Score:
PSG 1-1 Arsenal (PSG win 4-3 on penalties)

Goals:
• Kai Havertz (6') – Arsenal
• Ousmane Dembélé (65' Penalty) – PSG

Man of the Match:
Ousmane Dembélé – Scored the equalizer and played a key role in PSG's title-winning performance.

body.title: The Tale of Dane - ENG- SPA
body.body: > By fate, luck, or chance, Dane was born in a country that was highly repressive regarding one thing in particular: music. In this country, music was prohibited for several reasons, including its status as a form of free expression. Therefore, it was persecuted, and no one was allowed to sing, whether professionally or even casually. Singing in public was considered insurrection and a form of protest, resulting in all kinds of punishments, including imprisonment. For this reason, there were no parties with music or street musicians, as one might see in other countries. Only a select few were allowed to make music; they were chosen. These individuals had to assure the authorities that the sole purpose of their music was to entertain the people and not to profit from it. And if, for any reason, they became famous in the country for their music, they had to stop performing and accept retirement to avoid attracting attention. Into this bleak landscape was born Dane. He was a very special child because he was born with musical talent running through his veins, and this would sooner or later become a major problem for him. As he grew up, he learned to sing online. He saw on social media how great singers from abroad were building successful careers and achieving their dreams, but despite his talent, he couldn't achieve anything due to his circumstances. He felt a great envy of being able to do the same, but there was nothing he could do at that time.

> Por cosas del destino, de la suerte o de la casualidad a Dane le tocó nacer en un país muy represivo con una cosa en particular, la música. En este país la música estaba prohibida por varias causas, entre ellas que era una forma de libre expresión, por eso era perseguida y no se dejaba cantar a nadie de forma profesional o hasta casual. El que cantara en público se consideraba insurrección y forma de protesta, por eso habían castigos de todo tipo, incluida la prisión. Por esta razón en el país no existían las fiestas con música, o los músicos callejeros como se puede ver en cualquier país. Solo se le permitía hacer música a un número reducido de personas, ellos eran los elegidos, estas personas debían asegurar a las autoridades que el único objetivo de su música era entretener al pueblo y no sacar crédito económico de ella. Y si por alguna razón se hacía famoso en el país por esta música tenía que dejar de hacerla y aceptar retirarse para dejar de llamar la atención. En este panorama tan desolador nació Dane, el era un niño muy especial porque nació con el talento de la música corriendo por sus venas y esto más temprano que tarde sería un gran problema para él. A medida que fue creciendo el fue aprendiendo por internet a cantar. Veía en las redes sociales a los grandes cantantes del exterior del país llevar carreras exitosas y conseguir sus sueños, pero él a pensar de tener talento no podía conseguir nada, por culpa de las circunstancias. Sentía mucha envida de poder hacer lo mismo, pero no había nada que pudiera hacer en ese momento.
![horserat-Ln62QBYis8c-unsplash.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nelsoncu/23vsL1kwqn3QgtEbi1LrYWtGgUE8PcnArXGAb7RBX9Ukrwa1dUhBDbjau68qip4BgPoFn.jpg) ...Free image from Pixabay...

> At home, he would sing with the doors and windows closed; it was the only place where he could truly sing. He would let it all out by singing at the top of his lungs. His parents told him to sing more quietly because someone might hear him and get them all in trouble. This upset him greatly because even at home he couldn't sing with all the power he felt inside. He could sing, but softly, and without any emotion. He spent his entire youth and part of his adulthood like this: shut away, yearning, longing for something unattainable. Upon reaching adulthood, he understood that he couldn't live like this forever. He couldn't simply die without having done anything to achieve what he loved. He couldn't imagine disappearing, letting others decide what he should love and do. For this reason, he devised a plan to leave the country. But carrying out this plan would be very expensive. It involved leaving the country and moving to a less restrictive place. The problem was that he needed a lot of money to buy plane tickets.

> En su casa el cantaba con las puertas y ventanas cerradas, era el único lugar donde de verdad podía cantar. Se desahogaba cantando a todo pulmón. Sus padres le decían que cantara más bajo pues alguien podía escucharlo y meterlos en problemas a todos. Esto lo ponía muy mal, porque ni siquiera en su casa podía cantar con toda la fuerza que tenía por dentro. Podía cantar pero bajo, y sin emoción alguna. Así pasó toda su juventud y parte de su adultez. Encerrado, añorando, deseando algo que no se podía ser. Al llegar a la parte adulta de su vida el comprendió que no podía vivir así para siempre, no podía simplemente morir y no haber hecho nada por conseguir lo que amaba. No concebía en su mente desaparecer y ya, dejando que otros decidan lo que debes amar y hacer. Por esta razón ideo un plan para salir del país. Pero llevar a cabo ese plan sería muy costoso, consistía en salir del país y mudarse a otro sitio menos restrictivo. El problema se necesitaba mucho dinero para poder comprar los pasajes de avión.
![you-le-W7KBvEmCXRM-unsplash.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nelsoncu/23zkte598D79NeNXFvo56KCLx6sGGwyC4GFgxVi3Xr1UzEopvwbwGVQq27dwKTWJJfWdV.jpg) ...Free image from Pixabay...

> That's why he would have to keep waiting, remaining silent, not letting his inner self, his music, out. He had to save for several years, often forgoing basic necessities, so that one day he could have what now lacked life. Every sacrifice, every hour of work, would be worth it, because although it took time, he was finally able to buy a plane ticket and leave the country. When he left the country and arrived in his new one, he immediately began preparing to sing. Within days, he had started, first as a street musician, then as a musician in bars and entertainment venues, and finally as a professional singer. It was a long and very sad road to get here, but he made it. He deeply regrets that in his home country, it's still not possible to be a singer. He hopes that one day things will change and others will also be able to fulfill their dreams, while he sings for himself and for those who cannot.

> Por eso tendría que seguir esperando, manteniéndose callado, sin dejar salir su yo interior, su música. Tuvo que ahorrar unos cuantos años, a menudo dejando de comprar cosas básicas para la vida, con tal de poder algún día tener lo que ahora no tenía vida. Cada sacrificio, cada hora de trabajo, valdría la pena, porque aunque tardó por fin pudo comprar un vuelo y marcharse del país. Cuando salió del país y llegó al nuevo de inmediato se puso a preparase para cantar. En unos días ya había empezado, primero como músico callejero, después como músico en bares y lugares de recreación y finalmente como un cantante profesional. Fue un largo y muy triste camino hasta aquí, pero lo logró. Lamenta mucho que en su país de origen aún no se pueda ser cantante, desea que algún día las cosas cambien y los demás también puedan cumplir sus sueños, mientas el cantará por él y por los que no pueden.
![cord-allman-M9xgEB6Gjm4-unsplash.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nelsoncu/23tbPF7cf8cZv4ZF2HnmTYagbdTm76iUyCUv6jQa31XXafkpyyPJ6SLamVdtuiV8JK2ZL.jpg) ...Free image from Pixabay...

> This post is completely original and my own. No programs have been used to edit the text or correct the grammar. I wrote it exactly as you read it. The English version was translated using Google Translate. Esta publicación es completamente original, y de mi autoría. NO se han usado programas para modificar el texto o para reparar la gramática. Tal cual lo lees así lo escribí. La versión en ingles fue traducida usando Google traductor.
