body.title: Mushrooms after heavy rains.
body.body:
Mushrooms after heavy rains.
It's been raining almost every day here lately. It's windy, and the wind whips up black clouds, then it rains. For example, today there was a strong wind, then the sky became covered with dark blue clouds. A thunderstorm began, followed by heavy rain.
Because it rains so much, mushrooms have appeared. 🍄 Mushrooms 🍄‍🟫 usually begin to grow after rains, especially in the fall. But even in the spring, after heavy rains, the ground gets thoroughly soaked, the mycelium gets wet, and the mushrooms begin to grow.
We were on a walk, exploring nature. We were just strolling, enjoying the wonderful air after the rain. Then I saw mushrooms. I don't know the name of this mushroom. Or rather, I forgot it. It's probably not edible.
I love mushroom picking. I like the taste of wild mushrooms.
Wild mushrooms are delicious fried, and they're also delicious canned. My favorite is the porcini mushroom. It's a type of mushroom that often grows in the forest. But this is a different variety, the one in the photo. I think it's delicious. We didn't go far in the meadow, nor did we go into the forest. But we could have gone and seen if there were any mushroom patches. It's a great time to pick mushrooms now, after the rain.

But it's best to pick mushrooms with people who know about them. For example, I don't know much about mushrooms. If you don't know which mushrooms to pick, you might find poisonous ones, which, of course, you shouldn't eat. It's best to take friends who know mushrooms well on a mushroom hunt.

But still, if you've picked mushrooms, it's best to boil them in a saucepan with an onion. Then drain the water and fry them in a frying pan.

Mushrooms also give a nice after-rainy feeling. Everything smells fresh after the rain, and mushrooms still smell fresh. It's especially nice in the forest. After the rain, it's fresh and perfect for picking lots of mushrooms.

body.body: it's springtime here so it's a great time to see baby birds. the most easily spotted ones for us are ones swimming in the water, such as these charming mallard ducklings. the city of Fredrikstad in Norway is located on the largest river in Norway, the Glomma River. the city includes several islands which divide the river making for sections with less current than the main section. the areas with greatly reduced current are ideal for mallards so they are plentiful here. i took these shots of the ducklings with their mother from a low wooden bridge that connected one of the smaller islands to the mainland. when we were on the bridge they happened to swim under it, giving me the opportunity to get these shots from above at a close distance yet without disturbing them in any way.\n\n

/>\n\nthis particular mother mallard was very dark with a white breast indicating that she is likely a wild/domestic hybrid. her brood of ducklings was darker than the other ones we observed. most of the other females we saw had the typical wild mallard mottled brown appearance. likewise for the males, most had the typical wild pigmentation.

We are created to glorify God, and also reflect His good image to the people around us in this world. Scripture shows that we are placed here not only for personal salvation but also to serve, care for others, and spread goodness in the world. body.body:
![ad.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aubryd/23wMTzEUDqukUqSkUrnDHLnAJdY8UyuQrPhaVo8Jo5M4QBmtxcqBS3gqKEiSnYpZZJTxs.png)

Hello everyone, have a nice day and good battles. After many difficult battles in this season, I finally managed to reach a rating of 4300 in the modern ranked format, which means I made it to the Champion I league. Thanks to this, I got a lot free loot chests: 15 minor, 15 major and 6 ultimate chests.

Unfortunately, this time I had very bad luck, I would say. I didn't get any legendary, epic or even a single gold card in all these loot chests. Well, at least I got a lot of common cards, 2 rare cards, 8 legendary potions and 5 alchemy potions. In addition, I also got 4 common scrolls and exactly 3826 merits. And finally, 9 energy and 13 entries for the weekly fortune draw.
<center>![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aubryd/23u5tauaaEETzuFKutWbvnKE8zeDpQSQTL6cA8EY8uroEHBXDHVDDDRUXCPzuF2iDV5WH.png)

Now, I only need two more copies of the avian, Thornmaw Berseker, so that it can reach level 10 (max), where it will learn the Charge ability, which allows it to attack from any position.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aubryd/23tRviy6Aj9qwkjhPCRgw2DNpUubhxwxmBq3TwSp2Vbgcjn6gPfAa8vDB6dSnnxYQukcF.png)

---

And my undead, Cullborn Revenant also needs two more copies so it can reach the max level, where she will learn the Spite ability, so that when she is defeated, she will perform an attack against the unit that defeats her.

---

Currently, I only have the avian, Ironwing Juggernaut at the max level. And all my other common conclave arcana reward cards are at level 9. It's very probably that next season many, if not all, will reach level 10. I hope to get some gold cards in my loot chests next time, and I wish you the same. Have fun playing.

Are you not playing Splinterlands yet? You can join with my [referral link](https://splinterlands.com/register?ref=langice) and I will give you 600 DEC when you buy the spellbook.

body.title: SPS Delegations & Purchasing Some MAX Cards
body.body:
/>
\-------------------- \## SPS Delegation One of the aspects of earning with Splinterlands that I don't see many posts about is the fact players can earn through delegating our Staked SPS tokens. Before we go any further lets define what delegation is. The mechanics of delegation ensure that an owner of an asset retain full custody of their loaned assets. Meaning your private keys and crypto remain securely in your wallet. The Hive Blockchain utilizes such a feature with the chains main token known as the Hive Token (can be found in the wallet section). Splinterlands has multiple examples of utilizing delegation. The rental system comes to mind. Players can rent cards from different owners of said cards without a single card ever moving from anyone's wallet. The same is true for SPS. The Splinterlands team has built a dedicated SPS delegation market directly on the official Splinterlands site. Directly below this paragraph will be a screenshot of such. As seen in that screenshot the BID section is showing a return value of 2.93% while the BUY section is showing a return of 5.87% for delegated SPS. How quickly do these bids fill? To that I will say it all depends on what choice you make. If you are willing to delegate your SPS for 2.93% all you need to do is set an offer that requests just that. If there is a BID available your offer will almost instantly fill. Doing such is my action of choice when delegating. You can OFFER delegation for a higher percentage and wait to see if someone comes along to pick it up. To get to the correct section log in to Splinterlands > Click the SPS icon (top of page) > You are now in the SPS wallet section > Scroll to and click the MANAGE link within your SPS wallet > BAM you are now in the right place. Toggle the options to get to the template section you wish to utilize. OUTGOING shows your current active delegations. INCOMING shows active delegations you purchased. MARKET is where you see the order book (this is where you place bids or create an offer). MY RENTALS shows current and past rentals. \-------------------

/>
\------------------------ \## Maxing Some Cards Every so often I go through my collection and upgrade some cards. Here today we will be doing that. I grown found of the Foundation League so lets take a look at what cards I have that are near MAX. I do heavily focus on GOLD but I also like to MAX regular foils as well (lets take a look at those first). Looking at my collection I determined that I don't have any cards known as Agniavan Salamander which is a Legendary fire 8 mana card. It's Gold version is currently listed at the low price of $1.59 USD. It's regular foil version (level 2) is currently listed at the very affordable price of $0.09 USD. Today we will be picking up the regular foil version. Level 2 is the MAX for Legendary cards in the Frontier mode. Purchases can be made using Paypal or DEC. I decided to utilize the CREDITS I have. The total cost for this card was just 90 CREDITS. Lets check the Epics next. Looks like I don't have any Echelon cards which is an Epic Fire with the mana cost of 4. This one caught my eye because there is only two MAX copies on the market for sale. The first being available for $0.10 USD (reg foil). The second being valued at $0.38 USD. Now that we picked up a MAX Legendary and a MAX Epic it's now time to look at the Rare cards. As all good warriors within the Splinterverse know its always best to MAX our ARCHONS first. This time we will look at our GOLD Death Archon known as Thalgrimore. We already own two level 2's (min level for Rare Gold cards). That means we have to purchase two more gold variants of this card (Done and Done). We paid roughly $0.25 for each card using credits bringing our total cost of both purchases to 500 CREDITS (50 cents). As I make that purchase I realize that I actually do already have one MAXED. No biggie - I'm happy to have the extra cards. I also don't have a MAX Scales of Justice (GOLD) which is a RARE Unit. I see one listed for the low price of $0.10 so I'll add it to the collection. Moving on to the COMMON cards. I notice one of my favorite commons to utilize in battle isn't MAXED. This won't do -- lets max the card known as New Beluroc Aegis. The cost was just 120 CREDITS for the Gold variant. \-------------------

/>
\---------------- \### That's it for now Our Splinterland purchases for the day has concluded. Over-all we are happy with the purchases we made here today. Although we did make a slight blunder with purchasing a card we already had maxed. We still have a few thousand CREDITS left in our wallet so our purchasing/ combining and window shopping aren't done yet. We are simply just done for the day. CREDITS can be purchased on the Splinterlands site using Paypal. Simply log in to the main Splinterlands site > click the CREDITS icon and you'll be in the right section. It really is that easy, just point and click (always check your values to make sure you entered them correctly and never click links from unverified sources). As always we here at the @rentmoney blog thank you for visiting us and we hope to see you at our next post (you are appreciated). Upcoming Content: More Splinterlands content, More Gaming Content, re-re-entry into the poker world and much more. No financial advice was giving in this post or any other post created by the @rentmoney blog. All images have been sourced and are property of Splinterlands. \---------------------

body.title: WEEKEND EXPERIENCE: MY PERFECT SATURDAY 🌊💋💝
body.body:
Good day Weekend Experience family 💛
I’m @nc6 and this is how I spent my Saturday today. 
I started with morning self-care, then ate healthy fruit salad, rushed to market for Sunday stew, and ended with hot noodles + movie in bed. 

Healthy start, fresh body, busy middle, chill ending 😌 Join me 👇

   1. Morning Refresh: Brush + Bath Time 🪥🚿
My Saturday always starts with taking care of myself first. 
I brushed my teeth with Pepsodent, washed my face, then had a proper bath with my exfoliating gloves + soap. 

There’s something about Saturday morning baths that just resets my whole body and mind. Clean skin, fresh breath, ready for the day!

     
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfDHdj8sgeeDCYCXiV6XrmFhUSMAoALzXXSVDus6bbhfR/1780151860666.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPMYeN8Msi5YQKjn1avCBos3CeEtcY2p2MFebgRiV2V3T/1780151860712.jpg)


What’s your Saturday morning routine? Do you also start with self-care?

    2. Breakfast: Colorful Fruit Salad 🥗
After freshening up, I treated myself to fruit before going out. 
Banana, kiwi, grapes and pawpaw in one bowl. No sugar added, just natural sweetness to fuel my body. 

Eating fruit after my bath gives me energy for market stress later. Plus it’s so pretty to look at 😊


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVFe84GbBbvqGeF52sWkvLiAxRZNKsTCcQQwn8An4T7nB/1780151829179.jpg)


Team fruit or team heavy food for Saturday breakfast? Tell me!

     3. Market Run: Colors, Noise + Hustle 🛒
Now fresh and fed, it was time for serious business. Saturday market for Sunday stew ingredients! 

The place was full of life - red tomatoes, pepper, and everyone bargaining for Sunday. I love the energy even when it’s stressful 😂 



![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmR2EA9dww4W69KWbrCfpvd1DgrHNdEE3oBzgGYAuntr4j/1780151808199.jpg)


Saturday markets taught me patience again. But those colors make the hustle worth it.

  4. Afternoon Reward: Noodles + Movie in Bed 🍜🎬
After market + cleaning, I was tired but happy. I made spicy noodles with fish, grabbed my tray, and watched a movie right from my bed. 

This is my favorite part of Saturday night. Food + phone + comfort = perfect weekend ending. 



![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcbUv8v4KBn48uBtKxwpppwcmkJvGfwVgAYTyBNy2p85w/1780151761962.jpg)


Sometimes the best plans are no plans. Just food and rest.

     final Thoughts
Saturday for me = self-care, healthy food, market hustle, chill night. Balance is everything 😊

  l want to know:
How did you spend your Saturday? Market run like me, or pure rest? Drop your story in comments, I’ll reply everyone 👇

Thanks for spending part of your Saturday reading my day. 💚

>woke up with a headache and some neck ache.

This usually happens to me when I overthink before bed, and it causes muscle tension.

Always drink water before bed. Even mild dehydration can cause headaches. If you changed your pillow, it could be that too, and stress can generally cause this as well. De-stressing is important. You do so much for other people, don’t forget to look after yourself as well, as you are important too. :)

body.body:
Introduction


Hello everyone! This is @ybanezkim26 and I'll present today's edition of Travel Digest. In our featured posts, we have a church in Kwiaton, Poland, the city of Wroclaw, Poland, and a park in Bangkok, Thailand. Enjoy and keep on pinning your travel posts to the map!


All featured posts are visible on the Editors Choice Map and upvoted by @worldmappin, our curation trail, and potentially @blocktrades. For more travel digests check out #traveldigest.

Our winners today


🥇 UNESCO TREASURE HIDDEN IN THE MOUNTAINS by @ladytruckview

It was finally time to show you another church from Beskid Niski. Before going on this trip, I had not spent much time researching which churches were particularly worth visiting. In fact, I probably would never have seen this one, as it was not located anywhere along my planned route. However, while my friend and I were talking to a priest in Smerekowiec, he told us about a church in Kwiatoń that had been added to the UNESCO World Heritage List. I decided that even though it meant driving a few extra kilometers, it would definitely be worth visiting. In the end, I managed to see it literally at the last moment — just before leaving the area and just before sunset.

This post on Worldmappin - This user on Worldmappin



🥈 Wrocław - the city of bridges and the world of dwarfs in Poland by @dragan1957

Hi everyone. today I will write to you about a city in Poland, Wroclaw. I arrived in the city by plane from Sofia, it was a direct flight and Sofia is very close to me. The flight was about 35 minutes. We had a bus from the airport to the city center. Otherwise, we went in an organized manner, as always in our old society.I wasn't blown away by this trip, but I was really pleasantly surprised by the beauty of the city.Namely, the city extends over the Oder River and its 4 tributaries, more than 25 small islands, and has over 200 bridges.We started our tour of the city from the main square, Reinek. The square is very large and is where most of the tourist attractions are located.In order to photograph the panorama of the city and at the same time enjoy the view, one group went to the high tower and I climbed the stairs to the Cathedral of St. Mary Magdalene.The two towers are connected by a pedestrian bridge 45 meters above the ground, which offers panoramic views of the city. Legend has it that the bridge is haunted by the souls of women who preferred partying to housework, hence the name Bridge of Penitents.The photo shows the bridge, and there is also a bronze figure of dwarfs, which are the symbol of the city, so I wanted to see that too.

This post on Worldmappin - This user on Worldmappin



🥉 Parque Lumphini en Bangkok [ESP/ENG] by @evelynchacin

Hi everyone! One incredible place we absolutely loved in Bangkok (Thailand) was Lumphini Park. It’s a huge park with plenty to see and do—it’s the perfect spot to sit back and relax, enjoy the view or nature, or go for a run or a walk. Even the kids have a blast there, Believe me, Olivia really enjoyed the playground every day we were in Bangkok, so it’s a great place to visit as a family—but you’ll see for yourselves further down in this post.

body.title: Charity Edge - A saviour or Oppressor?
body.body:
Hello everyone,  

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma2vzkdZEAeBNeQPW3gwouM5UoRdNw3iNx5V3VzJm38q1/1780150329500.jpg)


I believe charity must begin at home because home is where love and responsibilities is required more.  
If extending charity to outsiders means neglecting your family, it is likely ignoring yourself.  
You may be seen as an enemy or a wicked person for not offering help to the people close to you. 

I heard a young woman saying that her father is so generous outside while they are barely holding up in the family. At first I doubted it. 

Until the mother said *\

.*

I know this man to be actively donating to different projects and was lauded for his selflessness. 
Yet to his daughter and spouse it was a lost trust and hope  despite his generosity outside. He was seen as an oppressor. The man may likely not be aware of how his family view him. 

 *One can be right to the world and wrong to the people close to them.*

This is where people get it all mixed up because they feel the applause and acknowledgement ranks highest and louder from the crowd than the small voice of true appreciation.

It is not right to neglect the people that are close while choosing to help people far away.
In the case of emergency or domestic accidents, it's more likely that the people at home are the ones who show up.

Yes, I know the people close by can be demanding and entitlement driven but the possibility of rescue and response is higher with them than strangers.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmU1aLMZPPXLwpBNWLLzdYw3RdyaqvvP9B2pLC2wYmv2B8/1780150352088.jpg)

*The charity planted at home is like a seed that takes root and grows into a giant tree that bears fruit you can reap from.*

It is a good thing to show charity outside, but you must build and enforce it in your home first.  
Because you will still go back home after the charity to outsiders. And home is where your presence and welcome are truly valued.

*Charity at home is not optional, it is responsibility.*

If you ignore it for outsiders, you are not paying careful attention to the conditions of the people close to you and the future. 

*Charity that begins at home is a race but charity outside is oftentimes a sprint.*

Well, at the end of the day, you get what you started at home. Charity applies to everyone irrespective of age, gender and level. Charity is learned and taught from the home like the children learning to be consistent in sharing toys and being friendly to other kids on the playground.

Extending charity to outsiders is not bad but should be balanced and thoughtful. 
Charity should not only be for the performance of an audience but to boost harmony and well-being of everyone whether close or far away.

body.title: A Riverside Weekend Lunch Filled with Family, Love, and Laughter
body.body:
***Weekends are always special for our family because they are the perfect time to pause from our busy schedules and spend meaningful moments together. After days filled with work, responsibilities, and stress, weekends become our chance to reconnect, relax, and enjoy each other’s company. This past weekend became even more memorable because we had the opportunity to spend it with our beloved balikbayan cousin, Kuya Auie, who recently came home from America. His visit brought excitement, joy, and warmth to the whole family, making our simple riverside lunch truly unforgettable.***

![1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/48mAU7qApCd8wdsrtxzrFerTi3xUmJBogHzZend2W2j25aUtEyky5YQrymRd4VHnpV.jpg)

Early in the morning, everyone was already busy preparing for our family gathering. The atmosphere inside the house was lively, with laughter and conversations filling every corner. Some were preparing the ingredients, while others were arranging the things we needed to bring to the riverside. Even before we left the house, the feeling of togetherness was already present. 

![2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/EpLeUXVfqY21y7bQLyMmVuHybHRRnTV3JoApPXr7kzixYYFzjVTQLKcLJCrcEE7UjX5.jpg)

***Moments like these remind me that happiness does not always come from expensive celebrations, but from simple bonding moments shared with the people we love the most.***

![4.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/EpLfWNt3n2PDHHaMcR1TNeEvrMd66ozuBRJZM7V6fhVNELnXbmMAMYwehLg38wNASBq.jpg)

When we finally arrived at the riverside, we were welcomed by the calming beauty of nature. The fresh air, the sound of the flowing water, and the peaceful surroundings instantly made us feel relaxed. The riverside was the perfect place for our family lunch because it let us enjoy both good food and beautiful scenery. The green trees dancing with the wind and the sparkling water created a peaceful environment that made our hearts feel light and happy.

![11.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/Ep7v9XMrnQdMAZANijRyGa5w8dQ5MQ1dHHwJ72xaC1DqBc5Qaos79S7LN81yZyNHcRA.jpg)

![17.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/23wgU4vo92bEpqvQGMPogkQUJDWQhCteQMCS3jYUFvBMaJu31g3maU6RhLpsGk6np854E.jpg)

Of course, no family gathering is complete without delicious food lovingly prepared. One of the highlights of our lunch was the flavorful roasted liempo. The crispy skin and juicy meat made everyone excited to eat. Its smoky aroma blended perfectly with the fresh air of the riverside, making every bite more satisfying. Beside the roasted liempo was a warm serving of papaitan, a dish loved by many in our family. Its rich flavor and comforting soup brought a sense of home and tradition, connecting us even more.

![15.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/23xVTP35ddvAq2moweqJCP8XxwQnsH3VyE1MtrPg3RuuKom56WrpTGw3k62dWZ7TzPFeQ.jpg)

What made our lunch extra special was our favorite sawsawan made from green mango, tomatoes, onions, and bagoong. The combination of sour, salty, and savory flavors perfectly complemented the roasted liempo and became everyone’s favorite dipping sauce. It may sound like a simple side dish, but for us Filipinos, sawsawan adds life and excitement to every meal. Watching everyone enjoy the food while sharing stories and laughter made the experience even more heartwarming.

![13.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/23xKvAAmzwsEJMrXq5W1HXge4469bGpjvdGn9Cvxi3Um3cWkd4SudSAfcBYaKJHruRVL5.jpg)

To complete our riverside feast, we also prepared fresh pakwan or watermelon. Under the warm afternoon sun, the cold, sweet watermelon slices made the perfect dessert. It refreshed everyone after enjoying the delicious meals. While eating the fresh fruit, we sat together on the riverside, sharing funny stories, childhood memories, and exciting experiences from Kuya Auie’s life in America. Listening to his stories reminded us how precious family connections are, no matter how far life takes us.

![14.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/23uQy6NDdKzU17tvSpfLxMfxu1uVJqpXvM7TjKPuRHbu7BP96UzgjNBNa1YYKLBbnEDor.jpg)

The most beautiful part of that day was not only the delicious food or the scenic riverside view, but the presence of family. Seeing everyone complete, smiling, and genuinely happy made my heart full. In today’s fast-paced world, spending quality time with loved ones has become rare, which is why moments like this should always be treasured. The laughter of my cousins, the endless conversations of the adults, and the simple joy of eating together created memories we will always remember.

![7.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/23tmFvMHmRwMUmDvDKcnhzj1RvP8pVKCj88U1JyrdqQK9KutBEUMnivzffsg3JX7gSfJU.jpg)

Kuya Auie’s visit also reminded us of the importance of coming home and reconnecting with family roots. Even though he has been living in America, the love and closeness within our family remained the same. Distance may separate family members physically, but love keeps everyone connected. His presence made our weekend lunch more meaningful because it became a celebration not only of food, but also of reunion, gratitude, and love.

![8.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/241tYuXxg2LTKwhRgjsGDMvuygEce77pZxLCQ4PJthdgeAK2vVMfbjwGMQDufd4VunZrM.jpg)

As the afternoon slowly came to an end, we spent our remaining time taking photos, enjoying the cool breeze, and appreciating the peaceful beauty around us. Before leaving the riverside, I quietly reflected on how blessed I am to have a family that values togetherness despite life’s challenges. The simple weekend lunch became a beautiful reminder that the greatest happiness in life comes from shared moments with the people closest to our hearts.

![9.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teacherlynlyn/23tviP5drLZZuuxkuYzYTzrUvTvuWfwcfy4QJWg6tFUpcGfpEmk7cFwFv4FUhvqfyEjxJ.jpg)

***Indeed, our riverside weekend lunch with family and our balikbayan cousin Kuya Auie was more than just a meal. It was a day filled with love, laughter, delicious food, and unforgettable memories. It reminded me that family gatherings, no matter how simple, are treasures that nourish not only our bodies but also our hearts and souls.***

body.title: Film Review: Drug War (2012)
body.body:
![(source:tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/lsxwefRtjGPp6euqxhfzko3r8sz.jpg)


Johnnie To enjoys a reputation as one of the most successful and internationally renowned Hong Kong filmmakers of the 21st century. Much of this esteem is owed to his skilful handling of the gangster genre, for which Hong Kong cinema was best known in past decades. With his 2012 film *Drug War*, however, he ventured slightly outside those well‑worn genre parameters, weaving together elements of police procedural, action thriller and, somewhat unusually, the road movie. This ambitious amalgamation results in a taut, brutal, and distinctly mainland Chinese crime epic that both honours and subverts the traditions of Hong Kong action cinema.

The film’s relocation to mainland China is a structural necessity for its road‑movie aspirations. Hong Kong’s cramped urban landscape offers little scope for the long, open roads that define the genre. Consequently, the plot is set in the industrial zones and highways around Tianjin, a major northern port. The narrative engine ignites when Timmy Choi (Louis Koo) crashes his car into a restaurant. Hospitalised, his plight coincides with a police crackdown on his drug‑mule operation. Captain Zhang (Sun Honglei) quickly deduces Choi is the survivor of a catastrophic meth‑lab explosion that killed his family. Facing China’s mandatory death penalty for drug manufacturing, Choi’s attempted flight from hospital fails, forcing him into a desperate bargain: he will betray his upstream partners—the flamboyant fishing magnate Bro Haha (Ping Hao) and the shadowy kingpin Uncle Bill (Zhenqi Li)—in exchange for his life. This sets in motion a complex series of undercover stings, with Zhang reluctantly posing first as Choi’s new partner and then as Haha himself. The procedural mechanics are meticulous, but To masterfully tightens the screws; two of Choi’s henchmen escape a police raid, and Choi’s own commitment to the deal begins to waver, seeding the dread that the entire operation is spiralling towards disaster.

*Drug War* is a profoundly unusual film, particularly for audiences accustomed to Hong Kong genre fare. Its status as a co‑production between Hong Kong and mainland studios necessitated, and surprisingly benefited from, a stark authenticity. The mainland authorities, it seems, did not object to the film’s unflinching portrayal of less‑than‑commendable realities: rampant drug crime, a desperate underclass willing to risk death by becoming “mules” with ingested drug capsules, and the sheer bureaucratic scale of the police response. This grants the film a gritty, almost documentary‑like texture that distinguishes it from the more stylised moral universes of To’s earlier works like [*Election*](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/retro-film-review-election-2005) or *PTU*. It is a film that acknowledges the People’s Republic not as a monolithic entity but as a vast, conflicted landscape where high‑tech policing battles entrenched, desperate criminal enterprise.

To and his cinematographer Cheng Siu‑keung make brilliant use of this northern Chinese setting. The open, often desolate spaces—framed under a pallid, cold sky—create a sense of bleak isolation that mirrors the characters’ moral desolation. This is not the neon‑drenched, rain‑slicked Hong Kong of noir tradition; it is a world of concrete, steel, and frost. Conversely, the film equally portrays modern China as a surveillance state where technology is a key battleground. The police, with their access to vast databases, omnipresent CCTV, and Zhang’s own dogged experience, consistently hold the upper hand in information warfare. This technological realism grounds the cat‑and‑mouse game, making the eventual unravelling not a failure of intelligence, but a tragic consequence of human unpredictability and violent chance.

And unravelling it does, with a ferocity that remains shocking. The film’s commitment to visceral realism is established early with grotesque, matter‑of‑fact scenes of drug mules being forced to defecate under police watch. It escalates in a central, unbearably tense sequence where Captain Zhang, to maintain his cover as Haha, must inject himself with methamphetamine, his salvation relying on the advice of the very man he is trying to convict. Yet this all serves as a prelude to the film’s devastating final act. The plot’s carefully constructed house of cards collapses into near‑Jacobean levels of bloodshed. In a prolonged, chaotic shootout at a primary school, allegiances shatter and bodies fall with ruthless impartiality. The violence is graphic, messy, and punctuated with startling details of bodily fluids and brutal physics.

This carnage sets the stage for one of modern cinema’s most chilling and memorable conclusions. The actual final scene returns to a cold, procedural silence. Choi, having survived the bloodbath only to be captured, is strapped to a gurney. In a desperate, futile bid to bargain, he spews names and dates as a prison official administers the lethal injection. His voice slows, slurs, and stops. It is a stark, unglamorous depiction of state execution, a rare and courageous ending for a gangster film that pointedly refuses any catharsis or redemption. The law, impersonal and absolute, has the final word.

For all its impressive power, *Drug War* is not a flawless film. Its principal weakness, as noted, stems from its sprawling narrative ambition. The relatively large number of secondary characters—police subordinates, various gangsters—means many are sketched too thinly. The audience has little time to become attached to their fates, which can dilute the emotional impact of the later massacre. While this perhaps intentionally mirrors the impersonal machinery of both the drug trade and the police state, it does create a certain emotional distance at the very moment the film seeks to overwhelm.

Despite this flaw, *Drug War* proved to be a massive box‑office hit in both China and Hong Kong, a testament to its gripping execution and topical ruthlessness. Its influence extended beyond borders, inspiring a 2018 South Korean remake, *Believer*, which later spawned a sequel. Over a decade on, *Drug War* appears as a pivotal work in Johnnie To’s filmography. It represents a successful grafting of his genre mastery onto a new, harsh national canvas, producing a police thriller of exceptional tension and a bleak, enduring commentary on crime, punishment, and the desperate calculus of survival under the shadow of the death penalty.


RATING: 7/10 (+++)

body.title: White Lies That Can Help Protect Those We Love
body.body:
# Happy warm weekend learners and friends 😍💕.


I don’t think there will be anyone exempted from white lies because these are lies many of us has told to either keep a relationship going or to maintain the peace in our marriages. White lies has helped most of us save and make those  we love not to be worried about us even when we are suffering from situations that we don’t want them to be involved in until its over.

# What Is A White Lie?

White lies in simple understanding are lies we humans tell to others to avoid hurting them or the lies we tell to also protect peace and make things seem all good.

As an adult 👩🏻 I came to understand why sometimes white lie is very important and necessary because it helps us to manage our home properly by trying to hide the situation when things are not rosy. And I then remembered my father while he was still alive. 

There was a time my father was facing challenges with his business due to how he lost huge sums of money 💰 he invested in a full truck of yam 🍠. He usually will bring yam in those days from the Northern  Nigeria 🇳🇬 to the Eastern Nigeria. Bulk trading was what he was into, because once his goods arrives, retail traders will come and buy in bulk from him. He buys all sorts of food stuffs in bulk. But it happened that when he ordered a truck of yam 🍠 in one if those trips, the truck got into a serious accident. This was a big blow on him then, but he manages to keep hiding by telling us everything is okay, especially to my mom who was so worried. He made sure to keep going and with time got back to his old self.

As a mother now, I sometimes feel so overwhelmed with things that are not properly situated, but I try all I could to make my family, especially the children believe  things are okay to avoid them worrying and make me loose focus. And  this usually will make me not feel so down knowing that I can manage my mood. Although my spouse as an adult surely will see signs of worry in me and will just keep reassuring me.

I do not see white lies as something totally 💯 bad as long as we are using it to keep worry away or to create peace of heart ♥️ . And as long as people are not hurt with this kinds of lies, we can say its a nature humans has devised for the sack of avoiding pain for others and creating peace of mind. The only danger in white lies is when people begin to constantly tell lies and use it as an excuses to get away. Too much of every thing is bad especially when it is done without sincerity.

Peace of mind is very important especially in the world 🌎 we are living today. Things are not as it use to be but we must not carry it on our faces . Many people are struggling with work, family, marriage, businesses and relationships. One needs wisdom at this very phase of life to carry on until things turns around for that dreams we individually are striving to achieve.

This is my response to the #hiveleaners featured content for week 219, edition 03.

# Best Regards @sunshine29 🧡

body.title: Chicken Adobo with Lots of Tofu
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmViqXntkA9deBcSmqqh3XJNxK6y9AkPUGZNBY7sMeQXYw/1780149945499.png)

Hello, food lovers! 🌷🌸🌷 
‎
‎Today I want to share what we had for lunch. It's one of our all-time favorite Filipino dishes with a little twist. 
‎
‎I cooked Chicken Adobo with Tofu. ✨ 
‎
‎That time, we only had a few pieces of chicken left in the kitchen, so I remembered that tofu is such a great alternative or partner to meat. That gave me the idea to combine them.
‎
‎**Ingredients:**
‎
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVbbmz9Ejnh8DSKryprhADaGXkF8ifWvNLJvck4KJfgxE/1780149982264.jpg)

‎• 500 grams chicken
‎• 2 cups tofu, cubed
‎• 5 cloves garlic, minced
‎• 1 medium onion, sliced
‎• 1 piece green chili
‎• 1/2 cup soy sauce
‎• 1/3 cup vinegar
‎• 1/2 cup water
‎• 1 teaspoon black pepper 
‎• 1 teaspoon sugar
‎• 1 piece chicken cube
‎• 2 tablespoons cooking oil
‎
‎**Let's cook!**
‎
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQpDhwXLBCyes2GVbRjEzjurxxjdccnxJVgxDJQnJ47gz/1780150003617.jpg)
‎
‎Before frying, I seasoned the tofu cubes first with a little salt and pepper. This gives it instant flavor.
‎
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQ2UGKEqk2ZhbxmsDMvs9GzgGpFFuEbKbbMyHNgFMgVSu/1780150024596.jpg)
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaHJi47U8spkDFe1tvxJcBDB53rtuyRDnpjQQcbCsnsXW/1780150024794.jpg)
‎
‎Then I heated some oil and fried them until they turned light golden on all sides. Frying them first keeps them from breaking apart later and gives them a nice, slightly crispy skin. Once done, I set them aside on a plate.
‎
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQm7YyAW5eAUNU67iQdpw6FXC63KyDhtDScrY7q9Qhwos/1780150050723.jpg)
‎
‎In the same pan with a little oil left, I sautéed the garlic and onion until they smelled so good. Then I added the chicken pieces and cooked them until they were light brown on all sides. 
‎
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcppWyTqkeHF1YUdtmkffe4uGRSbDvi47goojpRHbT5Bv/1780150073223.jpg)
‎
‎I poured in the soy sauce, added the peppercorns, and the chicken cube. I gave it a quick mix, then added a little water. I let it boil gently, then lowered the heat, covered the pan, and let it simmer until the chicken was almost tender and cooked through.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSxnhaYzPhtNxSNhD5rNCq67kmw5uDDw8wTQLaBYFiq12/1780150141287.jpg)
‎
‎Now it’s time to add the fried tofu back, I also put the green chili for that extra aroma. Then I pour in the vinegar and add a tiny bit of sugar. I didn’t stir it right away when I added the vinegar, I just let it boil for a minute or two to help remove that sharp sour taste. Then I mixed everything carefully so the sauce coats every piece of chicken and tofu. I let it simmer until the sauce thickened, and the tofu had soaked up the adobo goodness.
‎
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmduJAA4SGug5kpRf5S8f4aaFt9wK8UHsMRDGpzfjpuBpk/1780150172680.jpg)

body.title: When the Brain Fails to Move: Parkinson’s, Dopamine, and What Families Should Know
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYp9mKQxY2fUM12WmVveX8LcjrFgWJcUt5ZcNhXLRViUM/1780014339360.jpg)


English Version

When the Brain Fails to Move: Parkinson’s, Dopamine, and What Families Should Know

You already know Alzheimer's steals memories. But Parkinson's? It steals the ability to move with ease.

I explained this to someone recently: two diseases, two different brain chemicals. In Alzheimer, the problem is acetylcholine – the memory messenger. In Parkinson, it's dopamine – the movement lubricant.

Let me tell you what happens inside.

The Tiny Area That Changes Everything

Deep in your brain, there is a place called the substantia nigra – Latin for \

It produces dopamine. And in Parkinson's, those neurons die one by one.

Without dopamine, your muscles don't relax properly. They fight against you. The result?

· Slow movement (walking becomes heavy)
· Rigidity (arms don't swing freely)
· Tremor at rest (hand shaking while doing nothing)
· Freezing (feet stuck to the floor)

This is not laziness. This is not aging. This is a broken circuit.

Why Parkinson's Is Not Just \

Families often expect their loved one to forget things. But in early Parkinson, memory is usually fine. Instead, the person struggles with procedural learning – how to button a shirt, tie shoes, or start walking.

Think of it this way:
Alzheimer asks \

Both are cruel. But they need different understanding.

The Hidden Causes (What We Learned in Modules 1 and 2)

Parkinson doesn't come from nowhere. Three key factors:

1. Epigenetics – Stress or toxins can silence the gene that makes dopamine. Your DNA is not your destiny.
2. Microglial inflammation – The brain's immune cells overreact, killing dopamine neurons slowly.
3. Low BDNF – This \

drops without exercise. That's why movement therapy helps.

Treatment Today: Helpful but Not a Cure

Doctors give L-DOPA – a chemical that surviving neurons turn into dopamine. It works for years. But it doesn't stop the death of brain cells. Like Alzheimer, we are replacing what's lost, not rebuilding the factory.

A Question for You (Think About It)

Why doesn't an antidepressant like fluoxetine (which works on serotonin) help Parkinson's movement symptoms?
Hint: It's not because dopamine is the only problem. It's about circuits. Motor symptoms live in a dopamine highway, not a serotonin path.

What Families Can Do Right Now

· Learn about procedural memory – your loved one may not remember how to start walking. Cues help (visual lines on the floor).
· Exercise together – BDNF rises with movement. Even slow walking helps.
· Reduce inflammation – sleep, low sugar, and stress management protect remaining neurons.
· Be patient with freezing – it's not stubbornness. It's a brain stuck.


Spanish Version 

Cuando el cerebro olvida cómo moverse: Parkinson, dopamina y lo que toda familia debe saber

Ya sabes que el Alzheimer roba recuerdos. Pero el Parkinson roba algo igual de importante: la facilidad para moverse.

Hace poco se lo explicaba a alguien: dos enfermedades, dos mensajeros distintos. En el Alzheimer falla la acetilcolina – la química de la memoria. En el Parkinson falla la dopamina – el lubricante del movimiento.

Te cuento qué pasa dentro del cerebro.

El área diminuta que lo cambia todo

En lo profundo del cerebro hay un lugar llamado sustancia negra. Produce dopamina. En el Parkinson, esas neuronas mueren poco a poco.

Sin dopamina, los músculos no se relajan bien. Pelean contra ti. El resultado:

· Movimiento lento (caminar se vuelve pesado)
· Rigidez (los brazos no se balancean)
· Temblor en reposo (mano que tiembla sin hacer nada)
· Congelación (pies pegados al suelo)

Esto no es pereza. No es vejez normal. Es un circuito roto.

Por qué el Parkinson no es solo \

Las familias a veces esperan que su ser querido olvide cosas. Pero al principio del Parkinson, la memoria suele estar bien. En cambio, la persona lucha con el aprendizaje procedural – cómo abrocharse una camisa, atarse los cordones o empezar a caminar.

Piénsalo así:
El Alzheimer pregunta \

Ambas son crueles. Pero necesitan comprensiones distintas.



El Parkinson no aparece de la nada. Tres factores clave:

1. Epigenética – El estrés o toxinas pueden silenciar el gen que fabrica dopamina. Tu ADN no es un destino fijo.
2. Inflamación microglial – Las células inmunes del cerebro se exaltan y matan neuronas dopaminérgicas lentamente.
3. BDNF bajo – Este \

cae sin ejercicio. Por eso el movimiento es terapia.

Tratamiento actual: útil, pero no cura

Los médicos dan L-DOPA – una sustancia que las neuronas vivas convierten en dopamina. Funciona durante años. Pero no frena la muerte neuronal. Como en Alzheimer: reponemos lo perdido, pero no reconstruimos la fábrica.

Una pregunta para ti (reflexiona)

¿Por qué un antidepresivo como la fluoxetina (que actúa sobre serotonina) no ayuda con los síntomas motores del Parkinson?
Pista: no es solo porque la dopamina sea la única afectada. Es por los circuitos. Los síntomas motores viven en una autopista de dopamina, no en una ruta de serotonina.

Qué pueden hacer las familias ahora mismo

· Aprende sobre memoria procedural – tu familiar quizá no recuerde cómo empezar a caminar. Las pistas visuales ayudan (líneas en el suelo).
· Hagan ejercicio juntos – el BDNF sube con el movimiento. Aunque sea caminar lento.
· Reduzcan la inflamación – dormir bien, bajar el azúcar y manejar el estrés protege las neuronas que quedan.
· Ten paciencia con la congelación – no es terquedad. Es un cerebro atascado.


Final Hook for Your Hive Post

\

Share this. Let families know they are not alone – and neither is their patient.

body.title: The Love and Pain I Carry on Your Birthday
body.body:
Today I want to share a few thoughts on my non-biological mother's birthday. I was not able to greet her personally. I only sent my birthday greeting through one of our relatives because until now, we still don't have communication with each other.

![1747.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/usagigallardo015/23wqiMLktD1ejiNY1PcLj3EHDu8RT79Hw8caKtfyz41FcaeZod5Yuv88D8n66nxKDhosN.jpg)

![1746.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/usagigallardo015/23wC9VSmgFXfoFSfvNVkzmsGqs4pXsRzicYQjrqeFpGnJjrmGr2xCJm26tAigNUAebx5K.jpg)

To be honest, there are times when I wonder why life turned out this way. Maybe this is one of the realities of being adopted. Sometimes it hurts, and sometimes I feel sad about the things that can no longer be changed. There are moments when I regret some parts of my past, but I also know that looking back will not bring those days back. Life keeps moving forward whether we/I like it or not.

Even with everything that happened, I still want to greet her a happy birthday. I may not always understand everything, but I am still thankful to her. Without her, I would not be here today. The life I have now may not be perfect, but it is still a life worth being grateful for. Like many people, I also experience many ups and downs, but I continue doing my best for my family.

<div class=\

>https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/usagigallardo015/23vsQY5mrFhkh6hxPpxjdDrsN6k9qo4SgY5PAtsHWHGsph5zNB3enzRWtwwpTbbzmyA7d.jpg Looking at my children reminds me of how important family is. I am especially thankful for my daughter. She is not only a loving sister to her younger siblings, but sometimes she also acts like a second mother to them. She helps me in many ways without being asked. Seeing her care for her brothers and sisters makes my heart happy. ![1751.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/usagigallardo015/EqYw2kpQxTDt7Nugs5VVDhKgWYQp6m1SQeKMnU7KLGHkidKoZAV4de2N7q6EHh5wDix.jpg) ![1755.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/usagigallardo015/EpnFDDHnqh5Y5cWq1tKwcQfUrsga6c2E49oCBG9k8gWKrgJTM4CCWWXjnwXXiVepC28.jpg) 8 ![1753.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/usagigallardo015/Eq7PNWfmogVECEjkQGSBN1jMLfALCQRyvx1Dvdu8FrePAmbEdcnab9FcspdSB4NVDhJ.jpg) There are days when problems become too heavy. Sometimes when my husband and I argue, I feel like running away for a while. But then I realize I have nowhere else to go. There are moments when I feel sorry for myself because I do not have the kind of family support that others have. Still, whenever I look at my children, I remember why I keep going. Maybe I was left behind before, but I never want my children to feel that kind of pain. No matter how difficult life becomes, I will always choose to stay with them, love them, and guide them. They are my greatest blessing and my reason to keep moving forward. To my mom Happy Birthday, Mama. I hope you are healthy, happy, and at peace wherever you are. *Thank you for reading my post* *@usagigallardo015*

body.title: [Esp./Eng.]   Respiremos juntos.   ||   Let’s breathe together.
body.body:
*** *** #
If you prefer the English version, click on the following link 👉 [**HERE**](#english)
*** ***

; no es metáfora, es un nudo que se instala cuando la felicidad parece un lujo lejano y la paz, más bien, un refugio urgente. He visto a otros sufrir, bajo esa fe que antes les sostenía se quiebra como vidrio bajo el peso de la pregunta: *¿dónde estabas?* Es intrigante escuchar que \
. Duele más cuando quienes hablan de amor, paz y libertad lo hacen con palabras vacías, sermones que no tocan la tierra donde la gente camina descalza. Tal cual: *\

*.
# ***
Respiremos juntos
*** Me he preguntado tantas veces, ¿para qué estamos aquí?; es que, no puede ser solo sufrir y desaparecer. He estado leyendo a Viktor Frankl, queen conoció el abismo y escribió: *\

… No lo dice para glorificar el dolor, sino para recordarnos que en la oscuridad más densa podemos elegir cómo habitarlo. Es mucho más que simple resignación, *es dignidad*.

<center>![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNM6Jewt4ysjbXHbnFsyTzEKA7FXyKXZqNNmErS4svrjw/pasado.jpg)
</center>

El tiempo corre acelerado —así lo percibo últimamente—, hoy estamos —aquí me encuentro publicando—, mañana quién sabe y en esa fugacidad, hay algo que sí permanece: *la luz de quienes luchan*. Los que madrugan en hospitales con las manos cansadas y el corazón en alerta. Las madres y padres que convierten un puñado de monedas en cena, en abrazo, en futuro… Ellos, no son héroes de portada; representan la humanidad en su forma más real, la que no necesita discurso porque ya lo es. Como acostumbran a escriben en la comunidad Holos&Lotus, a veces la evolución no es hacia afuera, sino hacia adentro, algo que denominan \

, quitar lo que sobra para dejar espacio a lo esencial [@danielvehe77]. Y a veces ni se dispone d lo esencial.\n\nLa tecnología avanza, a pasos agigantados. Tenemos máquinas que podríamos afirmar que \

, redes que conectan continentes en milisegundos. Pero, como reflexionamos en #Humanitas, ¿nos estamos volviendo más humanos o solo más eficientes?. Me gustaría leer la apreciación del amigo @emilirios, quizá él de en el clavo, je, je, je.\n\nLa vulnerabilidad —esa que nos hace temblar, llorar, preguntar— no es un error del sistema, es más que  eso..., es la puerta. \

, compartía alguien en Holos&Lotus hace poco [@isaacmf123]. Dejarnos ver, sin filtros, sin máscaras de éxito -a quién le importa-. Eso es revolucionario hoy; no le encuentro sentido por qué es mal visto por muchos.

<center>![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPDPnLRsm4wYTCFXSR8hb6hhJhA87Ej7z9in7u6XApkAR/1a.png)
</center>

Albert Camus nos dejó una brújula, para algunos incómoda: *\

*… No es pesimismo, es honestidad radical-humana. La protesta, aquí, no es solo contra sistemas injustos; es contra la indiferencia, contra la prisa que nos roba el mirar a los ojos, contra la palabra hueca que sustituye al abrazo. Les estraño: @lecumberre, @mllg, @fibra69… Ultimamente pienso en @charjaim. ¿Y ustedes?\n\nEduardo Galeano, cronista de esperanzas porfiadas, nos cuenta que la condición humana vale la pena *\

*…  Rehacernos, no solos…, juntos. En la fila del supermercado, en la sala de espera, en el comentario sincero que rompe la soledad del scroll infinito.

No tengo respuestas definitivas. Solo sé que, en medio del torbellino, hay gestos que son oración sin palabras: *la mano que sostiene, el silencio que acompaña, la comida compartida, la lágrima que no se juzga*. Esos son los sermones que sí sanan. Querida @issamari2, mis oraciones para que tu esposo mejore pronto.

<center>![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSc2AoHVtYKmpd9bgRjTpzazDH7fKsmEsU8wKX6u6b5P7/ellas2.jpg)
</center>

A ustedes, luchadores, de madrugada, de sonrisa cansada pero firme: *este escrito es para ustedes*. No por ser perfectos, sino porque, en su imperfección valiente, encienden la luz de otros. Y la luz, aunque pequeña, siempre gana a la oscuridad. No con estruendo, sino con presencia.

El tiempo pasa. Sí, pero mientras haya alguien que elija la compasión sobre el cinismo, la escucha sobre el sermón, la paz sobre la ilusión de control… mientras haya eso; hay sentido. No un sentido grandilocuente, sino uno cotidiano, terrenal, humano.

Como el aire que entra por la ventana después de la tormenta. No cura todo, pero permite respirar. Y a veces, respirar juntos ya es una forma de rezar.

<center>![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaAsWtz1UTMk99uhuGM5Cor9Z1BGdNiBFR5p6qdfpBr4i/elllas1.jpg)
</center>

Con gratitud a las comunidades #Holos&Lotus y #Humanitas por tejer espacios donde la palabra honesta encuentra hogar. **\
**. Porque al final, después de tanto pensar, tanto dolor y tanto buscar, lo único que nos salva es eso: ***no estar solos en el aliento.***

> **Creciendo como persona, busca y encuentra lo que necesitas para ser un mejor humano en la Comunidad [Holos&Lotus](https://peakd.com/c/hive-131951/created). De seguro, hay un tema que te llamará la atención.**
https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/holos-lotus/245n3ai2B1twdEnyzuYXmYiNoGag22e7ZZQ7uz72NKdqPqaR6PyaDrSeA7EMUq9RuNPHc.png Infografía propia de la Comunidad [Holos&Lotus](https://peakd.com/c/hive-131951/created)
*** ***
🔆+++🔆+++🔆+++🔆+++🔆+++🔆+++🔆+++🔆+++🔆+++🔆

*** *** ##
Dedicado a todos aquellos que, día a día, hacen del mundo un lugar mejor.
*** ***
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcnceTgTBLgAUkErZfdoePC7twytC1CTcqQYDKkU4Lrrd/1024espa_ol8.gif) ***
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbdpsZFqtrcoLk94sUV8oHkjnx8PAdgfACMfJ9UpcriNF/perfil2026_hecho_con_clipchamp_2_.gif) ***

*** *** ***

> ‘The weight of the burden on one’s back hurts’; it is no metaphor, but a knot that forms when happiness seems a distant luxury and peace, rather, an urgent refuge. I have seen others suffer, as the faith that once sustained them shatters like glass under the weight of the question: *Where were you?* It is intriguing to hear that ‘perhaps they are right’. It hurts more when those who speak of love, peace and freedom do so with empty words, sermons that do not touch the ground where people walk barefoot. Just like that: *‘words are carried away by the wind’*.
# ***
Let’s breathe together
*** I have asked myself so many times, why are we here?; surely, it cannot be just to suffer and disappear. I’ve been reading Viktor Frankl, who knew the abyss and wrote: *“If there is meaning in life, there must be meaning in suffering”…* He doesn’t say this to glorify pain, but to remind us that in the deepest darkness we can choose how to inhabit it. It is much more than mere resignation; *it is dignity*.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNM6Jewt4ysjbXHbnFsyTzEKA7FXyKXZqNNmErS4svrjw/pasado.jpg)
Time is racing by –that’s how I’ve been feeling lately– today we’re here –here I am, writing this– tomorrow, who knows? And yet, amidst all that fleetingness, there is one thing that endures: *the light of those who fight*. Those who rise early in hospitals, their hands weary and their hearts on high alert. The mothers and fathers who turn a handful of coins into a meal, a hug, a future… They are not cover-story heroes; they represent humanity in its truest form, the kind that needs no grand speech because it already is. As they often write in the Holos&Lotus community, sometimes evolution is not outward, but inward—something they call ‘minimalism of the soul’, removing the excess to make room for the essential [@danielvehe77]. And sometimes we don’t even have the essential. Technology is advancing by leaps and bounds. We have machines that we could say “think”, networks that connect continents in milliseconds. But, as we reflect on in #Humanitas, are we becoming more human or just more efficient? I’d like to read my friend @emilirios’s take on this; perhaps he’ll hit the nail on the head, heh, heh, heh. Vulnerability —the kind that makes us tremble, cry, and ask questions— isn’t a glitch in the system; it’s more than that… it’s the gateway. “Vulnerability isn’t always about asking for help; sometimes it’s about letting others see us,” someone shared on Holos&Lotus recently [@isaacmf123]. Letting ourselves be seen, without filters, without masks of success –who cares?– That is revolutionary today; I cannot understand why it is frowned upon by so many.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPDPnLRsm4wYTCFXSR8hb6hhJhA87Ej7z9in7u6XApkAR/1a.png)
Albert Camus left us a compass, one that some find uncomfortable: *‘I cry out that I believe in nothing and that everything is absurd, but I cannot doubt my cry and I need, at least, to believe in my protest’*… It is not pessimism, it is radical human honesty. Protest, here, is not just against unjust systems; it is against indifference, against the rush that robs us of looking into each other’s eyes, against the empty words that replace a hug. I miss you all: @lecumberre, @mllg, @fibra69… Lately I’ve been thinking of @charjaim. And you? Eduardo Galeano, chronicler of stubborn hopes, tells us that the human condition is worth it *‘because we have been badly made, but we can remake ourselves’*… Remake ourselves, not alone… together. In the supermarket queue, in the waiting room, in the sincere comment that breaks the loneliness of endless scrolling. I don’t have any definitive answers. I only know that, in the midst of the turmoil, there are gestures that are prayer without words: *the hand that holds, the silence that accompanies, the meal shared, the tear that is not judged*. Those are the sermons that truly heal. Dear @issamari2, my prayers are with you for your husband’s speedy recovery.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaAsWtz1UTMk99uhuGM5Cor9Z1BGdNiBFR5p6qdfpBr4i/elllas1.jpg)
To you, the fighters, in the early hours, with a weary but steadfast smile: *this is for you*. Not because you are perfect, but because, in your courageous imperfection, you kindle the light in others. And the light, however small, always triumphs over the darkness. Not with a clamour, but with presence. Time passes. Yes. But as long as there is someone who chooses compassion over cynicism, listening over preaching, peace over the illusion of control… as long as that exists; there is meaning. Not a grandiloquent meaning, but an everyday, earthly, human one. Like the air that flows in through the window after the storm. It doesn’t heal everything, but it allows us to breathe. And sometimes, breathing together is already a form of prayer.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSc2AoHVtYKmpd9bgRjTpzazDH7fKsmEsU8wKX6u6b5P7/ellas2.jpg)
With gratitude to the #Holos&Lotus and #Humanitas communities for weaving spaces where honest words find a home. **“Breathing together”**. Because in the end, after so much thinking, so much pain and so much searching, the only thing that saves us is this: ***not being alone in our breath.***

> **Growing as a person, seek and find what you need to be a better person in the [Holos&Lotus](https://peakd.com/c/hive-131951/created) Community. Surely, there's a topic that will catch your attention.**
https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/holos-lotus/245n3ai2B1twdEnyzuYXmYiNoGag22e7ZZQ7uz72NKdqPqaR6PyaDrSeA7EMUq9RuNPHc.png Community's own infographic [Holos&Lotus](https://peakd.com/c/hive-131951/created)

body.title: A Massive Makeover for the Mithril Diesel Pool (And Other HiveTools Updates)
body.body:
Lately, I’ve been busy making a bunch of changes to **HiveTools** and **Market-Viewr**. 

This wasn’t just one big feature drop. Instead, it was a laundry list of layout cleanups, UI/UX polish, dark mode fixes, and some under-the-hood structural changes that I finally got around to staging.

Before I jump into the details, I want to give a massive shoutout and special thanks to **@forkyishere**. Most of the UI improvements and functional tweaks listed below came directly from his suggestions and feedback. Working with the community to make these tools less annoying is easily the best part of building them.

Here is the rundown of what has been going on.

---

## 1. Beeswap is now the Mithril Diesel Pool

The first big change is a branding shift. The old Beeswap references and modules are now rebranded to **Mithril Diesel Pool**. 

Along with the name change, the layout got a complete makeover:
- **Theme-aware banner headers** that match your preference.
- A **responsive sidebar** layout for balances.
- Clearer spacing and typography across the swap and pool pages.

It looks a lot cleaner and feels like a cohesive part of the tool suite.

![The new Mithril Diesel Pool swap interface](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/thecrazygm/23swgX7S58JUVo33FwA6R9LvNDg9iPBKe596wSjEHvBwxHLM7DnWKi3o1hZCuZ99vPREd.png)

---

## 2. Dynamic OpenGraph Preview Images

If you shared a specific pool link on Twitter/X or Discord before, you just got the default site metadata. 

Now, pools have a dynamic OG image generator built on the backend using Python's Pillow library. When a link is shared, the server dynamically draws a custom preview image showing the pair symbols, active reserves, current price, and TVL metrics.

You also get full OpenGraph, Twitter Cards, and Facebook tags generated dynamically for every single pool route. Sharing is much more visual now.

![Example of a dynamic OpenGraph preview card](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/thecrazygm/23tRrJ5CsgSFMZWMyJEwV4hiz8rojbctXrjFSCtoPFypioruwEJXtnxhHgCnesqQ8j1bb.png)

---

## 3. Dropdowns Aren't Stupidly Long Anymore

In the pool pages, we have long dropdowns listing available tokens or user positions. If you are dealing with common base tokens like `SWAP.HIVE`, that list can stretch to dozens or hundreds of items. It overflowed the screen, looked terrible, and made selection a chore.

We fixed this by:
- Adding **sticky search boxes** at the top of the dropdown lists.
- Restricting list height and making them **scrollable** (`max-height: 250px` or `300px`).
- Preventing the dropdown from closing when you click the search box.
- Auto-focusing the search input as soon as you toggle the dropdown open.

This is active on the main swap interface, the tokens list, and the add/remove liquidity screens.

![The new searchable, scrollable token/pair dropdown menu in action](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/thecrazygm/23tkfpWaY6uQuFS7iaEWKowZvWrXkYgNGrgZJ1Z9zsx7qcvsNZ3eoZ3qdDFNStoVx3gp4.png)

---

## 4. Dark Mode Actually Works Everywhere

Dark mode is great until you find pages with high-contrast text that look like they were styled in 1998, or cards with white backgrounds that blind you.

I did a sweep across the code and fixed these:
- Changed remaining hardcoded `bg-light` classes to theme-aware `bg-body-tertiary` or `bg-body-secondary`.
- Resolved contrast issues in the Post Curation Tool (PCT) post cards, links, badges, and tag chips.
- Removed outdated `table-light` headers that overrode dark mode table rendering.
- Fixed text colors on error pages and feature headings to use `text-body-emphasis` so they are readable.

---

## 5. Dynamic Sitemap and Favicons

Search engine optimization isn't exciting, but it has to be done. 

I wired up a `/sitemap.xml` endpoint that dynamically queries the Flask application's `url_map`. It automatically lists every static and tools route while filtering out dynamic detail pages, API endpoints, and redirects. If I add a new tool tomorrow, it will show up in the sitemap automatically.

Also, I finally put together a proper **favicon suite** (including high-res icons and a web app manifest) so the app icons look crisp on mobile home screens and modern browsers.

---

## 6. Market-Viewr Updates

On the **Market-Viewr** side, I made a couple of adjustments to align with the new design:
- Updated the header layout and external links to match the Mithril Diesel Pool branding.
- Fixed a bug in the services layer where market history queries weren't filtering data by the requested timeframe on the python backend. Now, history charts display only the selected range instead of throwing range mismatches.

![The updated Market-Viewr layout and history charts](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/thecrazygm/23wMyixjU2DqfoDSkPVUtGwpXM23xtxg88w37zPK3x2kJj54eZ1bDyJHTwM3JHoH2KSC2.png)

---

It feels good to get these details sorted. 

As always,
**Michael Garcia** a.k.a. **TheCrazyGM**

body.title: Is life a responsibility or a pleasure?
body.body:
![280824.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josediccus/23uQhkBQvEwhaU1vn4RPNd8gR3oc7bTaQZWByrNCq3qR8TmK8i9TMFUKvSVQbGq3rhNAb.jpg)


<hr>

I saw a post sometimes back about a very good footballer who said he actually didn't enjoy playing football and that all it was to him was a business and a job. 

A lot of people thought that it was weird for someone to do something they didn't like and I find it very funny.

 A lot of people are unhappy with the things they have to do for money, but they still do it anyway because responsibility does not recognize passion, likeness or love.


 Life requires a lot of responsibility and a lot of the decisions we make in life shows how responsible we choose to be. We don't have to like life to be responsible, and to be responsible is mostly likely not something we always like to do.


 To be responsible means to make the tough choices, it means to do what takes gut to do, to bury our innermost desires and choose that which is right and tenable. 



This is exactly why people can work and not love their jobs, the paycheck is all the fulfilment they need, their ability to solve problems, the joy the derive from being able to pay their way out of life is always the biggest motivation to get their hands dirty and muddle in the things they never wanted.


 This isn't me saying people cannot love what they do, or that there aren't people who don't love the thing they do. 



Infact the best profession in life or hustle is that type where you actually love what you do and are paid very handsomely for it, there's no greater fulfillment than this. Infact being a master, a pro at what you do, and infact having a level of passion for what you do makes you one of the best. 


This is why when it comes to careers like football, the best in the game are those with love for the game. Those who just wants to do the game before the money. 


Although money can also be a passion that drives the love for the game, but it's better for money to drive the passion, than for people to have no drive at all because they already made enough money. 



Inasmuch as we can be passionate or hungry for success, some people become complacent, lose their drive when they already feel that they've made enough money.



 They got diminishing returns so fast that you won't even remember that there was a time they were very passionate about the business, the game and all that. 



However the person I talked about at the beginning of the post is a rare breed: they don't like or rate the game, for them it's a business, and they just want to keep putting in their best, training to make sure that they make enough money to retire happily.


### Passion/business 

 For example, I'm a football fan, I'd probably have loved to be a player, even though I didn't have the requirements to become one, I know that it would be an honor to be able to step out on a good day, impress my employers, the customers (the fans) and raise my stock and quality myself for a raise.


 I can love the game, because the money is good, but this mostly appeals to business and not a lot of other jobs. I worked as a school teacher for over 7 years, and I loved the job because I got the meet people and I used it as a coping mechanism for the trauma I was already facing, but the money was very poor. 


This is the business, responsibility and the need to sort something is why we mostly do what we do, it's what the average person mostly do. People wake up, do the business their supposed to do and then make out tome to go to the park, unwind and do other things, why?

 **Because the business is business and not for relaxing and not for any other things.**


 Life is bizarre and strange, and in that state of incomprehensibility, people build patterns of sustenance and that's why we have the concept of responsibility: doing what matters most, when we should do it and why we need to properly do it.


 We don't need to love the concept of responsibility to actually be responsible people, although people run away from it because it's not always pleasant. It's not always comfortable to be the \

, the one who have to bear the burden with two-sided consequences, it's a tough world, but it's what it is. 


The world is a tough place but we live it nonetheless, sometimes we don't find pleasure but we still do the tough things.

body.title: Chainlink Market Update and Price Outlook
body.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmeZgXV8f8jqRk6JV3TKk9UFmoez3kcMWnneq17qdHTJd8/1000010773.png 

Chainlink just made a big move that caught everyone's attention. Their Cross Chain Interoperability Protocol (CCIP) is now officially used by Saturn for the Strategy's STRC digital credit infrastructure. With total deposits hitting $220 million in no time, it is clear proof that Chainlink is becoming the backbone of the global DeFi ecosystem.

Beyond the tech side, on chain data shows a bullish signal from the big players. Currently, the number of whale wallets holding over 100,000 LINK tokens has hit a record high of 805 wallets. This massive accumulation shows that institutional investors are quietly soaking up supply while the price is still moving sideways.

  https://img.leopedia.io/DQmdH5kadX1EREFcU35gVcmAQ3FpA5Xyzu8JoQLa9ABWFRv/1000010764.png 

 


**Price Action Analysis**
Looking at the current market, the price is hovering around $9.15. For traders, there are a few key zones we need to watch closely to see where the trend is heading next.

  
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmPyigoou9HhpZyZWjcQdUo3LMBUeYZZTFJzpboRcjnHq3/1000010765.png 


The main resistance zone is sitting between $13.36 and $14.54. This is a tough wall to break if we want to see a real bullish run. On the flip side, we really need to watch how the market reacts if the price drops into the support zone between $7.10 and $7.73.

    
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmeTYQtoiopbVJ11kJyJvdEaLbhZAtqX7NScoiDfAMvFDk/1000010766.png 


Derivatives data shows active long and short positions on big exchanges like Binance and OKX. This reflects both the excitement and the caution that traders have regarding short term price swings.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmeYa12Xp57DyTFdSVqyhVtZtjDoVaGJ87gHr1wv3o3FeF/1000010767.jpg 


For now, we just need to stay calm and watch how the price behaves when it hits these technical zones. Always remember to do your own research before making any trading moves.

**My Take**
Looking at the market right now, I think we shouldn't just rely on support and resistance lines. Even though Chainlink keeps showing its strength with aggressive CCIP adoption, the market is still clearly thirsty for liquidity.

Keep in mind that whale accumulation doesn't mean the price will skyrocket tomorrow. It is often just a game of patience. In my opinion, many retail traders get trapped because they react too quickly to news hype without looking at institutional order blocks. If we are not disciplined with risk management at those support zones I mentioned, market volatility can easily wipe out our positions before the real trend even starts. Don't let fomo beat your technical strategy.

While walking, I accidentally saw many shadows around me. The shadows were caused by the light of the setting sun behind the light, which provides a lot of natural beauty that we don't expect. body.title: SATURDAY PREP VIBES🙂🥳😜: HOW MY DAY WENT
body.body:
Good morning family 💛 

I’m @shugarito and welcome to my Saturday! 
From a fresh fruit salad breakfast, to the Saturday market madness for Sunday stew, then ending my day with hot noodles. 

If you love simple, real-life stories with Nigerian flavor, come along 👇

    1. Breakfast: My Colorful Fruit Salad 🥗
I kicked off my Saturday with something light + healthy. 
Banana, kiwi, grapes and pawpaw. No sugar added, just pure fruit goodness. 

I’m trying to eat clean before I cook Sunday stew tomorrow, and this combo gave me energy for the market stress 😂


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVFe84GbBbvqGeF52sWkvLiAxRZNKsTCcQQwn8An4T7nB/1780149645569.jpg)



What’s your go-to fruit? Mine is kiwi all day!

     2. Saturday Market Run For Sunday Stew 🛒
After breakfast, I rushed to the market. You know how Saturday markets are - crowded, noisy, and everyone buying for Sunday 😅

Tomatoes, peppers, onions, and palm oil everywhere. I had to use my “market voice” to bargain well o 😂 


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcbUv8v4KBn48uBtKxwpppwcmkJvGfwVgAYTyBNy2p85w/1780149507647.jpg)


Saturday market taught me patience again. But I still love the energy. People laughing, shouting prices, children running around. That’s home.

     3. Afternoon Rest: Hot Noodles 🍜
I came back home tired but satisfied. After market + cleaning, I just wanted food that’s fast + comforting. 

Noodles saved me this afternoon. Simple, hot, and it felt like a reward for my Saturday hustle. 



![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcbUv8v4KBn48uBtKxwpppwcmkJvGfwVgAYTyBNy2p85w/1780149408517.jpg)


Sometimes after “adulting” all day, noodles is therapy 😊

   Final Thoughts 
Saturday for me = healthy morning, busy market afternoon, chill night 😌


   So tell me:
How do you spend your Saturdays? Market like me or rest at home? Tell me in comments, I’ll reply everyone 👇

Thanks for spending part of your Saturday reading my day. Drop an upvote if you felt the vibe 💚

body.body:
Full Metal Ox Day 1917
Saturday 30, May 2026
Abundance Year Episode 1982
Noxsoma Life Camp:  

Sabado Grande Mi gente. Welcome to one more show above ground. El Nino is on the way. I watched a documentary about the history of the climate phenomenon. Maybe it’s a phenomenon to us exceptional humans, but it may be something very natural to the planet. 

We’re on this language “kick.”, which has actually become more of a tradition than kick, and more of a lifestyle than tradition. (Reminder, “lifestyle” was coined by one of those Austrian psychologists.) Language locks humans into behavior, identity and emotion, and is used deftly by the Supremacy to control and manipulate. Maybe you can think of a word right now that “triggers” you. Maybe it’s the very idea that you can be triggered by a sound, that triggers you. 

Today’s word exploration is, “bling-bling,” which was later truncated to simply, “bling.” It’s sort of the slang of the slang. 

This is how the Supremacy defines the word.  

“Bling originated in American rap slang around 1997, referring to wealth and expensive accessories, and is thought to mimic the sound of sparkling jewels. The term gained popularity through hip hop culture, particularly after the release of the song \

by rapper B.G. in 1999.”   

Because, “bling” is believed to mimic the sound of the representation of opulence, it’s considered an onomatopoeia. For those who are encountering this word for the first time, (onomatopoeia, not bling), it’s a word, that describes a word that makes a sound. Like BOOM! 

There are few words that emerged from hip-hop culture that expose the colonized mind like, “bling.” But it didn’t start with hip-hop. Iconic actor and former professional wrestler Mr T arguably started the trend.  

“Mr. T began wearing his iconic gold chains while working as a bouncer at a nightclub in the 1970s, where he would wear items left behind by customers. He later adopted this look as part of his public persona in the 1980s.”

The mid 1970s was the “Disco Era” in America and “gold medallions” were a thing particularly among Italian-Americans. They were a demonstration of wealth, affluence and respect. The psychological need for such displays says a lot about life in America. 

When African-Americans, particularly rappers and DJs, performed, they often reflected the disco-era, (hip-hop sprung from disco), status symbol tradition of wearing their presumed wealth around their necks. DJ Cool Herc, and Afrika Bambaataa were both pioneers of hip-hop and, “the bling.” 

Hip-hop was damn-near a quarter century deep by the time the word was attached to the psychosis. MCs, rappers, and such, who were getting signed abundantly in the early 1990s, would spend their advances, (which were supposed to be used to produce recorded products), would go out and buy “bling.” 

“Bling” as a word, had a short lifespan. The recently deceased MTV, which is probably at least partially responsible for spreading the word, declared it dead in 2003. Then, a year later released a satirical cartoon showing the term being used first by a rapper and then by several progressively less \

characters, concluding with a middle-aged white woman describing her earrings to her elderly mother. 

In hindsight, we can see “bling” as not merely a word, but as a early representative of the proto-social media culture where displays are wealth, affluence & influence are paramount, yet substance is minimal, if it exists at all. 

From gold medallions, to fake-gold chains, to fake-gangsters, to Milli Vanilli, to fake profiles, to fake news, to fake solutions, to living in a simulation. 

We cannot say that it all started with “bling-bling.” But every so often a word is injected into the zeitgeist, without thought or meditation, and it reveals more about human-herd behavior in its short lifespan than all the dream interpretations of Carl Jung, and the sleep predictions of Edgar Casey.   

Stay safe, stay strong, stay savvy, stay sane, stay serene, stay sovereign, stay subscribed.   

PEACE
