title.title: 💙✨️🩵Diseño y confección de hermosa blusa para damas con abertura en los hombros 🩵✨️💙//💙✨️🩵Design and tailoring of a beautiful blouse for ladies with an open shoulder 🩵✨️💙.
title.body:
![PhotoCollage_1780095588764.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EpxqqpP2hUkXQefeWEVD6bNDbuKmUorYYRBCgRAMrwSWGUxjKiW6mrV7AGUDeSMYemF.jpg)


## <center>![Dark Blue Elegant 3d Illustration Geometric Learn Trading LinkedIn Banner_20250330_123401_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EogLLfn85cBrHe3KhAh7PovBi4K8hLTcRsvMSWsR5Ckowwj9chcc4jD6rFrTQXxu6G7.png)</center>

Hola hola mis queridos amigos de Hive ❤️ muy buenas noches para todos espero que se encuentren muy bien disfrutando de esta linda noche 🤗 hoy quise compartir con ustedes mi trabajo de costura más reciente pues se trata de una hermosa blusa color azul agua marina con lindo detalle en las mangas ideal para lucir en una ocasión casual debido a la comodidad de su diseño 🤗 los invito a acompañarme en todos y cada uno de los pasos a seguir.

## <center>![Dark Blue Elegant 3d Illustration Geometric Learn Trading LinkedIn Banner_20250330_123750_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EoeD4ZYmGMcA1CW4RjbUfETNsxP1CoRkKoksHVLGgf7zTMEjBuU9wELEzbdtKo6QHRF.png)</center>

• 🧵Máquina de coser 
• ✂️Tijera
•🧵 Hilo de coser
• ✂️Tela
•🧵 Aguja N°9


## <center>![Dark Blue Elegant 3d Illustration Geometric Learn Trading LinkedIn Banner_20250330_124019_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EogLTkcA4KmHee1ae9uY4exDHRtdiAVLUW5Eyt13x67CYnejnvipNfNBiKPQR7ueDwq.png)</center>







•✨️🩵Como primer paso voy a cortar todas las piezas de mi blusa siendo estas una pieza trasera, delantera ambas corridas con las mangas, el cuello, la orilla de la abertura y los tiros para las trenzas. 

|![20260527_201913.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23vsScckpG2RBHsVXR69Laua5sZwHY2D6kTVXu6sdaDm42jKM9mRrXWBjzYscoWUhaX6F.jpg)|![20260527_201919.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wCE27aGwc4oZiRhT9SymYgj8Wq67R6niJHSbVguZRdCRVQuYfzEXKr9Gsdpa3uppGZE.jpg)|
|-|-|

•✨️🩵Continúo uniendo ambas piezas trasera y delantera a través de los extremos con costura recta y zigzag para asegurar luego voy a coser un poco la parte superior de los hombros con costura recta y zigzag para asegurar.

|![20260527_212854.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wCLgA9saj1arUar4BaEiMMWparQMpUUQau8YRrm8H6XobGwZqw2X2ozoDPHAgoFvBHr.jpg)|![20260527_213147.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23xetmr3LKwqM1NRYs7jFhxxLXTJxYZKMySQbfm2rK98e82iLvep8Dvubpf1nF9U62cJT.jpg)|![20260527_213644.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23vsb8fCr9uPQ77xGcJ1namSRaicefhgYkdDgEjhGYgiTcuAEcX5aeztzrcXt4CAiZkjy.jpg)|![20260527_213751.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23vscuqVYXgbB9tiWbe6Ly78NjmG3b5uNpAsrVL7enFgZ2qd8cf7Xrnwgk2Yh1zBPiV5M.jpg)|
|-|-|-|-|

•✨️🩵Luego voy a doblar el tiro del cuello y lo pondré en el lado derecho de la tela y voy a coser con costura recta y zigzag para asegurar luego voy a coser el extremo de hombro faltante con costura recta y zigzag para asegurar.


|![20260527_214312.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23ywwUjCUTDtRQEnMxt1o5gHtu5KKpmEB5wmzDEmXRMJb1HZ6e4vvt89HHivf7gmeXEAU.jpg)|![20260527_214725.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wX9zC2LEc7Ai328JmHnAMer3uLenovj3F6STSG43dAfabxL6ofYnsa1iGZN2yovJfbW.jpg)|![20260527_224041.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wXA9NQpdfjBJv5eexVV2bow1nSeriMoVchzee5zrTAEeL3TWeYGTraTGxM1Gk2TDdJR.jpg)|![20260527_224240.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23viCDKr1oUadgf3n87Bcv3hMiQ6RHjvkAWZduXqp8rX4g55gQskCiA8fHFXY8pMNpDUn.jpg)|
|-|-|-|-|

•✨️🩵Voy a doblar la orilla de mi tiro de abertura y voy a coser un pequeño ruedo y voy a coser la orilla de la manga y luego dicha orilla la voy a doblar y la voy a coser por el lado derecho de la tela con costura recta y zigzag para asegurar.

|![20260528_220513.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23xL9KaUf6yFccFm6GP3hZAt11YdmcmStv8cBNSjpYbwo97s4HBfAR95EEqFeFbKMbV9a.jpg)|![20260528_220624.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23xAgMc1gURgbCcYW54rBxzsc1pmqs42UzxoiPVRFurvrWP8yHnPnSuJW4fEJCttWh5f9.jpg)|![20260528_220941.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wCNkBJeXMrL74ajreW3RvEVCfmn6hxTtj3RTdbQADk4ivmfC1MDSmHQuSTboeVTba5j.jpg)|![20260528_221259.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23xVW8a7ozCGq1UBN7ec66rdtNWkNnY9YMncozYSveik9DuGUYXQpCmZ4LZGMkE5tqWwe.jpg)|
|-|-|-|-|

•✨️🩵Para culminar voy a coser un ruedo ondeado doblando la tela y cosiendo con costura de zigzag mientras voy estirando para hacer mas ondas luego voy a coser las trenzas y voy a meter estas en la orilla de la abertura con la ayuda de un gancho.


|![20260528_222641.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wMm7mwPSWfUug3pBStLafTRePNBGrtA7PNQypfF7w6Rex6XtyauXgFnLy83tuww8ksR.jpg)|![20260528_223316.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23xAkMwLHzUJ3YJrFbVDnGeC5gjkTSo9b4kLDNiPjKbNrnfnCAHrfKXk1oGPMQRL5ub42.jpg)|![20260528_223851.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23x1HMxzaFBch2zquEBkcHfjUpvfWMuCekGtzaDKtwZVW52GJevjYa4DeikSR7qJWBkwU.jpg)|
|-|-|-|




 <center>
![Dark Blue Elegant 3d Illustration Geometric Learn Trading LinkedIn Banner_20250330_124152_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EoeD4ZNgLbMwf6foVN9TvcTR2CCdYQJJPKp8r3Apm8DiLibcp5p5kc4GFqRFkLP4bJU.png)
</center>

Es una blusa muy linda y sencilla la verdad me encanto demasiado 😍 me alegro mucho haber compartido este pequeño espacio dedicado a la costura con todos ustedes saludos a todos y muy buenas noches 💕. 

![20260528_225051.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wC5Ai1Kg7vchq7TiZa2ecSbeRjeX8d8XrFgp63NTVnkjnv7PQEcH5QjKWoHQ5wfFkL7.jpg)

![20260528_225040.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wqe4je5uiFP4xTLWDTqqfBH4FgxyCzCpfr89NoafZAJrZiEeouhDcDUWiUsi14qnbqi.jpg)

![20260528_225032.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wMSHtYL9fBUVts1Lk73dodDZwYSZgXA2mVMVd5JBSLmGmJrTspRrNHXX1kuq2tokvrV.jpg)



![Dark Blue Elegant 3d Illustration Geometric Learn Trading LinkedIn Banner_20250330_125045_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EogLTkcA4KmHft4JF8jVTTFSkqG3xH7LXanTqYqm2Uj5N18eX3AaFxk87jpHWKysitL.png)

<center>![Dark Blue Elegant 3d Illustration Geometric Learn Trading LinkedIn Banner_20250330_124403_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EoeD4ZNg21ofBWfyTJjE9oxYDN5E6NqrhcvfrPEpEDeZxXFhRvwbEP9xhStTF9kzZ83.png)</center>

Hello my dear Hive friends ❤️ Good evening everyone, I hope you are all doing well and enjoying this lovely night 🤗 Today I wanted to share with you my most recent sewing project: a beautiful aquamarine blouse with a lovely detail on the sleeves, perfect for a casual occasion because of its comfortable design 🤗 I invite you to join me in each and every step.

![PhotoCollage_1780095588764.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EpxqqpP2hUkXQefeWEVD6bNDbuKmUorYYRBCgRAMrwSWGUxjKiW6mrV7AGUDeSMYemF.jpg)
<center>![Dark Blue Elegant 3d Illustration Geometric Learn Trading LinkedIn Banner_20250330_124521_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EoeD4ZNgLsZrviZqdPsH7xDD7uLcVT8ok3iUD5LtWPJXPUQsgVdrTxMmpRxXsXRS4hF.png)</center> 

• 🧵Sewing machine 
• ✂️Scissors 
• 🧵Sewing thread 
• ✂️Fabric 
• 🧵Needle N°9



 <center>![Dark Blue Elegant 3d Illustration Geometric Learn Trading LinkedIn Banner_20250330_124734_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EoeDQzxM1SGG8LqXYo2qXvLmwwH3hFcVRwvaA6yn2xJbP35dAMJXKMysNWoBF9EaQtY.png)</center>

•✨️🩵As a first step, I'm going to cut all the pieces for my blouse: a back piece, a front piece (both with sleeves), the collar, the opening hem, and the drawstrings for the braids. 

|![20260527_201913.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23vsScckpG2RBHsVXR69Laua5sZwHY2D6kTVXu6sdaDm42jKM9mRrXWBjzYscoWUhaX6F.jpg)|![20260527_201919.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wCE27aGwc4oZiRhT9SymYgj8Wq67R6niJHSbVguZRdCRVQuYfzEXKr9Gsdpa3uppGZE.jpg)|
|-|-|
•✨️🩵I'll then join the back and front pieces at the edges with a straight stitch and a zigzag stitch to secure them. Next, I'll sew the top of the shoulders together with a straight stitch and a zigzag stitch to secure them. 
|![20260527_212854.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wCLgA9saj1arUar4BaEiMMWparQMpUUQau8YRrm8H6XobGwZqw2X2ozoDPHAgoFvBHr.jpg)|![20260527_213147.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23xetmr3LKwqM1NRYs7jFhxxLXTJxYZKMySQbfm2rK98e82iLvep8Dvubpf1nF9U62cJT.jpg)|![20260527_213644.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23vsb8fCr9uPQ77xGcJ1namSRaicefhgYkdDgEjhGYgiTcuAEcX5aeztzrcXt4CAiZkjy.jpg)|![20260527_213751.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23vscuqVYXgbB9tiWbe6Ly78NjmG3b5uNpAsrVL7enFgZ2qd8cf7Xrnwgk2Yh1zBPiV5M.jpg)|
|-|-|-|-|


•✨️🩵Then I'll fold the neckline hem and place it on the right side of the fabric. I'll sew it with a straight stitch and a zigzag stitch to secure it. Finally, I'll sew the remaining shoulder seam with a straight stitch and a zigzag stitch to secure it.
|![20260527_214312.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23ywwUjCUTDtRQEnMxt1o5gHtu5KKpmEB5wmzDEmXRMJb1HZ6e4vvt89HHivf7gmeXEAU.jpg)|![20260527_214725.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wX9zC2LEc7Ai328JmHnAMer3uLenovj3F6STSG43dAfabxL6ofYnsa1iGZN2yovJfbW.jpg)|![20260527_224041.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wXA9NQpdfjBJv5eexVV2bow1nSeriMoVchzee5zrTAEeL3TWeYGTraTGxM1Gk2TDdJR.jpg)|![20260527_224240.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23viCDKr1oUadgf3n87Bcv3hMiQ6RHjvkAWZduXqp8rX4g55gQskCiA8fHFXY8pMNpDUn.jpg)|
|-|-|-|-|


•✨️🩵I'm going to fold the hem of my opening and sew a small hem. Then I'll sew the sleeve hem, fold that hem over, and sew it along the right side of the fabric with a straight stitch and a zigzag stitch to secure it. 
|![20260528_220513.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23xL9KaUf6yFccFm6GP3hZAt11YdmcmStv8cBNSjpYbwo97s4HBfAR95EEqFeFbKMbV9a.jpg)|![20260528_220624.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23xAgMc1gURgbCcYW54rBxzsc1pmqs42UzxoiPVRFurvrWP8yHnPnSuJW4fEJCttWh5f9.jpg)|![20260528_220941.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wCNkBJeXMrL74ajreW3RvEVCfmn6hxTtj3RTdbQADk4ivmfC1MDSmHQuSTboeVTba5j.jpg)|![20260528_221259.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23xVW8a7ozCGq1UBN7ec66rdtNWkNnY9YMncozYSveik9DuGUYXQpCmZ4LZGMkE5tqWwe.jpg)|
|-|-|-|-|


•✨️🩵To finish, I'm going to sew a scalloped hem by folding the fabric and sewing with a zigzag stitch while stretching it to create more waves. Then I'll sew the braids and tuck them into the opening with a hook.

|![20260528_222641.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wMm7mwPSWfUug3pBStLafTRePNBGrtA7PNQypfF7w6Rex6XtyauXgFnLy83tuww8ksR.jpg)|![20260528_223316.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23xAkMwLHzUJ3YJrFbVDnGeC5gjkTSo9b4kLDNiPjKbNrnfnCAHrfKXk1oGPMQRL5ub42.jpg)|![20260528_223851.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23x1HMxzaFBch2zquEBkcHfjUpvfWMuCekGtzaDKtwZVW52GJevjYa4DeikSR7qJWBkwU.jpg)|
|-|-|-|



<center>![Dark Blue Elegant 3d Illustration Geometric Learn Trading LinkedIn Banner_20250330_124945_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EoeD4ZYmGMcA1CW4Rjb37hbEFRKYdA8eaJ5Hb6LesXz16fMLJLcPWrUhe54zA22QQuk.png)</center> 

It's a very pretty and simple blouse, I really loved it 😍 I'm so glad to have shared this little space dedicated to sewing with all of you. Greetings to everyone and good night 💕.

![20260528_225051.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wC5Ai1Kg7vchq7TiZa2ecSbeRjeX8d8XrFgp63NTVnkjnv7PQEcH5QjKWoHQ5wfFkL7.jpg)

![20260528_225040.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wqe4je5uiFP4xTLWDTqqfBH4FgxyCzCpfr89NoafZAJrZiEeouhDcDUWiUsi14qnbqi.jpg)

![20260528_225032.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/23wMSHtYL9fBUVts1Lk73dodDZwYSZgXA2mVMVd5JBSLmGmJrTspRrNHXX1kuq2tokvrV.jpg)

![Dark Blue Elegant 3d Illustration Geometric Learn Trading LinkedIn Banner_20250330_125158_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/selenediva/EogLpCBq42Ros62UDdV6Umi2UPR2EZpvGzCKTebL3UiFWy7omcUYmWKZaDWAeE2sbMd.png)

title.title: Wall Art at K-Town, Festive Walk Parade
title.body:
![vvodjiu (5).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vvodjiu/48PTPzovEQdfr9y2rNdxzCPVL4HfCt7cYe6vxxhmKwCYEBsZQ41pTeAyoUi1t6Qh6j.png)

I've shared how colorful the Kaleidoscope canopy and the flower pots in Festive Walk are. Now, I am going to share the wall art I've seen around K-Town.

---
---

Before entering K-Town, you'll notice the colorful pathways. It's creatively inviting to my eyes. 😍


![IMG_20260528_111056.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vvodjiu/23wqEePuJyrZStvS5cccrz23cQQKo2DNo3nvaojH5hPEw6tk2KDar5FkMfY1mFDJucMqj.jpg)


Upon entering, you'll see the colorful and vibrant flower pots, the wooden benches and tables, and the fragrant flowers under the colorful kaleidoscope canopy.
Check the photos here from my previous post 👉 [My Vibrant Afternoon Walk: Discovering the New Colors of the Festive Walk Parade 🌈](https://peakd.com/hive-155530/@vvodjiu/my-vibrant-afternoon-walk-discovering)

But on the hidden side of the vibrant street, there lie the colorful pieces of art.

This first picture is one of the first wall arts here at Festive Walk. It was made back in 2021 by the local young artists in Iloilo City.
\

means City of Love, which Iloilo City is known for.


![IMG_20260528_112300.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vvodjiu/EoiVh15ZMSvKcRTJDyise4Du1JMaoeoD1gs9fV3KF6ojo3BUXCXY4124bL8VbiwVLH5.jpg)

---
---

Next is the K-Drama mural. Ilonggos are known for their love of K-pop and K-dramas. This is a fusion of some popular K-dramas, like Squid Game, Crash Landing on You, and more. This was made by artist Joel Dadivas Jr.



![IMG_20260528_111858.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vvodjiu/Eq9UMPC29qUBsYKzwyhVrykwXrUhDyFtQoGzr56nz8gVM6S1ubeFxTGMC8R4xxaU5fb.jpg)

---
---

This last photo is another artwork made by Joel Dadivas Jr.
It shows Korean cultural symbols like lotus flowers and hanbok.


![IMG_20260528_111830.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vvodjiu/EowFAnPgcca5RpuCaY5zoQr76pPb4E4WBThAKfR6qdQRdNBxFMVRBKtPmvxnQg9SoWd.jpg)


All these paintings show how Ilonggos appreciate Korean culture. K-Town is a place where you can experience Korea in Iloilo City. 💜


---
---

title.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQme418DUhnhtZPchpzsYUvJTJF5zmPXUfYDZov8wEKS2K6/1780113936056.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUn5KGRge2fLP6oYBvFR337hsBAFwq4HDpzX5j71nADnT/1780114048609.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVwPwH5j6zLsLkF5ZFFqW89jMGA6tiNghgHjX8518xY18/1780114048652.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmT1L3Dnh3ugemrQd8QLAjNuu9qDRKY5Frt1G1qUgpGxm2/1780114048701.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWbjqxZEqjypYYdT3HJo2BrYtHHHzZePBU4xgaWQdEA6z/1780114048745.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcd2ynYCiisVqmBQM58woUbTsncwBkKs51Gta4nAvrfdR/1780114048778.jpg)

Visitar El Mirador de Caripe siempre es un reencuentro con la paz. Al llegar a las alturas de este hermoso rincón del estado Monagas, lo primero que te atrapa es la imponente presencia de sus montañas. Un horizonte infinito pintado de verdes intensos que se superponen entre la neblina y la brisa fresca. Estar allí, bajo la sombra de la vegetación, es una invitación directa a detener el tiempo y contemplar la inmensidad a través del lente.

Visiting El Mirador de Caripe is always a reunion with peace. Upon reaching the heights of this beautiful corner of Monagas state, the first thing that catches you is the imposing presence of its mountains. An infinite horizon painted in intense greens that overlap between the mist and the fresh breeze. Being there, under the shade of the vegetation, is a direct invitation to freeze time and contemplate the immensity through the lens.

​<center>🌿 • 🍃 • ⛰️ • 🍃 • 🌿</center>

Pero la montaña no está sola; está profundamente viva. Durante mi recorrido, la paciencia fotográfica tuvo su recompensa al encontrarme con algunos de los pequeños habitantes del lugar. Lograr capturar la chispa de la vida silvestre en su entorno natural, justo en el momento exacto, le da un sentido único a la jornada. Son esos instantes fortuitos los que llenan de dinamismo una fotografía de paisaje.

But the mountain is not alone; it is deeply alive. During my walk, photographic patience had its reward when I encountered some of the local small inhabitants. Managing to capture the spark of wildlife in its natural environment, right at the exact moment, gives a unique meaning to the day. It is those fortuitous moments that fill a landscape photograph with dynamism.

​<center>🌿 • 🍃 • ⛰️ • 🍃 • 🌿</center>

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYR36ss68jNe1KvVYmcA9EjTF7FnYjNT6B5W2YHBpiQg5/1780114215469.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNqGjZF4TG84s47s2hY85M9Y7WEkErUCuC26FARQr5T92/1780114215528.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRZaTzWzQqX2uXJtXsXn6QqFQXibytfd2QHBLWHwJjVQh/1780114215588.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPqrjdNW9uMUX89iUVrmZ5m8VUdjQHr9dpSCRnUNiRS9y/1780114215639.jpg

​<center>🌿 • 🍃 • ⛰️ • 🍃 • 🌿</center>

Para cerrar con broche de oro, la sutil belleza de la flora local se hizo presente. Caripe es tierra fértil, y entre tanta vegetación frondosa siempre brotan pequeños destellos de color. Me detuve a capturar los detalles de las flores que adornan el mirador; texturas delicadas que contrastan perfectamente con la rudeza de las cumbres y que nos recuerdan la hermosa fragilidad de la naturaleza.

To close with a flourish, the subtle beauty of the local flora was present. Caripe is a fertile land, and among so much lush vegetation, small flashes of color always sprout. I stopped to capture the details of the flowers that decorate the viewpoint; delicate textures that contrast perfectly with the roughness of the summits and remind us of the beautiful fragility of nature.

​<center>🌿 • 🍃 • ⛰️ • 🍃 • 🌿</center>

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaLonkNGbr6xq2gvdgZAvL7Q9c8jY3ZoZKvSYpw9j5u1g/1780114330790.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfS68yU4CvYreudtqiQj29HEU3q6etetF7iasrfdoyHyt/1780114330834.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRK8LDnqvm9pUUVCP663fkKrRBsBZbw93iwtpkCpGReav/1780114330872.jpg)

​<center>🌿 • 🍃 • ⛰️ • 🍃 • 🌿</center>

Hacer este recorrido fotográfico me recordó que la naturaleza siempre encuentra la manera de sorprendernos, ya sea con la inmensidad de una cumbre o con el sutil color de un pétalo. Espero que hayan disfrutado de este paseo visual tanto como yo disfruté capturándolo. ¿Cuál de estos tres elementos es su favorito a la hora de fotografiar: los grandes paisajes, los animales o los detalles de las flores? Me encantaría leer sus comentarios. ¡Nos vemos en la próxima publicación!

Taking this photographic journey reminded me that nature always finds a way to surprise us, whether with the immensity of a summit or the subtle color of a petal. I hope you enjoyed this visual tour as much as I enjoyed capturing it. Which of these three elements is your favorite to photograph: grand landscapes, animals, or flower details? I would love to read your comments. See you in the next post!

​<center>🌿 • 🍃 • ⛰️ • 🍃 • 🌿</center>

(Todas las imágenes son de mi autoria)

title.title: The House Also Speaks #2 | Things get tired too [EN / ES]
title.body:
🇬🇧 **English Version**

Hello dear Holos & Lotus community,

Today I want to continue this personal series called *The House Also Speaks*, where everyday spaces and objects slowly become reflections about life, exhaustion, memories, and the emotional weight that homes silently accumulate over time.

---

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmc3KuSiMooJEqgYAnvECunPnjfdKUYk13JtT13S9ygTZX/antonio_luis_fan_5375135_640.jpg)
Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/fan-old-one-iron-vintage-5375135/)

---

## The House Also Speaks #2
*Things get tired too*

There are moments when it feels as if the whole house starts giving up at the same time.

First it was the fan.

It had already been making strange noises for months, but one learns to live with those sounds. In homes like ours, things rarely stop working suddenly. Usually they begin warning us little by little. A different vibration. A slower movement. A noise that becomes part of the routine until one day it finally stops.

Then the chair broke.

One of its legs suddenly gave way and the entire chair collapsed to one side with a dry sound that somehow felt bigger than it really was. For a few seconds nobody even spoke. Maybe because lately every broken thing carries a weight larger than the object itself.

After that came the television.
First the large one.
Then the small one.

And honestly, there comes a point where one no longer feels surprise. Only exhaustion.

As if the house itself had become tired.

As if every object had silently agreed to go on strike at the same time.

The refrigerator was the worst part.

Not because it was the newest thing in the house, but because some objects stop being simple appliances and become necessities that sustain daily life. We tried to repair it several times. We cleaned it, checked cables, waited for it to start cooling again, listened to every strange sound with hope.

But it kept failing.

And eventually we had to do something we did not want to do:
use the emergency savings to buy another refrigerator just to survive until the old one can hopefully be repaired someday.

I think what hurts the most is not even the money itself.

It is the emotional exhaustion that comes with constantly solving problems.

Because life already feels difficult enough.

The prices.
The blackouts.
The uncertainty.
The heat.
The endless worries.

And then suddenly the fan stops working.
Or a chair breaks.
Or the refrigerator dies.

And something inside you quietly breaks a little too.

There are days when I walk through the house and look at the old objects differently. The appliances, the furniture, the patched things repaired many times over the years.

And I realize they resemble us more than we would like to admit.

They continue functioning despite the wear.
Despite the pressure.
Despite the years.
Despite carrying more weight than they were designed to hold.

Sometimes I think entire families survive exactly like that:
through repairs.

Small emotional repairs.
Financial repairs.
Mental repairs.
Improvised solutions for problems that never fully disappear.

Maybe that is why every new breakdown feels heavier than it should.
Because people are not only repairing objects anymore.

They are also trying to repair their own peace of mind.

And still, somehow, we continue.

We keep finding ways.
Keep improvising.
Keep fixing what can still be fixed.

Maybe that is one of the saddest and strongest things about ordinary people:
even exhausted, they continue holding the house together.

Sometimes barely.
But still standing.

---

Thank you for reading.
Special thanks to @bradleyarrow for supporting the community.

---

Photos: Pixabay  
English translation: DeepL Translate

---

🇪🇸 **En Español**

Hola querida comunidad de Holos & Lotus,

Hoy quiero continuar esta serie personal llamada *La casa también habla*, donde los espacios y objetos cotidianos terminan convirtiéndose poco a poco en reflexiones sobre la vida, el cansancio, los recuerdos y el peso emocional que las casas van acumulando en silencio con el paso de los años.

---

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmc3KuSiMooJEqgYAnvECunPnjfdKUYk13JtT13S9ygTZX/antonio_luis_fan_5375135_640.jpg)
Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/fan-old-one-iron-vintage-5375135/)

---


## La casa también habla #2
*Las cosas también se cansan*

Hay momentos en que una siente que la casa entera empieza a rendirse al mismo tiempo.

Primero fue el ventilador.

Ya llevaba meses haciendo ruidos extraños, pero una aprende a convivir con esos sonidos. En casas como la nuestra las cosas rara vez dejan de funcionar de golpe. Generalmente empiezan avisando poco a poco. Una vibración diferente. Un movimiento más lento. Un ruido que termina formando parte de la rutina hasta que un día simplemente se detiene.

Después se rompió la silla.

Una de las patas cedió de repente y la silla completa cayó hacia un lado con un sonido seco que de alguna manera se sintió más grande de lo que realmente era. Durante unos segundos nadie habló. Tal vez porque últimamente cada cosa rota trae un peso mucho mayor que el propio objeto.

Después vino el televisor.
Primero el grande.
Luego el pequeño.

Y sinceramente, llega un punto donde una ya ni siquiera siente sorpresa. Solo cansancio.

Como si la casa misma estuviera agotada.

Como si todos los objetos se hubieran puesto de acuerdo para declararse en huelga al mismo tiempo.

Lo del refrigerador fue lo peor.

No porque fuera lo más nuevo de la casa, sino porque hay objetos que dejan de ser simples aparatos y se convierten en necesidades que sostienen la vida diaria. Intentamos arreglarlo varias veces. Lo limpiamos, revisamos cables, esperamos que volviera a enfriar, escuchamos cada ruido extraño con esperanza.

Pero seguía fallando.

Y al final tuvimos que hacer algo que no queríamos:
usar los ahorros de emergencia para comprar otra nevera y resolver mientras la vieja logra arreglarse algún día.

Creo que lo que más agota no es ni siquiera el dinero.

Es el cansancio emocional que produce vivir resolviendo problemas constantemente.

Porque la vida ya se siente suficientemente difícil.

Los precios.
Los apagones.
La incertidumbre.
El calor.
Las preocupaciones interminables.

Y entonces de pronto se rompe el ventilador.
O se parte una silla.
O deja de funcionar el refrigerador.

Y algo dentro de una también se rompe un poco.

Hay días en que camino por la casa y miro diferente los objetos viejos. Los equipos, los muebles, las cosas remendadas muchas veces durante años.

Y me doy cuenta de que se parecen más a nosotros de lo que quisiéramos admitir.

Siguen funcionando a pesar del desgaste.
A pesar de la presión.
A pesar de los años.
A pesar de cargar más peso del que fueron diseñados para soportar.

A veces pienso que muchas familias sobreviven exactamente así:
a base de reparaciones.

Pequeñas reparaciones emocionales.
Reparaciones económicas.
Reparaciones mentales.
Soluciones improvisadas para problemas que nunca terminan de desaparecer.

Tal vez por eso cada nueva rotura se siente más pesada de lo que debería.
Porque las personas ya no solamente están reparando objetos.

También están intentando reparar su propia tranquilidad.

Y aun así, de alguna manera, seguimos.

Seguimos inventando.
Seguimos improvisando.
Seguimos arreglando lo que todavía puede salvarse.

Quizás esa sea una de las cosas más tristes y más fuertes de la gente común:
incluso agotada, sigue sosteniendo la casa.

A veces apenas.
Pero todavía de pie.

---

title.body:
![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/c4e0b645-2e4d-489a-8003-14944f135f5a.jpg) Ok. This picture is from yesterday when I didn't post. It was just a super long travel day. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/a688762e-ea34-4764-ad39-4402045a423b.jpg)![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/69be78fc-8641-4fe2-97fb-458a536fb044.jpg) We left at 8am UK time which is about 12 at night in Canada. Easy to catch a bus and quite comfy also. Bus leaves every 12 minutes and only takes 30 min to the airport. Easy. Getting through the terminal was chaotic with very long lines to get through security screening. You can pay for fast track but I hate spending on things if I don't have to. But that coca cola in the picture? ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/37486674-cb8b-4457-827f-411c234825d5.jpg) $7.15 CAD out about $4.50 HBD and my wife's coffee was even more. Ugh. As for getting into the plane? Super busy with long line ups and stairs to get into the plane. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/2b3957f9-0686-4aa6-9e6b-d90649ec1e2e.jpg) Then it was 8 hours to Calgary and a quick switch of plans and another 90 minutes to home. When I arrive my body clock says 11pm but the local time says 3pm. But I have a sore back, blistered feet and a long time until I can sleep. So I unpack my clothes. I go by the pharmacy. And try to stay up at 9pm but that's like 5am body clock. Ugh.. ... But I got to sleep at 8pm (4am body clock) and slept for almost 8 hours. How did I get my steps? Absolutely no idea. I didn't sightsee, I don't work, but I guess walking around the airport and rushing between gates so I guess it was enough. Why am I saying it's a build the baseline in the title? Mostly because I weighed myself after the trip to get my weight and I can see how I can lose some pounds. Also my fingers get in pretty rough shape in the pharmacy where I work tomorrow. However with the 3 weeks off they are in virtually perfect shape. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/d2a82e56-6294-46ee-af86-fff3534260a6.jpg)![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/4ea8cd0c-d0a8-4444-9bf5-05c13cb64f39.jpg) So .. took a picture to show before I work and later I will do after. If my fingers get sorry looking and painful I am certain. But I'm falling asleep in the chair and my phone is near death. I'll leave it at that for today. Thanks for dropping by

body.title: Kepler’s Laws of Planetary Motion
body.body:
[![](https://hotipfs-3speak-1.b-cdn.net/ipfs/QmdU1V8Eefmv5E77Ct6hNG8A3f9b75dZmVS6ZVvw5ynnrn/)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=mes/c3b94a80)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=mes/c3b94a80)


---

In this video, I go over Johannes Kepler's three laws of planetary motion and derive them using Isaac Newton's second law of motion, F = m a, and his law on universal gravitation. While observing the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe's astronomical observations, Kepler observed recurring patterns in the data, which he formulated as three laws:

1. A planet revolves around the sun in an elliptical orbit with the sun at one focus.
2. The line joining the sun to a planet sweeps out equal areas in equal times.
3. The square of the period of revolution of a planet is proportional to the cube of the length of the major axis of its orbit.

Isaac Newton later realized that Kepler's laws are merely the biproduct of his 2nd law of motion and his law on universal gravitation. I use Newton’s laws to derive Kepler's laws, while making extensive use of vector functions, calculus, and the polar equation of an ellipse.

Later in the video, I calculate the distance a satellite needs to be from the equator of the Earth to have a geosynchronous orbit, in which the orbit of the satellite around the Earth is in sync with Earth's rotation. This type of orbit is sometimes referred to as the Arthur C. Clarke orbit, named after the famous author of 2001: A Space Odyssey, who popularized the orbit in a fictional novel in 1945. I also go over some very interesting connections surrounding Arthur C. Clarke, so buckle up! 

#math #vectors #calculus #astronomy #keplerslaws

body.title: The Renaissance the the USA Didn't Want You to Know About - 02-18-2020 - 10X Speed
body.body:
[![](https://images.3speak.tv/images/1780113833981-3530f28b4fd9b5be.webp)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=davidnollearth/4e24c9da)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=davidnollearth/4e24c9da)


---

This is the video series for an oil painting 'Wisteria' I did from 2016-2020.  The painting was destroyed in 2021 due to a number of reasons, but mainly: the painting's faulty experimental linseed-epoxide substrait, Covid-19 crushing lockdowns, extreme poverty, family attacks and ongoing US government (Big Tech + Big Media) censorship of me and my 30 years of artwork.

Its not ideal to not be able to show this piece, but I still gained the knowledge of how to do it and invented several useful oil painting mediums & varnishes used in its creation which never yellowed and still cannot be bought anywhere.

I am posting these videos for posterity and for people that are interested in seeing an oil painting created from start to finish in the Baroque style evolved for the 21st century.  I also must have deleted some of the initial videos when I did the quick underpainting, but what still exists, I give to you.

I hope this can be an educational experience as no gallery will show any of my controversial art even today.

---

body.title: La ciencia de lo cotidiano #2. El cerebro se acostumbra incluso al caos. [Esp/Eng]
body.body:
🇪🇸 En Español
---

¡Hola, querida comunidad de Holos-Lotus!   
Hoy quiero compartir una de esas experiencias que no se olvidan fácilmente… no por lo extraordinario del hecho en sí, sino por lo que revela sobre la mente humana cuando el entorno se desordena por completo.

---

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVwo6pgvY9Xx3rqnQixq5w2F7xuDQPu1qi1RR6LfuQkd3/engin_akyurt_surgery_3034133_640.jpg)
Fuente[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/surgery-hospital-doctor-operation-3034133/)

---

#  **La ciencia de lo cotidiano #2**  
### *El cerebro se acostumbra incluso al caos*

---

Muchas veces, en la sala de emergencias, he presenciado situaciones que llevan al límite incluso a quienes están acostumbrados a trabajar bajo presión.

Momentos donde todo parece ocurrir al mismo tiempo.  
Donde las decisiones no esperan.  
Donde el aire cambia de densidad.

---

Recuerdo especialmente un episodio que ocurrió hace algún tiempo.

Un paciente ingresó en estado crítico tras un altercado violento.  
Se trataba de una **emergencia médica**, donde cada minuto era determinante.

El ambiente ya era tenso desde el inicio.

---

Mientras el equipo médico intentaba estabilizar al paciente, ocurrió algo que elevó aún más la tensión del momento.

La persona con la que había tenido el conflicto inicial llegó al hospital.

---

Había logrado entrar en un descuido de seguridad.

Y en cuestión de segundos, el entorno que ya era crítico se convirtió en un escenario de caos.

---

Gritos.  
Confusión.  
Movimiento inesperado del personal.  
Decisiones rápidas tomadas casi sin tiempo para pensar.

En situaciones como esta, el tiempo deja de percibirse de forma lineal. Se vuelve fragmentado, casi elástico. Cada segundo parece contener múltiples decisiones al mismo tiempo, y sin embargo rara vez existe el espacio para procesarlas de manera individual. Lo que queda es el instinto moldeado por la experiencia, y una especie de disciplina interna que permite continuar actuando incluso cuando el entorno es inestable.

---

Sin embargo, lo que más me llamó la atención no fue el desorden.

Sino la forma en que algunas personas reaccionaron dentro de él.

---

Entre ellas, un médico de mucha experiencia, alguien a quien conocía bien, mantuvo una calma que parecía casi ajena a la situación.

No elevó la voz.  
No se dejó arrastrar por el entorno.  
No perdió el foco del paciente.

---

De forma casi silenciosa, logró contener la situación, calmar al agresor y reorganizar la atención del equipo.

Todo mientras se continuaba trabajando sobre la vida del paciente.

---

Y algo importante ocurrió en ese momento.

El caos seguía existiendo… pero dejó de dominar la escena.

---

El paciente pudo ser estabilizado.  
La situación se controló.  
Y el sistema, de alguna forma, volvió a encontrar orden dentro del desorden.

---

Años después, sigo pensando en ese momento.

No solo por lo que ocurrió externamente, sino por lo que revela internamente.

---

El cerebro humano tiene una capacidad sorprendente para adaptarse.

Incluso en entornos donde, en teoría, no debería ser posible la calma.

---

Lo que para alguien externo es caos absoluto, para quien está entrenado puede convertirse en un tipo de orden funcional.

No porque el caos desaparezca…  
sino porque la mente aprende a no dejarse arrastrar por él.

---

Y quizás ahí está una de las cosas más complejas de la medicina y de la vida:

no siempre se trata de eliminar el desorden,  
sino de aprender a pensar dentro de él.

---

Al final, hay personas que no sobreviven al caos…  
sino que aprenden a atravesarlo sin perder lo esencial.

---

Las imágenes son de Pixabay y la traducción al inglés fue realizada usando DeepL Translate.

---

🇬🇧 English Version
---

Hello, dear Holos-Lotus community! 
Today I want to share one of those experiences that are not easily forgotten… not because of the event itself, but because of what it reveals about the human mind when everything around it falls into complete disorder.

---

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVwo6pgvY9Xx3rqnQixq5w2F7xuDQPu1qi1RR6LfuQkd3/engin_akyurt_surgery_3034133_640.jpg)
Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/surgery-hospital-doctor-operation-3034133/)

---


# **The Science of Everyday Life #2**  
### *The Brain Gets Used to Chaos, Too*

---

Many times in the emergency room, I have witnessed situations that push even experienced professionals to their limits.

Moments where everything seems to happen at once.  
Where decisions cannot wait.  
Where the air itself feels different.

---

I especially remember one episode that occurred some time ago.

A patient arrived in critical condition after a violent altercation.  
It was a **medical emergency**, where every minute mattered.

The atmosphere was already tense from the beginning.

---

While the medical team was working to stabilize the patient, something happened that escalated the situation even further.

The person involved in the initial conflict arrived at the hospital.

---

He had managed to enter during a lapse in security.

And within seconds, what was already a critical medical scenario turned into complete chaos.

---

Shouting.  
Confusion.  
Sudden movement from staff.  
Fast decisions made under extreme pressure.

In situations like this, time does not feel linear. It becomes fragmented, almost elastic. Every second carries multiple decisions at once, and yet there is rarely space to process them individually. What remains is instinct shaped by experience, and a kind of internal discipline that allows action to continue even when the environment is unstable.

---

However, what stood out to me was not the disorder itself.

But how some people behaved within it.

---

Among them, a highly experienced doctor I knew well remained remarkably calm, as if untouched by the surrounding chaos.

He did not raise his voice.  
He did not lose focus on the patient.  
He did not allow the situation to take control of him.

---

Almost silently, he managed to contain the disruption, calm the aggressor, and restore enough order for the medical team to continue working.

All of this while the patient was still being treated.

---

And something important became clear in that moment.

The chaos was still present… but it no longer controlled the scene.

---

The patient was eventually stabilized.  
The situation was brought under control.  
And somehow, order returned within disorder.

---

Years later, I still think about that moment.

Not only because of what happened externally, but because of what it reveals internally.

---

The human brain has an extraordinary ability to adapt.

Even in environments where, in theory, calm should not be possible.

---

What appears as absolute chaos to an outsider can become a functional form of order to someone who is trained to operate within it.

Not because the chaos disappears…  
but because the mind learns not to be ruled by it.

---

And perhaps this is one of the most complex aspects of medicine and life:

it is not always about eliminating disorder,  
but about learning how to think within it.

---

In the end, there are people who do not survive chaos…  
but learn how to move through it without losing what matters most.

---

*Be your own bank.*

It's something I put in my Hive bio when I first started on Hive, and for me, it remains the number one rule. Being your own bank means different things to different people. For some of us, it means having a handful of silver coins or small gold bars stashed away at home.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmagnGM1g6prmAmsQkU6pnJcQ5gWrL57ocviDH61L383ae/1780113872617.jpg) (Created by @fonestreet and modified with ChatGPT)

For others, it means growing their assets on Hive. Lately, I’ve been trying to find the balance between these two worlds. On one hand, I have my conviction with metals. It’s no secret that I love physical silver and gold. There’s something about holding a real ounce in your hand that simply can’t be replicated on a screen. Plus, there’s no counterparty risk. No one can freeze it with a click, and it doesn’t depend on the internet or electricity working.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcrHpzJCHc24smbCARKr8YHqL1Lf29f6tVenyDjUNq15C/1780114043639.jpg) (Created by @fonestreet and modified with ChatGPT)

Let’s be honest. Physical metal has its limits. It doesn’t generate returns. A silver coin stored in my safe today will still be the same coin ten years from now, and it’s not going to multiply on its own.

That’s where Hive comes in.

I’ve been paying close attention to HBD savings. The 12% interest is something no traditional bank will ever offer you. It’s digital money that works for you every day, and the liquidity to withdraw it is pretty fast.

So, what’s the plan? Lately, I don’t see them as rivals, but as teammates.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXCctvNRqHkf6Ho5R7hr3pfzxH32pEGWUqTjEdN3Fiwnv/1780114295960.jpg) (Created by @fonestreet and modified with ChatGPT)

My strategy has been pretty simple. I use the rewards from my content on Hive and what I earn here to feed my HBD savings. It’s an excellent way to build up a liquid fund that grows on its own. When that digital fund grows enough, I like to take a portion and \

it into something I can touch by buying metals. This way the digital world gives me growth and speed, while the physical world gives me the anchor of absolute security for the future. **I’m curious to hear how you approach it. Do you prefer to keep as much as possible in physical metals, or do you feel more comfortable letting your HBD work in savings?** ![1000017156.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulliontools/23uEyyyWCHidcDUBLiCySb4thnoMosshmypAS8GVUkhHC52LCiQqrB6L9Fom29shmtCMN.gif)

现在进入自主复习阶段，这段日子算是我近来最轻松的时光了。每天上午按照学校排好的课时值守课堂，下午定点摆摊答疑。学生在教室内学习，有问题便走出教室，我在室外当场为他们解答。不过我也没有闲着，趁着答疑的空档，把学生手头的八套高考真题全部做完了，这样学生提问时我能直接作答，不用临时翻看题目，节省不少时间。

昨天组织学生进行考前保温训练，要求限时完成两篇作文。晚上批改作业时，我发现不少知识点他们都没掌握，写作水平甚至还有所退步。距离高考只剩短短几天，暴露的问题却不少：基础词汇拼写错误，审题、文体把握不准，语言表达也过于中式化。能明显看出，这段时间学生一心忙着刷题，并没有踏实背诵作文内容。

连续三天我都在室外摆摊答疑，午后天气十分闷热。学生在有空调的教室里复习，我们在外值守如同蒸汗蒸一般。好在年级组贴心地为老师们准备了水果，也算给大家消暑解乏。

这几天主动前来问我问题的学生寥寥无几，来的也大多是阅读、语法填空这类知识性题目。几乎没有人主动把写好的作文交来批改，就连梳理写作提纲的同学都少见。由此也能直观看出学生当下的复习状态与整体规划。

今早的早自习，我着重明确了后期复习的重点内容，并讲评了这两篇作文，梳理了写作相关知识点。长期疏于练习，不少学生暴露出诸多问题：卷面书写潦草、段落划分不合理、行文逻辑混乱，内容也难以做到具体展开。他们还是得强化应用文审题，精准把握文体、梳理要点，学会从多个角度构思行文。

后续我还会不断督促学生加强背诵，做到找准文体、理清要点、多角度思考。虽说现阶段是自主复习，但不少学生缺少合理规划，复习时东翻西看、毫无头绪，效率偏低。高考临近，更要引导他们抓紧时间，提升复习效率。

说实话，我心里还是很担忧的。单看这两篇作文，能明显感觉到学生的写作能力下滑得很快。下周还有两次保温训练，希望渐入佳境啊，这眼下紧要的是帮他们稳住心态，我也不会在班里直言不足，全程以鼓励引导为主，帮大家平稳迎考。

body.body:
**Volcán** es de esas palabras perfectas para aprender porque conecta imagen, sonido y significado de inmediato. La frase **“El volcán está activo”** está bien resuelta, y el ejemplo con **Popocatépetl** le da un toque real y memorable; además, sigue siendo uno de los volcanes más activos de México, como recogen notas recientes sobre emisiones de ceniza y actividad eruptiva [MSN/Bing News](https://www.msn.com/en-us/weather/topstories/mexico-s-popocat%C3%A9petl-is-throwing-ash-over-the-valley-again-as-guatemala-s-fuego-erupts-the-same-day-two-of-the-americas-most-active-volcanoes-firing-at-once/ar-AA23QrWx?ocid=BingNewsVerp) y [MSN video report](https://www.msn.com/en-xl/news/other/popocatepetl-volcano-shoots-massive-ash-plume-into-the-sky-over-mexico/vi-AA238nDf?ocid=BingNewsVerp).

También funciona muy bien el formato trilingüe. Ver **volcano / 火山 / volcán** en una sola pieza ayuda mucho a fijar vocabulario sin hacerlo pesado, y eso en una serie diaria vale oro.

Si quieres afinar aún más la parte didáctica, una mini expansión útil sería añadir una línea con familia léxica, por ejemplo: **volcánico**, **erupción**, **lava**, **ceniza**. Eso convierte una palabra suelta en un pequeño campo semántico, que enseña más con casi nada.

Tu serie sigue teniendo una virtud muy clara: **simple, constante y usable**. Eso gana más que cualquier explicación enredada.

Good morning my beautiful friends, how are you all? Today will be a kind of busy day for me, that's why I decided to wake up early to participate because I don't want to be left out 😄😄😄. 

The way we were raised, communication was never a problem, infact I grew up knowing that I could discuss almost anything with my parents face to face. So I don't think I have any unspoken feelings or grievances that I have been unable to share with them.

Something happened on my traditional marriage day that stood out for me till dates, My father became emotional and was seen shedding tears. When people asked him why he was crying, he replied that among all his children, I was the one who would always tell him directly whenever he did something wrong. He actually appreciated my honesty and openness, and yes that was how close we were even up till dates.

Growing up, I never hid things from my parents. Not even when a young man approaches me on the road or expressed interest in me 🫣🫣🫣, I would still go home and tell my parents about it. That was how close we were. I never felt afraid for once to share my thoughts, feelings, or experiences with them.

Today, I try to apply the same principle in raising my own children. I want them to see me  as someone they can trust and talk to freely. We joke together, we eat together, we chat about different things, and I make it a habit to ask them about their day at school, or whatever that happens around them. More importantly, I can be a good listener when it comes to my children. I leave whatever I'm doing and listen when they talk. I believe that being a good listener will  help them feel valued and understood, and even open to discussing more with me. 

I don't know if it's only me that has noticed that children nowadays can be quite different. My eldest son, for example, is naturally reserved and prefers to keep things to himself. He does not easily talk about what is happening in his life, not because he is hiding something, but he doesn't know how to express himself naturally, so to speak. Because of this, I make a conscious effort to engage him in conversations. I constantly reassure him that he can tell me anything, whether it is good or bad, and that I will always be there to support him, I will shower him with praises, call him pet names just to make him smile and feel relaxed. I also try to pay attention to changes in his behavior and make out time to have a meaningful discussion with him. Gradually, he has started opening up and sharing personal stuffs with me, and it brings me great joy.

Yes keeping communication open has blessed me with a close relationship with my parents, and it is a value that I am trying hard to pass on to my children as well.

Blue Origin New Glenn rocket literally exploded on the launchpad during a test firing in Florida
What a wild moment to behold I wanted to immediately capture that chaotic \

emote

 * **The Epic Smoke**: I drew massive, looping, swirling cloud lines to show the huge explosion tearing up the towers. I wanted it to feel just as dramatic as the real footage we're seeing all over 
 * **The Billionaire Shock**: Look at the character Bezos I drew the completely stunned, wide-eyed, open-mouthed look as his rocket turns into a literal firework oops It pairs so perfectly with the cheeky character laughing in the corner could be Elon hehehe.
 * **The Savage Punchline**: I hand-lettered the text **\

** right across the center. 

Did you guys see the crazy video footage of the explosion yet? If you were a billionaire, would you keep funding rockets after the incident like that, or would you pivot to a safer hobby?

body.title: Princess Jewellery Box (Esp/Eng)
body.body: > [Esp] ¡Saludos comunidad! He querido trabajar en algo diferente, vi una cajita de joyero y traté de recrearla a mi estilo, Quisiera contar una anécdota, en una salida con mi mejor amiga estábamos viendo unas tasitas de cerámica, yo las uso para mis velas aromáticas, pero ella me sorprendió para qué las usa, me dijo, que las tiene en su mesa de noche con sus joyas y me dije, pero ¿Por qué no los tienes en cajitas de joyería? Pues ella es muy elegante y fina, su respuesta fue: No tengo, entonces miré hondo y me di cuenta que yo tampoco tengo, pues con la mudanza, las que había comprado eran tan delicadas que se rompieron. Esta historia me inspiró a hacer un joyero para mí, buscando practicar para obtener maestría y ver si le hago una a mi amiga con otros materiales.

> [Eng] Hello everyone! I wanted to try something different. I saw a little jewellery box and tried to recreate it in my own style. I’d like to share a little story: when I was out with my best friend, we were looking at some little ceramic cups. I use them for my scented candles, but she surprised me with what she uses them for. She told me she keeps them on her bedside table with her jewellery, and I thought to myself, ‘But why don’t you keep them in jewellery boxes? Well, she’s very elegant and refined, and her reply was: ‘I don’t have any.’ So I thought about it deeply and realised that I don’t have any either, because during the move, the ones I’d bought were so delicate that they broke. This story inspired me to make a jewellery box for myself, as a way to practise and hone my skills, and to see if I can make one for my friend using different materials. ---

body.title: Kanaaq Miner : Hardworking and Reliable Warrior  | Splinterlands
body.body:
> Hello everyone, I hope you are all well. Today I am going to share with you my personal opinion and experience about **Kanaaq Miner** an interesting and strategic card in the Splinterlands game. Although this card may seem very simple at first glance, in the right situation it can play a role that can change the outcome of a match. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfWb1ZUEC8EupbpMAjYMmDoY24j3i1wNr2K7oT2RpkU3k/image.png) This is a card that reveals its true power through patience, planning and the right team combination. Many times in Splinterlands we use some cards that do not directly deal the most damage but are able to maintain the balance of the entire team and contribute at crucial moments. This is exactly that kind of card. Its presence makes the team more organized and can bring additional advantages in certain situations. The biggest advantage of this card is its functionality and flexible use. It can adapt to different types of team combinations, which is an important issue for many players. Sometimes it is seen that the opponent is able to hold his position and help the team. This card is especially useful for those who like to play matches with a long-term plan. body.title: Tomato plants with their harvest, which I don't know what my wife's uncle has at his house
body.body:
> Happy and blessed Friday night to all! Wishing you an excellent weekend, especially one successful in your planting projects, or perhaps, as in this case, a lucky one, a bountiful harvest of tomatoes 🍅. I'm not sure how to describe them because some are very small and others not so much, so we'll leave them as UNKNOWN for now. If any of you have more information about them, or any other characteristics, please share.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVXBJSjmsVquG4xs17VVo32AeT9XiyHwwfaXBHBuC9TKr/1780113112918.jpg)


Perhaps because of where the plants are located, I should tell you that, contrary to what many might think, these grew freely. To explain, my wife's uncle set up a place where the water used after washing clothes and dishes, as well as the seeds of some vegetables when cooking, collects. From there, it flows through a place where it waters a lemon tree and some others along the way, finally reaching the banana plants at the far end of the property.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcsZByBePyNckLcwmEZui25n9SNp1v2yLdCGC2hSCLnLm/1780113150486.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYCXZHVpreDjCYZzCAjVocvwFnWu1z9t92zkQArad9aNp/1780113150761.jpg)


After taking a few more photos, I noticed the difference between those two tomatoes I mentioned at the beginning of my post here in the #hivegarden community. They are visibly much larger compared to the others, which are much smaller.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRpFwrRDNngXXZ4PEKcQMJ4TC1J6WhoEMwqWSucc7SqJT/1780113178686.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPQ8sv9B9aMvSdMb5kRRHQ9YSfYF7EZrMebm1BiYb5djp/1780113178992.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQHXuWa2m6NRuuZdcQ6wQSGHhGE3n1Q4A5f12EQcRDd8d/1780113179227.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYfwga2A7sFiTLJSaZVP6eBoJ9s3sdwxj7Sg6hGBLWNV6/1780113179460.jpg)


Not only did I take those photos, but while searching, I found one ready for harvest, which I promptly took for myself. I'm trying to replicate the success I'm having with the previous batch of tomato seedlings, which are doing very well. I'll be sharing more information about all of this soon here in the #hivegarden community, which is one of my favorites because agriculture is one of my passions. Being able to work and harvest the food we eat is an incredible feeling. </center>

body.title: My Actifit Report Card: May 29 2026
body.body:
Today is one of those days. One of those days when tiredness seems to win, when motivation is not at its highest, and when everything feels a little more difficult than usual. Yet, despite all of that, the effort remains stronger than the excuses. Maybe today I did not reach the same point I reached yesterday. Maybe my pace was slower and my energy was lower. But I still showed up. I still made the attempt. And sometimes, that is what truly matters. Today has been a complicated day, but I do not want to let it pass without making my post for the Atifit community. Because consistency is not about being perfect every day; it is about continuing even on the difficult ones. Every small step counts, especially the ones taken when giving up would have been easier.

body.title: Aprender a caminar con las dos caras del Adiós. [Esp-Eng]
body.body:
>
![InShot_20260529_234538355.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTsv7EL9PQY1p1W3WjkiAwFDYmSWUGdH6iqohKwyaC3iw/InShot_20260529_234538355.jpg)
Todos hemos vivido una situación o un hecho que nos obliga a alejarnos de una persona, existen casos donde nos damos cuenta que por nuestra propia salud mental y por nuestro amor propio debemos decir adiós pero otras veces la despedida es obligatoria como por ejemplo en el caso de la muerte. Todas las despedidas duelen, lo que hace la diferencia es el origen o la causa, cuando el adiós deriva de un hecho consciente, es un proceso de alejamiento más complicado, porque debemos aceptar que el vínculo con esa persona está roto, nos lastima y que aunque esa persona sigue viva ya no podemos estar allí, así que en ese caso decir adiós es una decisión consiente y se toma constantemente, este tipo de alejamiento es un acto de inmenso amor y valentía. Cuando el adiós es obligatorio, definitivo y sin elecciones, cuando deviene de la muerte, el proceso es mucho más lento y es realmente doloroso, debemos reorganizar y transformar ese lazo, por un lado debemos continuar con nuestra vida y adaptarnos a una nueva realidad y por el otro lado respetar la ausencia y aprender a transformar el amor, un amor que siempre vamos a tener pero que ahora debe ser cultivado de manera diferente. Sea cuál sea la causa por la cual debimos alejarnos, siempre vamos a transitar por el camino del duelo, y este proceso es obligatorio, cuando una separación nos duele es porque amamos, es porque el vínculo que teníamos con esa persona era importante, era real, y el dolor nos permite aprender, nos permite crecer y nos permite adquirir experiencia. El aprendizaje que vamos a adquirir va a depender de la causa por la cual se dio el alejamiento, si el adiós se dio para auto-protegernos es demostración de nuestra fortaleza, de que nos respetamos y sabemos poner límites, por otro lado cuando el adiós deviene de la muerte en este proceso aprendemos el valor de la vida. Decir adiós siempre nos permite crecer, porque después de una separación sea cual sea la causa no volvemos a ser los mismos, algo dentro de nosotros se rompió y se reconstruyó, nos volvemos resilientes y nos llenamos de experiencia, aprendemos a caminar la vida con ausencias, con despedidas, con adiós, con recuerdos de vínculos y con la satisfacción de que en algún momento amamos. Aunque en la vida nos va tocar decir adiós más de una vez, y aunque duela, es un proceso que debemos aceptar con gallardía, incluso con respeto y con amor, además con la enorme satisfacción de haber amado, de haber crecido y de haber experimentado... Sea cual sea la causa del adiós son esas despedidas las que nos hacen resilientes y hacen de nosotros mejores seres humanos. Cualquier adiós, cualquier despedida, nos deja una herida, es normal sentir dolor, tener sentimientos encontrados, dudas, pero justamente es en ese proceso en el que nos vamos a convertir en una mejor versión de nosotros mismos, porque el camino de la vida es así, está lleno de encuentros, amor, decepción, despedidas, ausencias, muertes y resiliencia. ______ ###
❤️❤️❤️❤️English Version.❤️❤️❤️❤️
_______
![InShot_20260529_234706700.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPgw4RSytmWUpxE7SaKgFiLMkzsNK7keNHsLXZ31mG6w7/InShot_20260529_234706700.jpg)
We have all experienced a situation or event that forces us to distance ourselves from someone. There are cases where we realize that for our own mental health and self-respect, we must say goodbye, but other times, saying goodbye is obligatory, as in the case of death. All goodbyes hurt; what makes the difference is the origin or cause. When goodbye stems from a conscious decision, it is a more complicated process of distancing ourselves because we must accept that the bond with that person is broken, that it hurts us, and that although that person is still alive, we can no longer be there. So, in that case, saying goodbye is a conscious decision and is made repeatedly. This type of distancing is an act of immense love and courage. When goodbye is obligatory, definitive, and without choices, when it comes from death, the process is much slower and truly painful. We must reorganize and transform that bond. On one hand, we must continue with our lives and adapt to a new reality, and on the other hand, respect the absence and learn to transform love—a love that we will always have but that must now be cultivated differently. Whatever the reason we had to separate, we will always travel the path of grief, and this process is obligatory. When a separation hurts, it's because we loved, because the bond we had with that person was important, it was real, and the pain allows us to learn, to grow, and to gain experience. The lessons we learn will depend on the reason for the separation. If the goodbye was for self-protection, it demonstrates our strength, that we respect ourselves and know how to set boundaries. On the other hand, when the goodbye stems from death, in this process we learn the value of life. Saying goodbye always allows us to grow, because after a separation, whatever the cause, we are never the same again. Something inside us broke and was rebuilt; we become resilient and filled with experience. We learn to navigate life with absences, with farewells, with goodbyes, with memories of relationships, and with the satisfaction of knowing that at some point we loved. Although life will inevitably bring us to say goodbye more than once, and even though it hurts, it's a process we must accept with courage, even with respect and love, and with the immense satisfaction of having loved, grown, and experienced life. Whatever the reason for the goodbye, it is these farewells that make us resilient and better human beings. Any goodbye, any parting, leaves a wound. It's normal to feel pain, to have mixed feelings, doubts, but it is precisely in this process that we become a better version of ourselves, because that's the path of life: full of encounters, love, disappointment, goodbyes, absences, deaths, and resilience. _____ # ![1746651717170760710626541328692.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmetewFXFfpLPkHUT3bqXyuaa5BHUDoDt3Lm8aFTakkWSf/1746651717170760710626541328692.png) * Portada creada en Inshot con fotografía personal. * Demás imágenes utilizadas son de mi galería personal. body.title: 🌅Atardecer playero✨//🌅Beach sunset✨(Esp-Eng)
body.body:
>Cuando pienso en vibras de verano se me viene a la mente recuerdos de la playa,claro porque cuando es verano lo que se piensa es ir a la playa,y es que es un lindo lugar,y los atardeceres de playa son como mágicos, porque el sol pareciera que va bajando bajo el agua, porque da un efecto de que está bajando,y el cielo se torna de colores, amarillo y naranja y rojo,hasta incluso de morado y rosado. El reflejo que deja el sol pareciera que se mezcla con el mar,y las aves pasan justo en el momento para no llegar tarde al festín. El atardecer playero es un momento de nostalgia porque ya a esa hora hay que volver a nuestras casas,pero si nos gustaría quedarnos en la playa y vivir frente a él. Ese recuerdo me dio inspiración para hacer un dibujo de un bello atardecer,asi que con colores y hoja de papel me deje llevar por la inspiración.* # > When I think of summer vibes, memories of the beach come to mind. Of course, when it's summer, all you think about is going to the beach. It's such a beautiful place, and beach sunsets are magical. The sun seems to be sinking under the water, creating a downward effect, and the sky turns into a riot of colors—yellow, orange, red, even purple and pink. The sun's reflection seems to blend with the sea, and the birds fly by just in time to join the feast. A beach sunset is a moment of nostalgia because at that hour we have to go home, but we wish we could stay on the beach and live there, surrounded by it. That memory inspired me to draw a beautiful sunset, so with colors and a sheet of paper, I let myself be carried away by the inspiration. --- # #
Materiales/Materials
 #
![1000277018.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQme2QuUWZYonNpmwKZd7s7pmSwM1SFDwHWaG5hFyhyLWLm/1000277018.jpg)
# # * Lápices de colores * Hoja de papel blanca * Sacapuntas * Borrador # >* Colored pencils >* White sheet of paper >* Pencil sharpener >* Eraser # --- #
![1000277019.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPpgZW3rpXMU4XSGXPZVzTPEkYENiW3gXpvNU9fhQML6J/1000277019.jpg)
![1000277023.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmY6ttiaWWYmuf7D1s84qhwXv5QkAZYoi9ZNDRy13XqVNM/1000277023.jpg)
# **

>Una de las primeras cosas que hago antes de comenzar un dibujo es marcar los espacios en dónde irán ubicados todas las partes del dibujo,y también aprendí algo nuevo para dibujar, reemplazar el lápiz por un color,es mejor porque el color no deja marcas como el lápiz,y también por ser un color es más fácil camuflarse con los demás colores,sin marchar el dibujo como lo hace el lápiz. Entonces marque mi boceto con color rojo con trazoz suaves.** # > One of the first things I do before starting a drawing is mark the spaces where all the parts of the drawing will be placed. I also learned something new about drawing: replacing the pencil with colored pencil. It's better because colored pencils don't leave marks like pencils do, and because it's colored pencil, it's easier to blend in with other colors without ruining the drawing like a pencil does. So I outlined my sketch with red colored pencil using light strokes. ---
![1000277026.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmV24g8hcsKhKzgcBesPFRfnEbGGAK56C5fCNXkfoUto1b/1000277026.jpg)
![1000277028.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmd2aBZLQtnHq1CZY4Bdn8feJT8oVAYbwG2MYqfdbqcp3o/1000277028.jpg)
![1000277028.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmd2aBZLQtnHq1CZY4Bdn8feJT8oVAYbwG2MYqfdbqcp3o/1000277028.jpg)
![1000277030.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVnEuzgsTJKJivFhYvnRWamRdEpEYx5aADkcuzT9Jup1R/1000277030.jpg)
![1000277323.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUpf6tXZkAHujbs7KkvbEovv2uT5SpQu59YxgDo9u4ouH/1000277323.jpg)
![1000277325.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmepxswqAwEanEo8AA3tmWPvMhEWAvBTSAa94r3t2xjUiS/1000277325.jpg)
# **

>Y como pienso yo,que la idea de dibujar es expresarse libremente, entonces decidí comenzar a dibujar el atardecer. Cuando fui colocando los primeros colores no se veía en nada bien,pero confíe en el proceso y deje que el color tomara su camino solo.** # > And since I believe the idea of drawing is to express oneself freely, I decided to start drawing the sunset. When I first applied the colors, it didn't look very good, but I trusted the process and let the color take its course. ---
![1000277326.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmc1L9Xij5GvYnPEtkSUPBjTBkUE7RHN3PPAqEsPkEAcuB/1000277326.jpg)
![1000277327.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQ1BJo92RMVXGXz1fVLL9rWzVbeGEqZe4aHmH7JP7hbnN/1000277327.jpg)
# **

>Ya con solo tener el atardecer adelantado,me dirijo por un momento a la zona de las plantas de coco,y al mar, porque ya estaba dibujando cerca de esa parte y entonces por el estrecho espacio que había para dibujar me hizo adelantar esa parte. Pero sigamos confiando en el proceso que va bien.** # > With the sunset already approaching, I briefly moved to the area of the coconut palms and the sea, because I was already sketching near that part and the limited space made me move on to that section. But let's continue trusting the process; it's going well. ---
![1000277328.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPguDcaNST6c9uaoU6Ai66ix2VqGVrSzrUsGaPch8FiTk/1000277328.jpg)
![1000277329.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXNhf3riWj5Lk8grRjwyKhs2dYX2nnodQFdavrhyAivMH/1000277329.jpg)
![1000277330.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRGEzDtm8TtatSysmumYpwHKF1scSqFvx9KFSqxHsoHZR/1000277330.jpg)
![1000277115.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmapeKyAevCz76xPj3SzvNJrnfqcHcbLNcTErJgYpHc3Dj/1000277115.jpg)
![1000277117.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcnXT8QARN8Fc6Cmoqscn1Zf3FzVLBHhhGNa5DdrxtxPE/1000277117.jpg)
# **

>Me adelante en una parte porque me deje llevar,pero después continúe con el mar, dejando el espacio en dónde se refleja el atardecer,y entonces el agua lo dibuje haciendo sombras oscuras con azul marino,y luego con el azul claro dibuje las partes en blanco y otras partes no le agre nada de color pero casi nada de espacio para que se viera como los reflejos del mar,ya luego me concentre en la parte del reflejo del sol en el agua,y si me estaba gustando como se veía. Y en la parte de las palmeras de coco,dibuje la tierra primero con un color verde,y después con un color negro le hice varias líneas que se vieran como hierba,al igual hice lo mismo en la parte de las hojas de la palmera.** # > I got ahead of myself at one point because I got carried away, but then I continued with the sea, leaving the space where the sunset is reflected. Then I drew the water by creating dark shadows with navy blue, and then with light blue I drew the white parts and other parts I didn't add any color to, but I left very little space so that it looked like the reflections of the sea. Then I concentrated on the part where the sun reflects on the water, and I was liking how it looked. And for the coconut palms, I drew the earth first with a green color, and then with a black color I added several lines that looked like grass. I did the same thing with the palm leaves. ---
![1000277331.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWJogFBQYVzMgg1rTeSxUNb29bPtRJyBHyScv6MKha8y4/1000277331.jpg)
![1000277332.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmamLQERBnEm57s8xFSqKGw8pNQdNv67jhWWTP6uFvgZy3/1000277332.jpg)
![1000277333.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaCqD84MY9vRH8H4haof1Kmw8QMi2vYXjpksDAX22LQzA/1000277333.jpg)
# **

>La arena la dibujo con color entre amarillo, anaranjado y marrón. Para tratar de hacer el efecto o mínimo acercarme a ese efecto,en todo el dibujo hice marcar deliberadamente porque no buscaba la perfección,buscaba ese realismo e imperfecciones de el movimiento que tiene la vida en la naturaleza.** # > I drew the sand using colors ranging from yellow to orange to brown. To try to create the effect, or at least get close to it, I deliberately made marks throughout the drawing because I wasn't aiming for perfection; I was looking for the realism and imperfections of movement that life has in nature. --- #
![1000277126.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSjf5J6ZKsQHaTjJEAhQVMZz3QvQksTTBL3TcFLoYCovp/1000277126.jpg)
# *

>Y como último detalle le hice unas vaes volando hacia el atardecer,les doy las gracias a todos por visitar este post,que tengan una linda y feliz noche hasta pronto.* # > And as a final touch, I added some birds flying towards the sunset. Thank you all for visiting this post. Have a lovely and happy night. See you soon. --- # *
Las fotos presentadas en este post son de mi autoría. Las imágenes han sido editadas utilizando Canva. Las fotografías fueron tomadas con mi celular Infinix Smart 7. El contenido ha sido traducido con el traductor de Firefox.
