body.title: LOH °290: Peace of mind is a safe place
body.body:
>

Hello, my dearest women's community, I hope you are all well. It's wonderful to be active in the community again, and what better way to start than with a post of reflection and introspection? I really like the question about the safe place; it makes us think a lot about what we consider safe or not in our lives. I've read most of the posts that answer this question, and something that has caught my attention is that they are different points of view—very complex, yet insightful. It's nice to see this diversity of opinions, so here's mine.

>Hola, queridísima comunidad de mujeres, espero que se encuentren bien. Es bastante grato para mí volver a estar activa dentro de la comunidad y, bueno, nada mejor que una publicación de reflexión e introspección. Me gusta mucho la preguntasobre el lugar seguro; esto nos hace reflexionar mucho sobre lo que consideramos seguro o no en nuestras vidas. He leído la mayoría de las publicaciones que responden a esta pregunta y algo que me ha llamado la atención es que son diferentes puntos de vista, muy complejos pero asertivos. Es agradable ver esta diversificación de opiniones, así que aquí va la mía.


<Center>![37185.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/uri07/23t7DLr7ZRx4WhziUSq1bgFjXu7hMyNFfBoqd7hbZ936XyNWVu8AtJpUEpfMb2rj2vpGD.jpg)</Center>

As such, I don't really have a safe place; most of the time I'm busy working and studying. I've found refuge in music; in my mind, sunsets have been moments of disconnection from the world and emotional connection. My best moments in safe places are in the mornings, when I leave for work or university and watch the sunrise while the wind caresses my face and I listen to music. That's where my best reflections arise.
>Cómo tal, no tengo  especialmente un lugar  seguro, la mayor parte del tiempo me mantengo ocupada trabajando y estudiando. He encontrado un refugio en la música; en mi mente, los atardeceres han sido momentos de desconexión del mundo y conexión emocional. Mis mejores momentos en lugares seguros son por las mañanas, cuando salgo hacia el trabajo o la universidad, y veo el amanecer mientras el viento me acaricia el rostro y escucho música. Es ahí donde surgen mis mejores reflexiones.


<Center>![143010.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/uri07/EpVC6j8m47DfXM12kUZnzVk1JPjAbcnU9acQgm2mfNHkUVfEucqJYWYjckrsr8dLwTE.jpg)</Center>

I believe that no matter where we are, if our mind isn't calm and at peace, we won't feel safe anywhere, no matter how peaceful the surroundings may be. For me, almost any place is good for reflection and tranquility, especially with music playing. It's in those moments that I have the best opportunities to think and improve myself. I truly believe that's what security is all about: the constant evolution we experience as people, accepting that we aren't perfect, that we make mistakes, and that we can improve every day. Although it sounds easy and a bit cliché, this kind of thinking has helped me a lot in the mornings, as everything is calmer and the sky seems to understand me.
>Creo que no importa el lugar donde nos encontremos; si nuestra mente no está tranquila y en paz, no nos sentiremos seguros en ningún sitio, por mucha paz que pueda irradiar el entorno. Para mí, casi cualquier lugar es bueno para reflexionar y estar tranquilo, y más si es con música. Es en esos momentos donde tengo las mejores oportunidades para pensar y mejorarme a mí misma. Justamente creo que de eso se trata la seguridad: de la constante evolución que experimentamos como personas, aceptando que no somos perfectos, que cometemos errores y que podemos mejorar día a día. Aunque suene fácil y un poco cliché, este tipo de pensamiento me ha ayudado mucho en las mañanas, ya que todo es más tranquilo y el cielo me comprende.


<Center>![307691.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/uri07/23xyUoWaBiGB3UnLy9ScQDyYzh1NgTKT16jGtxRgVZMhUVxPVcAJYzJJXVqKqooknSaHB.jpg)</Center>


I think the noise of the city and the outside world is fleeting when the mind is focused. Swimming pulls us out of that trance, and it's happened to me on occasion, but even more so with music, since for me, it's food for the soul. I've experienced countless moments with it, both good and bad, and it also teaches me to reflect and grow. As a musician, one has a rather arduous and long path, which involves overcoming one's own ego, evolving spiritually, reaching catharsis, among many other things. It helps a lot to feel secure in this crazy world.
>Pienso que El ruido de la ciudad y lo externo es efímero cuando la mente está concentrada. Nadar nos saca de ese trance, y me ha sucedido en ocasiones, pero más aún con la música, ya que para mí, es el alimento del alma, con ella he pasado muchísimos momentos, tanto buenos como malos, y también me enseña a reflexionar y crecer. Como músico, uno tiene un camino bastante arduo y largo, que implica vencer tu propio ego, evolucionar espiritualmente, llegar a la catarsis, entre muchas otras cosas. Ayuda bastante a sentirse seguro en este mundo tan loco.

<Center>![37165.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/uri07/23xKrGZsUxidWBvhSGsnB4iK7sn2umT5LqkTnAXtQ9PiAZCQPLDE8n1Hww4kRqvfei9iG.jpg)</Center>


Answering the second question, I wouldn't hesitate: I'd love to trade lives with the Scottish singer Enya. I've been a huge fan of all her music and recordings for as long as I can remember, and her lifestyle is something I aspire to at some point in my own life. She's a very private person who lives in seclusion in a castle with numerous cats. She's never given a concert in her life, yet she's sold millions of records and songs. She invented her own language, which she used to record some songs for the film \

Absolutely all of her singles are works of art. She owns houses and castles valued at over $30 million and, like a vampire, she doesn't seem to age.\n>Respondiendo a la segunda pregunta, no lo pensaría dos veces: me gustaría cambiar de vida con la cantante escocesa Enya. Soy un ferviente admiradora de todo su trabajo musical y discográfico desde que tengo memoria, y su calidad de vida es algo a lo que aspiro en algún momento de la mía. Ella es una persona muy reservada que vive aislada en un castillo con numerosos gatos. Nunca ha dado conciertos en su vida, pero ha vendido millones de copias de discos y canciones. Inventó su propio idioma, con el cual grabó algunas canciones para la película \

. Absolutamente todos sus sencillos son obras de arte. Posee casas y castillos valorados en más de 30 millones de dólares y, como si fuera un vampiro, parece no envejecer.
![499570.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/uri07/23xebSPgaTD45cU3MDZEw826vK6bGDrZaTYP7moc9U5eYzQRNy5t7S9oqBRrutjs7Y2k8.jpg)
[Souce](https://www.letras.com/enya/foto/318623/)
Beyond all she has accomplished, I long to reach the point where she is, for the peace she feels. I firmly believe that people who adopt this kind of lifestyle do so not for fame or fortune, but for the richness of their overall education, including their spiritual development. They are elevated individuals who have grasped many things and put them into practice. Her life can be summed up as absolute peace, and I, having lived in chaos for so long, yearn for nothing more than peace and to be peace for others. I have been in chaos and in the shadows for a considerable part of my life, and although I integrate them as part of who I am, I seek tranquility, not to silence my conscience, but because I believe that is the meaning of life. >Más allá de todo lo que ha logrado y alcanzado, quisiera llegar al punto donde ella se encuentra, por la paz que siente. Creo fervientemente que las personas que adoptan este tipo de estilo de vida no lo hacen por la fama o la fortuna, sino por la riqueza de su educación en general, incluyendo la espiritual. Son personas elevadas que han comprendido muchas cosas y las han puesto en práctica. La vida de ella se resume en una paz absoluta, y yo, después de haber vivido en el caos durante mucho tiempo, no anhelo más que la paz y ser paz para los demás. He estado en el caos y en las sombras una parte considerable de mi vida, y aunque las integro como parte de lo que soy, busco la tranquilidad, no para acallar la conciencia, sino porque creo que ese es el significado de la vida.
![363463.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/uri07/23x1BTCPuLbpqVRZ8mppPeMpQuEGUx6rMZ9DiNvkqW6RfwJzdRx2QSVxiVZhRX9kgrqit.jpg)
Furthermore, there's a stigma that a musician is only truly great when they're famous, but success doesn't lie in that. It lies in producing quality work, conveying a message, having a personal style that allows people to recognize your music, building a community, and doing what you're truly passionate about. That's true stardom. Often, fame can be your worst downfall, and it's something musicians face every day. It's not just about overcoming ego death, but about dealing with your own demons, which can manifest as addictions capable of destroying you. We've seen this with many greats, like Freddie Mercury, among others, who were crushed by the weight of their burdens, something Enya managed to overcome. >Además, existe el estigma de que un músico es realmente grande cuando es famoso, pero el éxito no reside en eso. Se encuentra en realizar un trabajo de calidad, en transmitir un mensaje, en tener un sello personal que permita a la gente reconocer tu música al escucharla, en construir una comunidad y en hacer lo que realmente te apasiona. Ese es el verdadero estrellato. Muchas veces, la fama puede ser tu peor perdición, y es algo a lo que los músicos se enfrentan día a día. No se trata solo de vencer la muerte del ego, sino de lidiar con tus propios demonios, que pueden manifestarse en adicciones capaces de destruirte. Esto lo hemos visto en muchos grandes, como Freddie Mercury, entre otros, quienes fueron aplastados por el peso de su cruz, algo que Enya logró superar.
![363407.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/uri07/23wqnfXjYhxbKj2BgCyoemsCjpzH4GG9sf5yB15rptfE5QrrH5Tk7XH9PUUfUUbLa7QK9.jpg)
Thank you so much for reading this far and for reading my post. I hope you enjoyed all the photos, which were taken with my Infinix Note 50 Pro phone. >Muchísimas gracias por llegar hasta aquí y por haber leído mi publicación. Espero que les hayan gustado todas las fotografías, las cuales fueron tomadas con mi teléfono Infinix, modelo Note 50 Pro.
![37949.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/uri07/244KZwwJ22RuUwHbaYQTtQmqa2he8tbpQL5fLuVfz7sNNcmVx1SG9oCx1HeFHdhnwzC27.jpg)

body.title: Mi problema con la solidaridad sin reciprocidad (Español-Inglés)
body.body:
>Sé que la invitación a este concurso estaba enfocada en la pérdida de la solidaridad como valor o práctica social. No obstante, yo tengo una visión un poco más crítica sobre el tema; quizás vengo de un país (Venezuela) donde esa virtud ha sido explotada por personas sin escrúpulos durante años.

Mi país es considerado por muchos extranjeros como uno de los más solidarios del mundo. Los venezolanos nos apoyamos durante las inundaciones de Vargas en 1999, brindamos apoyo a civiles de varios países de Latinoamérica cuando eran perseguidos en dictaduras o huían de guerras civiles, los ayudamos en desastres e incluso les dimos donaciones cuando podíamos.

Sin embargo, cuando nosotros sufrimos la tragedia de caer en una dictadura y hubo una emigración masiva para salir del infierno en el que se convirtió el país, mucha gente le dio la espalda a mi pueblo. Criminalizaron a personas pobres asociándolas con las bandas del país (que existen y hacen mucho daño, pero que no son, ni remotamente, la gran mayoría de los emigrantes venezolanos, como hacen parecer los noticieros amarillistas internacionales). Muchos fueron explotados en condiciones de esclavitud en minas ilegales en Brasil, fueron víctimas de trata de personas o murieron en el camino, terminando en tumbas anónimas.

>¿Y qué fue lo que hicieron la gran mayoría de esas personas para merecer ese trato?

La gran mayoría de los que emigraron no hicieron nada malo. Algunos abrieron nuevos emprendimientos, otros ayudaron al sistema sanitario de su nuevo país como médicos durante la crisis del COVID, e incluso hubo quienes estudiaron y trataron de hacer una carrera para ser ciudadanos de provecho. Sin embargo, eso casi no aparece en las noticias. Lo que suele aparecer más sobre nosotros es el \

, como si esos seis o siete millones de venezolanos que están lejos de su tierra porque no tienen qué darle de comer a sus familias fueran parte de una banda de criminales.

La solidaridad que muchos venezolanos les dieron a otras personas que atravesaban grandes dificultades no fue retribuida cuando pasamos de ser la \

a ser la Venezuela pobre. Y ese cambio sobre cómo nos ven nos dice algo sobre la naturaleza de la solidaridad que algunas personas no tienen el valor de reconocer: la solidaridad sin reciprocidad puede llevarnos a un camino de esclavitud y explotación.

Debemos ser más selectivos sobre con quién somos solidarios (si ayudamos a alguien varias veces y, cuando necesitamos ayuda, esa persona no la retribuye, entonces no vale la pena seguir apoyándola) y en qué circunstancias debemos serlo (ya que, si siempre lo hacemos para todo, acabamos creando una dependencia excesiva hacia nosotros); porque no todos son dignos de nuestra solidaridad y no todos tienen el deseo de retribuirla, por mucho que se beneficien de ella.

Hay mucha gente en la actualidad que se ha dado cuenta de ello, por lo que la falta de reciprocidad ha erosionado la predisposición social a ser solidarios en el futuro. No se trata solo de un cálculo egoísta, sino de una cuestión de supervivencia colectiva: cuando una sociedad normaliza la solidaridad unidireccional, termina incentivando el abuso y agotando los recursos de quienes realmente sostienen el sistema.

Para mí, la solidaridad solo es sostenible como un contrato social de doble vía. Si ignoramos la reciprocidad, no solo nos exponemos a la explotación individual, sino que condenamos a los colectivos (como ocurrió con los millones de venezolanos señalados injustamente) a quedar aislados cuando más necesitan de la red que ayudaron a construir. La solidaridad sin reciprocidad es una invitación al descarte; mientras que la solidaridad con reciprocidad, en cambio, es la única base sobre la cual se puede construir una comunidad digna, funcional y humanitaria.
>My Problem with Solidarity Without Reciprocity (English Version)\n\n

>I know the invitation to this contest was focused on the loss of solidarity as a social value or practice. However, I have a somewhat more critical view on the subject; perhaps because I come from a country (Venezuela) where this virtue has been exploited by unscrupulous people for years.

My country is considered by many foreigners to be one of the most supportive in the world. We Venezuelans supported each other during the 1999 Vargas floods, we provided aid to civilians from various Latin American countries when they were persecuted by dictatorships or fleeing civil wars, we helped them in disasters, and we even gave them donations when we could.

However, when we suffered the tragedy of falling under a dictatorship and a massive emigration ensued to escape the hell the country had become, many people turned their backs on my people. They criminalized poor individuals, associating them with the country's gangs (which exist and cause great harm, but are not, even remotely, the vast majority of Venezuelan migrants, as international sensationalist news outlets make it seem). Many were exploited in slave-like conditions in illegal mines in Brazil, were victims of human trafficking, or died on the road, ending up in anonymous graves.

>
And what did the vast majority of those people do to deserve such treatment?

The overwhelming majority of those who emigrated did nothing wrong. Some started new businesses, others helped the healthcare system of their new country as doctors during the COVID crisis, and there were even those who studied and strove to build a career to become productive citizens. Yet, this almost never appears in the news. What tends to appear more about us is the \

as if those six or seven million Venezuelans who are far from their land because they have nothing to feed their families were all part of a criminal gang.

The solidarity that many Venezuelans gave to others who were going through great difficulties was not reciprocated when we went from being the \

to being the poor Venezuela. And that change in how we are perceived tells us something about the nature of solidarity that some people do not have the courage to acknowledge: solidarity without reciprocity can lead us down a path of slavery and exploitation.

We must be more selective about whom we offer our solidarity to (if we help someone several times and, when we need help, that person does not reciprocate, then it is not worth continuing to support them) and in what circumstances we should do so (since, if we always do it for everything, we end up creating an excessive dependence on us); because not everyone is worthy of our solidarity, and not everyone has the desire to reciprocate it, no matter how much they benefit from it.

Many people today have realized this, and as a result, the lack of reciprocity has eroded the social predisposition to be supportive in the future. It is not just about selfish calculation, but a matter of collective survival: when a society normalizes one-way solidarity, it ends up incentivizing abuse and depleting the resources of those who truly sustain the system.

For me, solidarity is only sustainable as a two-way social contract. If we ignore reciprocity, we not only expose ourselves to individual exploitation, but we condemn collectives—as happened to the millions of Venezuelans unjustly targeted—to being left isolated when they most need the network they helped build. Solidarity without reciprocity is an invitation to disposal; solidarity with reciprocity, on the other hand, is the only foundation upon which a dignified, functional, and humanitarian community can be built.

\n\n
></center>\n\nLas imagenes y la traducción al inglés de este post fueron hechas por Gemini AI.

body.title: Planting Zukes and Cukes
body.body:
Yesterday morning I had in mind to plant some of my seedlings out into the garden. But I decided against it for two reasons: 1) it was going to be a very warm day (89 degrees), and 2) thunderstorms were forecast for the evening. It didn't seem wise to expose new plants to those kinds of weather. So I opted to do some preliminary weeding instead.

We did get the thunderstorms, although the heaviest parts passed us by. Still, we saw plenty of lightning, heard lots of thunder, and got some rain out of it. And a nice sunset.

<center>
![20260528_203516 resized and edited.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/scribblingramma/242NWe9nsokYYncaZbpebtvjKf3W8YmqcsTaPJyfsKVyYYSpRXDSwvFCbvRFZodqDkrTf.JPG)
</center>

This morning was sunny and pleasant once again, so I planted some of my starts. The cucumbers were barely big enough to plant; I hope they live.
<center>
![20260529_193633 edited.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/scribblingramma/23w2jGTzg1YDiA7YgM7LGPaCJWsZWoABDh5C7KTvpxxdUGHf4BhExYvAWYGGVYJ34ZdzG.JPG)
</center>

The golden zucchini were much bigger, and should be fine.
<center>
![20260529_193703 edited.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/scribblingramma/EoChc7vUFYJtRDs7uuQAvQvAPWjQzyHugdPgPWLjsXrEjL3B9t8iXySvsPL8CP4nzrF.JPG)
</center>

Likewise the yellow summer squash...
<center>
![20260529_193714 edited.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/scribblingramma/23uQpVSwZTw9WyP2ypjDyNvigzBP4bZccTK3JfmyqQBvVrCiMnmemS8sbmvUguJquw58Y.JPG)
</center>

...and the zucchini.
<center>
![20260529_193722 edited.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/scribblingramma/23tmDemVC8bn9oEY8qVXLGFixgVm4joA4CZknymwJ16Hp7rEyCjvPaUK2pUEcau3TNaby.JPG)
</center>

For years now, I've been planting \

in plastic buckets cut in half or thirds. It helps keep the water where I want it, especially when the plants are small, and helps keep out cutworms. While I was digging out the last few weeds I discovered several kinds of larva or caterpillar things, including tiny white ones, larger gray ones, and reddish brown ones. I have no idea what they are, I just figure I don't need them in the garden. So I flicked them out into the field with the tip of my trowel.

Of course, planting doesn't just mean digging a hole and sticking the seedling into it. Besides removing weeds and larva-like things, I mixed in some commercial chicken manure and some balanced fertilizer pellets. 

Monday I planted the sunflower and broccoli starts. The broccoli is in a raised bed, but the sunflowers went directly into the soil, inside a large tire. Two days later, two of them had been bitten off  and a third had big holes in its tiny leaves.

<center>
![20260528_072232 resized.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/scribblingramma/23wC389hwA9zHT4Sa9xiXeQwnEqs8zoo7VG2Vpq5gcVa1cSgQrSjhaF1pwkHsKeYnav68.jpg)
</center>

 After looking up information, I decided it might be the fault of slugs or caterpillars. In case it was birds or moths, I put the wire baskets over the remaining plants, and then sprinkled diatomaceous earth around them all. I hope those actions deter whatever was eating them.

<center>
![20260529_193743 resized.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/scribblingramma/EoK5tVfM8LLwYkd2gxHmZa7DkvVir6Na77aGbLfCqXWggkpzeiQ6LDr3QwoFxFG64MD.jpg)
</center>

Tomorrow I hope to plant a few more of the seedlings, and I need to dig weeds around the blueberry bushes again. We have a major infestation of bindweed, and it's coming up all around the bushes and throughout the clover patch. I've tried everything but toxic chemical pesticides to get rid of it,including agricultural strength vinegar and covering the garden with black plastic for several months, neither of which proved to be effective.  I've been told that chemicals are the only thing that will. But I don't want pesticides in the garden, so I guess I have to co-exist with bindweed.

<center>*All photos taken on my Android phone.*</center>

body.title: Freedom to play and enjoy the small nature of a bird
body.body:
The morning sun had just cast golden light on the garden which was still fresh with dew. Amidst a calming green backdrop, a small bird perches on a simple feeder. With agile movements and eyes full of curiosity, he jumps slowly while pecking at the available food grains. The atmosphere was so calm, as if the entire park was enjoying a peaceful start to the day.

The morning breeze blew gently, moving the leaves that reflected the sunlight. The little bird seemed to be playing by itself, occasionally looking in all directions before returning to enjoying its breakfast. Its presence adds color to a quiet garden, bringing life into charming simplicity.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUx9W7C864DyadFdmJFn3pFR6PR3Sixzp6qpBwkZ9zFoN/1780112723599.jpg)

In the midst of the hustle and bustle of a world that has not yet fully awakened, the garden becomes a place of calm. The little bird reminds us that happiness often comes in simple moments of warm morning light, fresh air, and the freedom to enjoy a new day. A small view that absorbs the peaceful beauty and leaves a sense of serenity for anyone who sees it.

body.title: Tasting Myka: Artisanal Greek Yogurt Ice Cream🍦
body.body: > Greetings and blessings to everyone in this community. I hope you’re all doing well and staying healthy. Last Sunday, my daughter and I decided to go for a walk together. So, that morning we put on some comfortable clothes and headed for the mountain that surrounds Bogotá, ready for a good hike. After nearly an hour of climbing and a good cardio workout, we ended up tired but happy that we’d done something for our health. The fresh air, the view of the city, and our conversations on various topics made the outing feel like a much-needed break for both of us. And as a reward after our workout, we decided to visit Myka, a new ice cream shop we’d been eager to try because the last time we passed by, there was a long line to get in. So we were really curious.

> Saludos y bendiciones para los comensales de esta comunidad. Espero que estén bien, con mucha salud. El domingo pasado mi hija y yo decidimos salir a caminar juntas. Así que, esa mañana nos pusimos ropa cómoda y nos fuimos hacia la montaña que rodea Bogotá, listas para una buena caminata. Después de casi una hora de subida y buen cardio, terminamos cansadas, pero felices porque hicimos algo por nuestra salud. El aire fresco, la vista de la ciudad y las conversaciones sobre diferentes temas hicieron que el plan se sintiera como un respiro necesario para las dos. Y como recompensa después del ejercicio, decidimos visitar Myka, una nueva heladería que teníamos ganas de conocer porque una vez que pasamos por ahí, había una larga fila para entrar. Así que teníamos mucha curiosidad. https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aurodivys/23tmDqtTXziSwjTRNKav2zdFPQYp2kLspNu53gPjkdHbCaywxRVMHnhfvVd1UYRGWTHF7.png |https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aurodivys/23wX1G4SeyvVd35BW2Z4rtkrTiJmnQyqph35icHUGsgaopBWzWFoHBP9oEwPeRHWYYKJT.jpeg|https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aurodivys/243M1Eifmjoz8mGEj9XjaBQWQ5EsWqUkxfPyCf91KRUZ4EtfjdnLSuBQm8n7RmYCwecRD.jpeg| |--|--| https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aurodivys/23tmDqtTXziSwjTRNKav2zdFPQYp2kLspNu53gPjkdHbCaywxRVMHnhfvVd1UYRGWTHF7.png

> I loved Myka’s concept from the very first moment: ice cream made with authentic Greek yogurt. It’s a unique ice cream—smooth, very creamy, and with a refreshing, delicious flavor. Plus, they have over twenty toppings to choose from, and honestly, picking just two for the medium size is almost impossible. My daughter ordered a mix of acai and lavender, topped with chocolate crumble, fleur de sel, and coconut sauce. I chose a mix of yogurt and mango with ground walnuts and coconut sauce as well. Both seasonal flavors were spectacular. Of course, we ended up trying each other’s ice cream, and we both agreed: everything was delicious.

> La propuesta de Myka me encantó desde el primer momento: helados elaborados con auténtico yogur griego. Es un helado diferente, suave, muy cremoso y con un toque refrescante delicioso al paladar. Además, tienen más de veinte toppings para escoger, y honestamente elegir solo dos para el tamaño mediano se vuelve una misión casi imposible. Mi hija pidió un mixto de açaí con lavanda, acompañado de crumble de chocolate con flor de sal y salsa de coco. Yo elegí un mixto de yogurt y mango con nueces de castilla molidas y también salsa de coco. Los dos sabores de temporada estaban espectaculares. Obviamente terminamos probando el helado de la otra y coincidimos en lo mismo: todo estaba delicioso. https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aurodivys/23tmDqtTXziSwjTRNKav2zdFPQYp2kLspNu53gPjkdHbCaywxRVMHnhfvVd1UYRGWTHF7.png |https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aurodivys/23vi4ABgzzXdmvCgdXqtWRw9LgFX7T8p8UJEpgDzDq9fqgorJ4SG4v14vog2F5zP2NmHE.jpeg|https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aurodivys/23vsSc5REC3mkaxXvMqcvCxZNL2BHzAFGKgDxboF5U9P5RXrUdmD39gEVkYQCr3WR1hTM.jpeg| |--|--| https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aurodivys/23tmDqtTXziSwjTRNKav2zdFPQYp2kLspNu53gPjkdHbCaywxRVMHnhfvVd1UYRGWTHF7.png

> We were thrilled to learn that their ice cream is artisanal, additive-free, and made with fresh, natural ingredients. It’s a real treat for the taste buds, and we’ll definitely be coming back to discover more flavors and combinations.

> Nos encantó saber que son helados artesanales, sin aditivos y preparados con ingredientes frescos y naturales. Una verdadera fiesta para el paladar y, sin duda, un lugar al que queremos volver para seguir descubriendo nuevos sabores y combinaciones. https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aurodivys/23tmDqtTXziSwjTRNKav2zdFPQYp2kLspNu53gPjkdHbCaywxRVMHnhfvVd1UYRGWTHF7.png ![WhatsApp Image 2026-05-29 at 08.28.09 (1).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aurodivys/23vsSPydMBUnjePeRdrK5diqEhrjaga581AU4R8aBYLTeeEnaEoXyFZCh8QmqpgP3C17p.jpeg) |https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aurodivys/23u64xSvfoCqkAvDW4yYbi4ZagmuNqUDmPHE1dd5ABHxhgJYxwxzGbjeY2s86hxuHuXxg.jpeg|https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aurodivys/23ynSE7sHBVaV1xeB6FWLUz61FnoTEHATDv7m79ebfgaFaQkMXudELpoQ2QLXWyTRzyd8.jpeg| |--|--| https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aurodivys/23tmDqtTXziSwjTRNKav2zdFPQYp2kLspNu53gPjkdHbCaywxRVMHnhfvVd1UYRGWTHF7.png

body.title: A Walk Through the Jose Marti Roundabout (Eng/Esp)
body.body:
> Today’s tour takes me to the Jose Marti Roundabout, named in honor of the Cuban philosopher, politician, and author who was born in 1853 and died in 1895. It is located on Gran Mariscal Avenue and was built in 1956. This roundabout helps reduce traffic congestion by distributing traffic in four directions. This roundabout was recently reopened, so the current infrastructure is new, including the bust of Marti.
![1000117863.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23vsNKPwcGjmDMu79DHRrCHVBfQLvoZFA2vx1wB9drAFce45NxckAhAwTZUHVoQTns9R4.jpg)
This roundabout is small and now features a colorful garden with palm trees and various ornamental plants. Despite the roundabout’s size, there are benches where you can rest for a while—of course, in the afternoon, when the Cumana sun has lost some of its intensity. Under the benches are colored lights that turn on at night, creating a pleasant spectacle.
![1000117442.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EpA1yHvCPxUbPYEqyxxpXybENvp4wzuijvBkbxf14qEfqYqJ3EPVKoPZxY14V93tEqS.jpg)
![1000117423.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Eqb2dtLvHvxaPxBv5T4LQRzhKpsyesDYAF3gkSv7BRKdRZtGAbeuQ9bSMu7BvtRgpqn.jpg)
In this square, you can see four flags: those of Venezuela, Sucre State, the municipality of Sucre, and Cuba. Access to this square is not usually easy because it is a very busy roundabout; one of its cross streets leads to the hospital, and it also provides access to Miranda Avenue, Andrés Bello Avenue (which connects to the Perimetral), and, of course, Gran Mariscal de Ayacucho Avenue, where the square is located.
![1000117419.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EqNFEvgZWbxjuiU42sSDSXYU7186W1YoPjd9rFSd16icxuYAgTCcELsGtgycN1zHLWg.jpg)
![1000117436.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/244UqsHsnbzmimFoir1QXQbTZPNSfY5XE95xbrcnVjbCwoWYdc7aN9VcENRp4GikFZaA7.jpg)
![1000117435.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EoyPzk7uh6doWwZVPunib1ahZHSc84UzKGGy59pKKTFvZXK6YujgqzogfXQhadtHKhh.jpg)
When I was here, I was somewhat intrigued by the meaning of the yellow and blue flag with horizontal stripes, and it turns out that upon researching it, I learned that it is the flag of Cumana, which I had not known until then. A few years ago, this square became a site for protests, especially when the Fondo Comun bank branch—the only one in Sucre state, located across from the roundabout—paid out Social Security pensions. People would begin gathering the night before to spend the night at the bank’s doors, and by dawn, chaos ensued as everyone scrambled to enter the bank.
![1000117430.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Eo8TivBh4Et64Hnu3Z7MeLVrymn73VvFsRfqtdya7ZT238yXEPpVqBXzb6SsGybehDq.jpg)
![1000117443.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EpLeyNWpwCQCRvh22aWHanny7WzzSbn3Bxyh699jo9QT3iXz4xZnwSg5p1uMDdPwXtb.jpg)
That unrest was exploited to use the square for political purposes, which hindered traffic in such an important part of the city. For that reason, it was decided to renovate the square, which is why it remained closed to the public for a time until its reopening. *** ***
## Versión en Español

> El recorrido de hoy me lleva a la Redoma José Martí, bautizada en honor al filósofo, político y autor cubano que nació en 1853 y falleció en 1895. la cual está ubicada en la Avenida Gran Mariscal y fue fundada en 1956. Este espacio ayuda a mantener la descongestión vehicular debido a que distribuye el tráfico en cuatro direcciones. Esta redoma se reinauguró recientemente, así que la actual infraestructura es nueva, incluyendo el busto de Martí.
![1000117863.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23vsNKPwcGjmDMu79DHRrCHVBfQLvoZFA2vx1wB9drAFce45NxckAhAwTZUHVoQTns9R4.jpg)
Esta redoma es pequeña, ahora posee un vistoso jardín, el cual está conformado por palmeras y diversas plantas ornamentales. A pesar de las características de la redoma, acá reposan unos bancos donde se puede reposar un rato, por supuesto, en horas de la tarde, cuando el sol cumanés haya bajado su intensidad. Debajo de los bancos se encuentran unas luces de colores que se encienden en la noche, brindando un agradable espectáculo.
![1000117442.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EpA1yHvCPxUbPYEqyxxpXybENvp4wzuijvBkbxf14qEfqYqJ3EPVKoPZxY14V93tEqS.jpg)
![1000117423.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Eqb2dtLvHvxaPxBv5T4LQRzhKpsyesDYAF3gkSv7BRKdRZtGAbeuQ9bSMu7BvtRgpqn.jpg)
En esta plaza se pueden observar cuatro banderas, la de Venezuela, la del estado Sucre, la del municipio Sucre y la de Cuba. El acceso a esta plaza no suele ser fácil porque es una redoma muy transitada, una de sus vías transversales comunica al hospital, también brinda acceso a la avenida Miranda, la Andrés Bello que comunica con la Perimetral y, por supuesto, la Avenida Gran Mariscal de Ayacucho que es su sitio de ubicación.
![1000117419.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EqNFEvgZWbxjuiU42sSDSXYU7186W1YoPjd9rFSd16icxuYAgTCcELsGtgycN1zHLWg.jpg)
![1000117436.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/244UqsHsnbzmimFoir1QXQbTZPNSfY5XE95xbrcnVjbCwoWYdc7aN9VcENRp4GikFZaA7.jpg)
![1000117435.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EoyPzk7uh6doWwZVPunib1ahZHSc84UzKGGy59pKKTFvZXK6YujgqzogfXQhadtHKhh.jpg)
Cuando estuve aquí quedé un tanto intrigado por el significado de la bandera amarilla y azul en franjas horizontales y resulta que investigando me enteré que es la bandera de Cumaná, lo que desconocía hasta entonces. Hace algunos años atrás, esta plaza llegó a ser un sitio para organizar protestas sobre todo cuando la agencia del banco Fondo Común, la única del estado Sucre y que está ubicada frente a la redoma, pagaba las pensiones del Seguro Social. Desde la noche anterior se empezaba a reunir la gente para pernoctar a las puertas del banco y al amanecer se advertía el caos por ingresar al banco.
![1000117430.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/Eo8TivBh4Et64Hnu3Z7MeLVrymn73VvFsRfqtdya7ZT238yXEPpVqBXzb6SsGybehDq.jpg)
![1000117443.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EpLeyNWpwCQCRvh22aWHanny7WzzSbn3Bxyh699jo9QT3iXz4xZnwSg5p1uMDdPwXtb.jpg)
Ese malestar era aprovechado para utilizar la plaza con fines políticos, lo que obstaculizaba el tránsito en una zona tan importante de la ciudad. Por ello se decidió remodelar la plaza, por tal razón permaneció cerrada al público por un tiempo hasta su reinauguración. *** *** ✓Photos from my personal gallery, edited with Fotocollage. ✓Text translated with DeepL.

body.title: Family decision
body.body:
![_DSC6084.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/guaicara/242YGWefur3Fo4Gz63VbiZ1VUzdWJ4qSqRX3RcHQgwngnwfvaeWx2x6NFMQWf1s5egtSh.jpg)
Is there anything better than a beach getaway to recharge your batteries? They say the sea heals everything, but if you add to that the company of the people you love most, you have the perfect formula for creating unforgettable memories. Today I want to share with you the story of a day filled with sun, waves, and, above all, lots of family time.

.

<div class=\

>Let's be honest, getting the whole family to wear the same outfit isn't always easy. However, when it's achieved, the result is spectacular! For this beach day, the chosen color was a bright neon yellow; a perfect choice that not only stands out against the blue sea, but also perfectly captures the essence of the day: pure positive energy, light, and fun. .

>Of course, a family photo isn't complete without everyone in the house. If you look closely, you'll see a cute little four-legged accomplice in one of the girls' arms, who didn't want to miss out on the sea breeze. Because happy moments are best enjoyed when we're all together (furry friends included!). .
>Moral of the day: Don't wait for a \
occasion to make a fun plan with your loved ones. Buy those matching shirts, travel to your favorite beach, take the picture, and above all, enjoy the beautiful chaos that is being with family.

body.title: What's it like working on a film set?  Working as an extra
body.body:
It's really tough to get into the film industry.  So many people go to LA every year with the idea being that they are going to be the next big thing and almost all of them fail.  I think it is rather important to kind of accept the fact that you are very unlikely to become famous, or even to get a speaking role.   

The thing about working in films though is that chances are it is not nearly as glamorous as you might be thinking.   The actors are worked very hard and even though we stand back and think that they all live these lives of complete luxury, that is just for the top folks.  A vast majority of the people that work in and on films do not achieve greatness and the work is actually quite exhausting.   

I have worked on a number of film sets though the years and mostly this is because I went to high school with a production assistant who is a part of a group that does contracts with a lot of films.   Most of these films are lower budget but they all need a bunch of people in the background so they can create the illusion of real life.   Getting work as an extra is actually really easy, but the job isn't likely to be what you think it is.

<center> https://d26oc3sg82pgk3.cloudfront.net/files/media/edit/image/54635/article_full%401x.jpg
[src](https://d26oc3sg82pgk3.cloudfront.net/files/media/edit/image/54635/article_full%401x.jpg)</center>

First off, check your ego at the door.  As an extra you are just one step above irrelevant as far as the production is concerned.  If you fuck about, you will get kicked out and nobody is going to miss you.   You are not supposed to stand out and if you try to do so, you will also get kicked out.  The film is not about you and if you think that you are going to get your \

as an extra you are delusional.  

There was a pretty decent TV comedy called *Extras* and I think it did a pretty good job of explaining what working in this field is like 

<center> https://i.redd.it/thoughts-on-extras-with-ricky-gervais-and-stephen-merchant-v0-eut7kenwoxlf1.jpg?width=718&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=1a23da3f517f0f5891c9dc11d1e982d6e36979ea
[src](https://i.redd.it/thoughts-on-extras-with-ricky-gervais-and-stephen-merchant-v0-eut7kenwoxlf1.jpg?width=718&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=1a23da3f517f0f5891c9dc11d1e982d6e36979ea)</center>
In all of these episodes Ricky Gervais' character and his friends spend most of the day simply sitting around waiting to be told to do something.   This is essentially what working as an extra is all about.   You will do a ton of sitting around and doing nothing.  Nobody really cares whether you are comfortable or not and there is a lot of cigarette smoking going on.   

There was one film that I worked on that had an outdoor scene that was merely an establishing shot for one single action sequence that involved a motorcycle.   There were dozens of people involved and some animals as well.  We spent a good 6 hours on this one scene and to this day I have no idea where that ended up or even what the film or TV series was.  I know Clive Owen starred in it and that is about it.  

Working as an extra is a good experience so that people can get a good idea of how not-so-glamorous the film industry is for people that are in it, and how huge the productions actually are.   It was really amazing to me the amount of people that were involved in just that one shot and smaller shots that I was involved in had dozens of people involved even though the film had very little in the way of budget.  As far as I know none of the scenes that I was in ever were involved in a huge blockbuster and I have only seen a couple of things where I can so much as pick myself out of the background, let alone see my face.

I suppose if there is one benefit of working as an extra is that you have virtually no responsibility and you get paid pretty well too.  I did it on a weekend where I had nothing else planned and was paid something crazy like $250 just to mostly sit around waiting to be told where to stand next.   

Costumes are changed, the people you are acting with changes, and often most films have the same extras in the background on a lot of different scenes.   They do a pretty good job of making you look different enough so that people don't notice it is the same people in the background over and over.   

I did find it a bit humorous on several occasions where I was in a group and some of the people there took it really seriously as if they were hoping that the director would take notice of them and put them in their next film or something.  Let me tell you something:  That is not going to happen.   

I know the story of how Harrison Ford was a carpenter on a movie set or something along those lines but for the most part the director and producers aren't even going to notice that you are there at all.  They often will not even speak to you and it is the job of assistant directors or production assistants to give you very basic instructions.  If you stand out or cause a problem you might get warned once, then you will be kicked out and probably blocked from ever participating in this sort of thing ever again.   

Your name will not be in the credits.

For me, I wouldn't do this anymore because now I know that any work of this sort is going to involve a very long day and nobody on the staff cares what your obligations are outside of the film set.  If you claim that you have somewhere to be do you really think they are going to shut down the set because of you?  ha!   

I'm happy I did this a dozen times or so just so that I could see what it is like to work on a film set.   Now that I have seen it I have a newfound respect for actors and especially the people who are on the other side of the cameras.  These are seriously long days with no definitive beginning or end and it looks to be a very stressful environment.   As an extra none of this stress is yours to worry about.  You basically get paid a couple hundred dollars to just sit around all day and while that sounds great to some people, trust me when I say that it stops being awesome after the first day or so.

body.title: [ESP-ING]  ESP-ING] Double-knit fabric for men
body.body: > ![Polish_20220302_164028364.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yolimarag/48ZbVDw1rPe3UB5MGmsJKe1Z3uXphrpXAqpRNicQMcWZ6bwQ2AXDHSfvGY6TRpkMto.jpg) Un saludo, mi gente maravillosa de Hive, y de @jewelry en este día traigo una accesorio muy bonita y sencilla de realizar, se acerca el día del padre y tenemos que dar algunos obsequios, nada mejor que hacer algo a mano, algo bonito, hermoso y cool para papá, a muchos hombres les encanta colocarse accesorios así que vamos hacer algunos. Las pulseras son accesorios que decoran, esta vez quise realizar una pulsera doble nudo con piedras negras onix mate, la cual es familia del cuarzo y simboliza un amuleto de protección contra malas energías, se le atribuye fuerza física y mental, además de que su significado es de uña o garra. Este proyecto no necesita materiales costosos, sino materiales que puedan combinar o vayan segun la creatividad que tengan, aproveche que tenia materiales en casa y quise aprovecharlos, me encantó mucho cómo quedó este proyecto, Espero que les guste este pequeño paso a paso, el cual fue realizado con mucho amor.

> ![Polish_20220302_164110218.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yolimarag/48eu38YaBkAfCWizTTiU2d1Pij8Px4pNYMB415n8fjQdhzn5BfZGwtKRUDGdZUVUXF.jpg) Greetings, my wonderful Hive community and @jewelry! Today I’m sharing a very pretty and easy to-make accessory. Father’s Day is coming up, and we need to give some gifts there’s nothing better than making something by hand, something pretty, beautiful, and cool for Dad. Many men love wearing accessories, so let’s make some. Bracelets are decorative accessories. This time, I wanted to make a double-knot bracelet with matte black onyx stones, which are part of the quartz family and symbolize a protective amulet against negative energy. They’re said to grant physical and mental strength, and their meaning is associated with a claw or talon. This project doesn’t require expensive materials, just items that can be combined or chosen based on your creativity. I took advantage of the materials I had at home and wanted to put them to use. I absolutely loved how this project turned out. I hope you enjoy this little step-by-step guide, which was made with lots of love. ---
---
> ### Materiales: ✅️ Piel de serpiente 2 metros cuarenta ✅️ Piedras onix 10 ✅️ Yesquero ✅️ Tijera

> ### Materials ✅️ 2.4 meters of snakeskin ✅️ 10 onyx stones ✅️ Tinderbox ✅️ Scissors

---

width=472 height=49 border=0>
### Paso a Paso / Step by Step
> Lo primero que haremos será cortar 2 tiras de 100 cm cada una y una sola de 40 cm.
> First, we'll cut two strips, each 100 cm long, and one strip that's 40 cm long. ---
> Vamos a colocar la tira de 40 cm en el medio y con la de 100 cm, con una vamos a hacer un nudo plano el cual pasaremos dos veces y en la tira de 40 cm introduciremos de una vez las 10 piedras ónix.
> We’ll place the 40-cm strand in the middle and use the 100-cm strand to tie a flat knot, which we’ll loop twice; then we’ll thread all 10 onyx stones onto the 40-cm strand at once. ---

> La idea de la pulsera es colocar el primer hilo, hacer los dos nudos completos del nudo plano, colocamos el otro hilo hacemos los dos nudos completos del nudo plano y colocamos una piedra, el primer hilo que nos quedó abajo es el que vamos a colocar alrededor de la piedra y hacemos un nudo plano como lo hicimos anteriormente, luego el otro hilo y así sucesivamente hasta terminar la piedra hasta el final son 10 piedras.

> The idea behind the bracelet is to start with the first strand, tie two full flat knots, then add the other strand, tie two more full flat knots, and place a bead. Take the first strand that’s now at the bottom and wrap it around the bead, tying a flat knot just as you did before. then the other string, and so on until you reach the end of the stone; there are 10 stones in total. ---
> Al terminar de tejer toda la pulsera Y colocar las 10 piedras vamos a cortar ambos lados quemamos con un yesquero y la presionamos.
> Once you've finished weaving the entire bracelet and added the 10 beads, cut both ends, seal them with a lighter, and press them down. ---
> Haremos un nudo doble vuelta en las puntas de cada uno nivelando por supuesto Siempre que estén a la misma altura Luego de eso vamos a cerrar con un nudo plano.
> We'll tie a double knot at the ends of each one, making sure they're at the same height. After that, we'll secure it with a square knot. ---

width=472 height=49 border=0>
### Resultado: / Result:

> Así ha quedado listo nuestra pulsera para papá, facil y sencilla de realizar, espero que sea de su agrado, tanto como me ha gustado a mi esta pequeña y hermosa creación, Gracias por estar aquí y ser parte de mi blog.

> And there you have itour bracelet for Dad is ready! It was easy and simple to make. I hope he likes it as much as I’ve enjoyed creating this little gem. Thank you for stopping by and being a part of my blog. . ---
> No hay límites para la creatividad, solo tu sabes hasta donde puedes llegar.

> There are no limits to creativity—only you know how far you can go. --- ---

body.title: We need to know how to protest injustice.
body.body: > https://images.pexels.com/photos/6257693/pexels-photo-6257693.jpeg [Source ]( https://www.pexels.com/photo/a-person-holding-a-pink-placard-6257693/ ) We have been hearing since childhood that injustice should never be tolerated with our mouths closed. This is absolutely true, it is as bad as doing injustice as tolerating injustice is also bad. In fact, the biggest truth is that the more we tolerate injustice, the more people will continue to do injustice to us and in many cases, until we say that this act is unjust, the person in front of us does not understand that he is doing wrong. Therefore, we should always point the finger at these ignorant people to explain how wrong they are. If we think that injustice is being done to us at present, but the person who is doing injustice to us will definitely understand his mistake one day and will stop doing injustice to us, but this does not happen at all. People who do injustice never understand their mistake and do not stop doing injustice to us. Rather, we see people around us who, despite knowing that injustice is being done to them, develop a habit of tolerating it and eventually breathe their last while enduring various hardships throughout their lives. Like these people, if we do not protest against injustice and oppression towards us, then our life will be completely ruined and eventually our life will end if we continue to tolerate it. If we have to live well, then we must learn to protest against injustice. Life is very big, so when we see injustice being done to us, we should protest at that moment and end that injustice and get out of there. If we can protest against injustice and stop ourselves from being oppressed and get out of there, then we will be able to live the rest of our lives very beautifully and happily. In many families, it is seen that the wife is completely devastated by the husband's oppression, and the husband's mental and physical condition is also very bad due to the wife's oppression. In that case, if they get out of that oppressive life partner, they will be able to spend the rest of their lives beautifully. We have to take action against injustice in every field, even if it is our own life partner, we should not back down. Just as injustice can happen in our families and we have to stand up against that injustice, similarly we have to take steps against various injustices in society. In society, both men and women are doing injustice and facing oppression in different ways. Injustice is being done to different people in different ways which many people are pretending not to see. In fact, we do not take any action or give importance to any injustice or oppression until it happens to us. And this is the biggest wrong step in our lives. Because if we all stand by each other at the wrong time and stand up against injustice, then one day the injustice and even unjust actions of strong people against helpless people will stop from this world. There are many powerful people who do not hesitate to oppress many helpless poor people just for their own petty interests, we need to take strict action against these people. In our society, we see injustice happening in various ways all around us, we constantly see the oppression of the strong against the weak. But we never consider it a personal matter and stand by each other in times of danger. But if we do not do this, every person stands by each other in times of danger and takes steps against injustice, oppression, injustice and various types of crimes, then our society will become much more beautiful at some point. A society free from injustice, oppression and various types of crimes occurring in different directions will be built. And with that, each of us will become much closer to each other and jealousy and selfishness will go away among us. We are group creatures, so we always have to live together and live together, so we all have the responsibility to build a beautiful society. Therefore, we should always protest strongly against injustice, oppression, injustice and various types of crimes. body.title: La solidaridad, que haríamos sin ella? [ESP - ENG]
body.body: >Saludos estimados amigos de Holos&Lotus, hoy me uno al tema propuesto por @damarysvibra [¿Quién dijo que la solidaridad se ha perdido?| Who said solidarity is lost?](https://hive.blog/hive-131951/@damarysvibra/quien-dijo-que-la-solidaridad-se-ha-perdidoororwho-said-solidarity-is-lost). Este tema es maravilloso, la solidaridad, un valor humano necesario, invaluable, que fomenta el bienestar y acaba con el egoísmo, no se ha perdido, sigue aquí y los buenos somos cada vez más._

>En lugar de preguntarnos si la solidaridad se ha perdido, yo más bien haría otra pregunta, que haríamos sin ella?. Como seres sociales que somos, no podemos ser totalmente independientes, o más bien, autosuficientes, porque todos necesitamos de todos, desde lo más sencillo que podamos pensar hasta en los momentos más difíciles o de vulnerabilidad. Cuando estamos en situaciones donde necesitamos una mano amiga, allí aparece la solidaridad, como un ángel para brindarnos ayuda. Este valor es gratis, no pide nada a cambio, lo precede la empatía, pero nunca trabajan por separado, siempre en equipo. La empatía no es igual que ser solidarios, entender al otro o ponerse en sus zapatos no es suficiente, hay que actuar para ser solidarios, y muy importante, debe ser mutua.
![1780107038809.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUwsf5N5ts4Jp6YwpWzTPvVkHzeYfLkWGNF8awcVu7cHt/1780107038809.jpg)

>La solidaridad siempre está presente en nuestras vidas, la practicamos con nuestros semejantes y ellos la practican con nosotros. Quien no ha solidario alguna vez con el prójimo y ha recibido solidaridad?, como una palabra de aliento para calmar el dolor emocional o aliviar la carga de esta. En mis tiempos universitarios, ya haciendo tesis, una de mis compañeras se sintió abrumada con el trabajo y estuvo a punto de abandonar, creo que a todos nos ha pasado, no es fácil hacer una tesis y sobre todo la presión que ello conlleva. La chica estaba realmente agobiada, así que entendiendo lo que estaba pasando porque en algunos momentos me sentí así, me ofrecí a ayudarla. Para ella fue un gran alivio y se sintió feliz al ver que sí se podía avanzar pese a las dificultades.

>En momentos de enfermedad, encontramos la solidaridad en muchas personas, a veces, en quien menos lo imaginamos. Cuando mi padre enfermó, aunque mi hermano y yo éramos los cuidadores principales, recibimos ayuda de familiares y amigos. Estuvieron pendientes de su salud todo el tiempo, nos donaron medicinas, recibió visita de amigos que lo aprecian para darle ánimo y hasta le llevaban sopas para ayudarlo en su alimentación. De aquellos días tan difíciles, muy a pesar del desenlace que ya sabíamos, conservo el buen recuerdo de una tarde que fueron a visitarlo sus nietos, mi hermano y su esposa, luego, llegó mi primo con su familia. Esa tarde nos reímos y pasamos un rato agradable porque ellos se encargaron de llevarle buenos deseos y algunas bromas que le sacaron a mi padre algunas sonrisas.
![1780107038792.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYXgaWPFph7rmk58gnkErcweCqxWV7SSjRp2CimfV8ofh/1780107038792.jpg)

>Yo también he recibido solidaridad de muchas maneras y me siento muy agradecida por ello. Hace un mes más o menos, se me dañó el teléfono, parece mentira, pero este dispositivo no es solo una herramienta de llamadas, es un instrumento de trabajo, es una agenda, es mi archivo personal para todo, incluyendo para publicar aquí en Hive. Me sentí muy angustiada de solo pensar que toda esa información que tenía guardada allí la podía perder y sobre todo tener el dinero para adquirir otro casi de emergencia, teniendo yo otras prioridades. Necesitaba solventar mientras reúno para comprar uno nuevo, me recomendaron un sitio, pero no recibí la ayuda que necesitaba. Sin embargo, una compañera de trabajo me recomendó un lugar donde trabaja el padre de su hijo. Ella le comentó el problema, yo no lo supe hasta después de haber recibido el teléfono arreglado. El chico no me cobró revisión (tenía que pagarla) y el servicio me lo dejó más económico.

>De verdad me sorprendí, pero, esa misma tarde, el teléfono se volvió a averiar, cuando ella me preguntó el sábado, le dije “solo duró un par de horas funcionando bien”. Tenía que volver a pagar porque ya él me había dicho que esos trabajos no tenían garantía. Me sentí triste y me resigné, “se echó a perder y no tiene arreglo” me dije. Pero luego, esta compañera de trabajo me dijo que el lunes le llevara nuevamente el teléfono al chico. Cuando se lo llevé, no me cobró y me lo entregó pasado un par de horas funcionando bien, gracias a Dios. Cuando hablé con ella, me comentó lo sucedido, ella le pidió que lo revisaría nuevamente y que no me cobrara. Sentí la solidaridad de corazón por parte de esta compañera que apenas tengo poco tiempo de tratarla. Así es la solidaridad, no tiene límites de tiempo para ponerse de manifiesto, llega sin avisar y de quien menos te imaginas.
Las fotos son originales tomadas con mi teléfono Xiaomi Redmi 9
# Gracias por leer
![1780107038835.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdN1zEgKL6g4N4du7MaZu6KvzVHVZBfKwTAvjByY6iu5j/1780107038835.jpg)
#

>Greetings, dear friends of Holos&Lotus. Today I’d like to weigh in on the topic proposed by @damarysvibra: [Who said solidarity is lost? | Who said solidarity is lost?](https://hive.blog/hive-131951/@damarysvibra/quien-dijo-que-la-solidaridad-se-ha-perdidoororwho-said-solidarity-is-lost). This topic is wonderful—solidarity, a necessary and invaluable human value that fosters well-being and puts an end to selfishness, has not been lost; it is still here, and there are more and more of us good people._

>Instead of asking ourselves if solidarity has been lost, I would rather ask another question: what would we do without it? As social beings, we cannot be completely independent—or rather, self-sufficient—because we all need one another, from the simplest of moments to the most difficult or vulnerable times. When we find ourselves in situations where we need a helping hand, solidarity appears, like an angel offering us aid. This value is free; it asks for nothing in return. It is preceded by empathy, but the two never work separately—they always work as a team. Empathy is not the same as showing solidarity; understanding others or putting yourself in their shoes is not enough. You must take action to show solidarity, and, very importantly, it must be mutual.
![1780107038809.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUwsf5N5ts4Jp6YwpWzTPvVkHzeYfLkWGNF8awcVu7cHt/1780107038809.jpg)

>Solidarity is always present in our lives; we show it to others, and they show it to us. Who hasn’t shown solidarity to a neighbor at some point—or received it in return—perhaps in the form of a word of encouragement to soothe emotional pain or lighten the burden of it? Back in my college days, while working on my thesis, one of my classmates felt overwhelmed by the work and was on the verge of giving up. I think we’ve all been there—it’s not easy to write a thesis, especially with all the pressure that comes with it. She was really stressed out, so, understanding what she was going through—because I’d felt that way at times—I offered to help her. It was a huge relief for her, and she was happy to see that progress was possible despite the difficulties.

>In times of illness, we find solidarity in many people—sometimes in those we least expect. When my father fell ill, although my brother and I were his primary caregivers, we received help from family and friends. They kept a close eye on his health the whole time, donated medicine, and friends who cared for him came to visit to cheer him up; they even brought him soup to help him eat. From those difficult days, despite the outcome we already knew, I have fond memories of one afternoon when his grandchildren, my brother, and his wife came to visit him, and later my cousin arrived with his family. That afternoon we laughed and had a pleasant time because they brought him good wishes and shared some jokes that brought a few smiles to my father’s face.
![1780107038792.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYXgaWPFph7rmk58gnkErcweCqxWV7SSjRp2CimfV8ofh/1780107038792.jpg)

>I, too, have received support in many ways, and I am very grateful for it. About a month ago, my phone broke. It’s hard to believe, but this device isn’t just a tool for making calls—it’s a work tool, a planner, and my personal archive for everything, including posting here on Hive. I felt really anxious just thinking that I might lose all the information I had stored there, and especially about having the money to buy a replacement almost immediately, given that I have other priorities. I needed a temporary solution while I saved up to buy a new one. Someone recommended a place to me, but I didn’t get the help I needed there. However, a coworker recommended a place where her son’s father works. She told him about the problem—I didn’t find out until after I’d received the repaired phone. The guy didn’t charge me for the inspection (I was supposed to pay for it), and the service ended up being cheaper for me.

>I was really surprised, but that same afternoon, the phone broke down again. When she asked me on Saturday, I told her, “It only worked properly for a couple of hours.” I had to pay again because he had already told me that those repairs didn’t come with a warranty. I felt sad and resigned myself to it, telling myself, “It’s broken and can’t be fixed.” But then, this coworker told me to take the phone back to the guy on Monday. When I took it to him, he didn’t charge me and gave it back to me a couple of hours later working fine, thank God. When I spoke with her, she told me what had happened; she had asked him to check it again and not to charge me. I felt genuine solidarity from this coworker whom I’ve only known for a short time. That’s what solidarity is like—it has no time limits for showing up; it arrives without warning and from the person you least expect.
The photos are originals taken with my Xiaomi Redmi 9 phone

body.title: Grilled hamburgers with rice (Eng/Esp)
body.body:
> Today's lunch was some delicious grilled ground beef burgers topped with onion, paprika, and bell peppers, along with some bread and carrots, both grated, for a very pleasant combination of flavors. I served it with white rice.
![1000444827.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23wC5G7MK34HLHQKbeFRVLVKVBtdQnU7sgezgcJC6BRTUNTxkuzZBGcC3w43qyKm5mrZb.jpg)
## Ingredients: - 400 grams ground beef - 8 sweet peppers - 2 onions - 1 carrot - 1 loaf of bread - Pinch of seasoning - Salt to taste - Oil
![1000444812.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23x1Q4staNuMKk98bBqeyxec1sJauU45nZJzy4QjmMtBBjA9PZFL6syJ3JwCwvBumcnwV.jpg)
## Preparation: I rinsed the peppers thoroughly with water and removed the seeds from both the sweet peppers and the bell peppers. Then I cut them into pieces and placed them in a skillet with a little oil, where I sautéed them. Once they had softened, I removed them from the heat and let them cool.
![1000444813.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23wgTtn367eCpBhv686tJnbHz6AUXHbXwWDZaHTSURSPpwgnNh5364Ka3tvojGcJ1dkH6.jpg)
![1000444818.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23xAkfLRyikqaUXnUgv1KrMQQKfjqMJCmUPky6uj4sZjL6Wr1PeAXRzPzKr21Z8yiKC7n.jpg)
Meanwhile, I peeled the onions and the carrot. Then I grated them, and took the opportunity to do the same with the bread. Next, I took the ground beef, kneaded it, and added the sautéed seasonings. I mixed everything well and immediately added the bread, onion, and carrot that I had grated earlier. I continued kneading, then added a pinch of salt and a dash of adobo seasoning.
![1000444821.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23xerRXTD6ak82ztfb6Agk4MnGyGWpWzadJ1AEJC3tCD86yPXLAj1GHrF8ycH7p4vu4pH.jpg)
![1000444822.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/243fxmvtwepzvpHcNJWrboMwzHYc8fP3rKqmnGbkJKvQ1rj1ygUrYsswgqcGcUjcFcTVo.jpg)
Once everything was ready, I set up a griddle and oiled the surface, then cooked five thick, juicy patties of ground beef on it. I kept them over low heat so they would stay juicy.
![1000444823.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23u6DddNgfiyhfcy7YuiRXijuBtnj4r8x5Fhe45rutcxQcK9pBo4Ev66PukM8MosLYrsu.jpg)
At the same time, I filled a pot with three cups of water and a pinch of salt. When it came to a boil, I added the cup of rice and lowered the heat. It was ready in just a few minutes. The next step was to plate the dish: I placed the rice on the bottom and the meat on top—a spectacular combination. *** ***
## Versión en Español

> El almuerzo de hoy fueron unas deliciosas hamburguesas de carne molida a la plancha aderezadas con cebolla, pimentón y ají dulce, también un poco de pan y zanahoria, ambos rallados para una combinación de sabores muy agradable. Acompañé con arroz blanco.
![1000444827.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23wC5G7MK34HLHQKbeFRVLVKVBtdQnU7sgezgcJC6BRTUNTxkuzZBGcC3w43qyKm5mrZb.jpg)
## Ingredientes: - 400 gramos de carne molida - 8 ajíes dulces - 2 cebollas - 1 zanahoria - 1 pan - Pizca de adobo - Sal al gusto - Aceite
![1000444812.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23x1Q4staNuMKk98bBqeyxec1sJauU45nZJzy4QjmMtBBjA9PZFL6syJ3JwCwvBumcnwV.jpg)
## Preparación: Lavé los aliños con suficiente agua, quité las semillas tanto de los ajíes dulces como del pimentón. Luego dividí en pedazos y los llevé a un sartén con un poco de aceite, allí los sofreí. Cuando se ablandaron, retiré del fuego y esperé que se enfriaran.
![1000444813.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23wgTtn367eCpBhv686tJnbHz6AUXHbXwWDZaHTSURSPpwgnNh5364Ka3tvojGcJ1dkH6.jpg)
![1000444818.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23xAkfLRyikqaUXnUgv1KrMQQKfjqMJCmUPky6uj4sZjL6Wr1PeAXRzPzKr21Z8yiKC7n.jpg)
Mientras tanto, retiré las cortezas de las cebollas y de la zanahoria. Luego procedí a rallar, aproveché la ocasión para hacer lo mismo con el pan. Después tomé la carne molida, la amasé y agregué los aliños sofritos, mezclé muy bien y de inmediato adicioné el pan, la cebolla y la zanahoria que rallé previamente. Continúe amasando, luego agregué un toque de sal y una pizca de adobo.
![1000444821.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23xerRXTD6ak82ztfb6Agk4MnGyGWpWzadJ1AEJC3tCD86yPXLAj1GHrF8ycH7p4vu4pH.jpg)
![1000444822.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/243fxmvtwepzvpHcNJWrboMwzHYc8fP3rKqmnGbkJKvQ1rj1ygUrYsswgqcGcUjcFcTVo.jpg)
Cuando la preparación estuvo lista, monté un budare y aceité la superficie, allí puse a cocinar cinco ruedas de carne molida gruesas y suculentas. Las mantuve a fuego bajo para que quedaran jugosas.
![1000444823.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23u6DddNgfiyhfcy7YuiRXijuBtnj4r8x5Fhe45rutcxQcK9pBo4Ev66PukM8MosLYrsu.jpg)
De forma paralela, monté la olla con tres tazas de agua y un toque de sal, cuando hirvió incorporé la taza de arroz y bajé el fuego. En pocos minutos estaba listo. El siguiente paso fue preparar el plato, abajo puse el arroz y arriba la carne, una combinación espectacular.   *** *** ✓Photos from my personal gallery, edited with Fotocollage. ✓Text translated with DeepL.

# INTERNAL MEMO — EYES ONLY
## Re: The Long Bond Is Trying to Tell You Something. Are You Listening?

*To: Anyone still long duration*
*From: The Yield Curve*
*Date: May 30, 2026*
*Priority: You should have read this six months ago*

---

Let me be direct with you.

I am a 30-year Treasury bond. My yield is sitting at roughly 5.1%. The last time I was here, Bear Stearns existed. The iPhone had just been announced. \

was a term that appeared only in academic journals and the fever dreams of heterodox economists. You did not think I could come back. You were wrong, and I am sending this memo because the equity market across the hallway is throwing a party and nobody has told them what building they're in.

Here is the situation as I understand it.

The United States government currently carries debt north of $39 trillion. The deficit is projected at 5.8% of GDP this year. Moody's stripped the Aaa rating in May 2025, completing the hat trick — all three major agencies have now downgraded American sovereign debt at some point in the past fifteen years. The response from Washington was roughly what you'd expect: a debt ceiling raised to $41.1 trillion in something called the \

signed on July 4, 2025, a date that was presumably chosen for the irony. The response from markets was a few days of politely nervous trading followed by nine weeks of record highs.

The debt compounds. The interest payments compound faster. Moody's estimates the deficit widens toward 9% of GDP by 2035 as entitlement spending rises and revenue stays flat. The self-reinforcing arithmetic is not complicated: bigger debt means higher interest expense, which means bigger deficits, which means more borrowing, which means upward pressure on yields, which means heavier interest burden on the next tranche of debt. This is not a forecast. It is a description of the current trajectory, already in motion.

And yet. The S&P 500 closed at record highs Friday. Again.

---

**On the matter of Bitcoin ($BTC), which is having a difficult spring:**

Bitcoin's advocates have spent years constructing an elegant argument. The fiscal trajectory is unsustainable. Debasement is structural. Hard-money assets will win eventually because fiat systems carrying this load cannot hold. The long arc of the argument is not obviously wrong.

The problem is the short arc. When I — the 30-year Treasury — yield 5.1%, the opportunity cost of sitting in a non-yielding asset becomes very concrete, very fast. Bitcoin ETFs bled roughly $700 million in weekly outflows when yields last spiked hard in mid-May. Spot volumes on Binance collapsed from around $50 million in net flow to $6.5 million. Coinbase went from $30 million to $5.7 million. The institutional bid, which everyone celebrated as Bitcoin's maturation into legitimate asset class status, turned out to have a rate sensitivity that looks almost identical to a leveraged tech growth stock.

CME FedWatch was pricing over 44% odds of a Fed *hike* by December, as of mid-May. The same market that entered 2026 expecting two cuts before year-end. Warsh wants to ease. The bond market is pricing the opposite, and the bond market has a better historical win rate in this particular argument.

The long-thesis Bitcoin crowd is not wrong about the destination. They may simply be wrong about the sequence. The fiscal doom loop that makes BTC's monetary thesis compelling is also the fiscal doom loop that sends yields to 5%, which is the exact environment that punishes the speculative capital needed to actually push BTC higher near-term. The irony is load-bearing.

There is one small signal worth watching: tokenized Treasuries on-chain hit a record $15 billion in total value locked as of mid-May, up roughly 70% year-to-date. Capital is not leaving crypto entirely. It is parking itself in the chain-native equivalent of what I am offering — dollar-denominated yield, DeFi composability, liquidity optionality. That is a pragmatic adaptation. Whether it is a prelude to a return to speculative excess or a permanent reclassification of what crypto capital does, nobody knows yet.

---

**A brief interlude on rice:**

Asia rice prices surged 20% in May, driven by the Iran war's disruption to shipping lanes and adverse weather across producing regions. Emerging market food inflation is not a footnote. It is a leading indicator of social stress, central bank policy divergence, and capital outflows that eventually loop back into dollar strength, which loops back into yield dynamics, which loops back into everything discussed above. The Bloomberg homepage carried it as a sidebar Friday. It should have been a headline.

---

**Back to the memo:**

The equity market's position is internally consistent, if you accept its premises. The premises are: AI capex continues uninterrupted. Corporate margins — at a record 13.4% for the S&P 500 in Q1 2026, with IT at a genuinely extraordinary 29.1% — hold or expand. The Iran situation resolves within the ceasefire window. Real consumer income, which has now fallen for three consecutive months in inflation-adjusted terms, does not matter because the consumer who matters most to the AI infrastructure trade is a sovereign wealth fund, not a grocery shopper.

Those premises are not insane. Some of them might even be right.

But sovereign credit is deteriorating. The long bond is at a 19-year high. The Fed's preferred inflation gauge just printed 3.8% — its worst reading since May 2023 — and the Cleveland Fed's nowcast suggests May will be worse. Real disposable income is falling. And the market is on its ninth consecutive week of gains.

At some point these two things — the structural deterioration of the fiscal and inflation picture, and the continued levitation of equity multiples — have to have a conversation. That conversation has not happened yet. When it does, it will probably happen very fast and feel completely obvious in retrospect.

In the meantime, I yield 5.1%. I have been trying to get your attention for months.

---

*— The 30-Year Treasury Bond*

---

*All figures sourced from government data releases, market close data, and institutional research, May 15–30, 2026. Not investment advice.*

body.body: Welding work, house chores, evening exercise, some repair work Dear friends, Yesterday was full with sorts of activities. The first was my welding work. I continued to built a stool out of metal scraps; otherwise, they would pile up for good for nothing.

/> Then, I transplanted one tray of beetroots to the ground. There were two more trays to transplant. I found those I transplanted the day before survived. I was just seeing the feedback results whether the plants were alright because that was my first time of growing beetroots.

/> In the afternoon, I went downtown and met a friend at a teashop for chitchat and sharing experiences. In the evening, I went to the football stadium for walking and jogging exercises. There was some rain and I had to wait until it ceased. I walked first before I started jogging and I completed five rounds that was over 2 km distance.

/> At night, when I got back home I replaced two lithium batteries from the battery pack. Because of those two broken batteries, the pack refused to be charged and after I replaced them, I could charge it.

/> Before going to bed I counted beads and recited a Buddha sutra. Those were some of the activities for yesterday. 30th May 2026 @princekham
